articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: ‘Abki baar, AQI 400-paar’: Congress takes a swipe at Modi over Delhi pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Jairam Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult

The Congress on Saturday (November 14, 2026) took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 2024 Lok Sabha election slogan, “Abki baar, 400-paar”, saying it had come true in the national capital, with Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) crossing the 400-mark.
In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!”

Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said.
“Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said.
Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Avian influenza confirmed in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore; over 1,500 chickens culled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1) has been confirmed in chicken samples collected from a poultry farm at Kattiyankuppam village in Kurinjipadi taluk of Cuddalore district.

“The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, had confirmed the H5N1 avian influenza virus in samples collected from a poultry carcass on November 5, 2026,” District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar told The Hindu .

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre.

According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.”
He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.”

As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai.
On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said.
Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease.

“Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.
The carcasses are being disposed of through deep burial in designated pits, with bleaching powder applied and biosecurity measures in place.
An official said that movement of birds to and from the affected farms has been strictly restricted.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 14 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Caste and class: On OBC reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu engages realty developers to fast track Global Capability Centre corridors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To advance the implementation of the Tamil Nadu GCC Corridor and Development Programme, the Department of Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, Government of Tamil Nadu, convened a roundtable discussion at Guidance Tamil Nadu on Friday with leading real estate developers from Tamil Nadu and across the country, in the presence of Industries Minister S. Keerthana.

According to details shared by Guidance, the discussion focused on accelerating the development of Grade-A office space and supporting infrastructure across the identified corridors to meet the needs of the state’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem. The roundtable brought together developers’ perspectives on strengthening these corridors as integrated destinations for GCC investment and growth.

Tamil Nadu is home to more than 460 GCCs, including over 405 in Chennai, with the sector adding more than 55,000 jobs in 2025. Continued expansion by existing centres, alongside interest from new investors, has increased the need for readily available, high-quality office space.

Participants discussed measures to accelerate project development, maintain competitive rentals and ensure that suitable space is available within the timelines required by global companies. Developers shared their perspectives on land availability, development costs, floor space index (FSI), approval processes and infrastructure requirements.

The discussion emphasised the importance of developing complete GCC ecosystems in Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road (PTR) and Mount–Poonamallee High Road (MPR) through mixed-use projects that integrate offices with housing, schools, healthcare, hospitality and retail. Public transport, last-mile connectivity and pedestrian access were identified as essential to supporting the growth of these corridors. Participants noted and appreciated the greater transparency and accountability they had experienced in their interactions with government departments, with fewer discretionary hurdles contributing to a more conducive environment for investment.
The roundtable also provided an opportunity to encourage greater use of the State’s Single Window Portal and explore investments beyond Chennai, including in emerging locations such as Hosur.

articles.title: BIM, Texas university to offer course on AI in Business from next year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), in collaboration with the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) in the U.S., on Friday announced the launch of the Master of Science programme in Artificial Intelligence for Business (MSAIB), which is aimed at working professionals in India.

On Friday, representatives of the two institutions exchanged Memoranda of Understanding for the course. The first batch of the course will start in August 2027. The first cohort will include 25 students, mostly working professionals, who are keen to upgrade their skills to secure better job opportunities in multinational companies, and the tuition fee is indicated to be around $27,000.

Asit K. Barma, Director, BIM, told presspersons in Chennai that the classes would be held at the IIT-Madras Research Park. The location, being a technology hub, will be beneficial to students in terms of access to industry interactions.

The conventional MBA course had, over the past few years, been losing its shine gradually, indicated by the falling enrolment for the Common Admission Test (CAT). Last year, there was a 2% drop in students taking the Common Admission Test compared to the previous year, Dr. Barma said. The two-year MSAIB course will provide an opening for young professionals to pursue an industry-oriented course, he said.
Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean, College of Business, UTA, said the course would be offered in hybrid mode, with faculty members from the UTA visiting the Chennai campus for conducting classes.
The curriculum for the course would be the same as the one offered at its Arlington campus.

Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor, Information Systems and Operations Management, UTA, said the faculty for each course would spend about a week on the Chennai campus, while the rest of the classes would be conducted online. For the intake of students, candidates’ holistic performance, including undergraduate GPA score, rigour of courses taken, exposure to mathematics, and even job experience, will be considered, UTA representatives said.

Ravi Appaswamy, chairman, Board of Governors, BIM, said the MSAIB course would provide an avenue for young professionals to learn the use of a tool that had become so indispensable to every profession and industry.
R. Siddharthan, managing director, Accenture India, and Mafruza Sultana, assistant professor and faculty chair-international relations, BIM, were among those present.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha panel visits ISRO, HAL facilities in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Members of the Subordinate Legislation Committee of Rajya Sabha on Friday visited key defence, space and finance institutions in Bengaluru as part of a study visit.
The committee, led by Chairman Milind Deora, visited the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), toured the LCA Tejas Division and witnessed a static display of the defence PSU’s various platforms.
The HAL said the committee reviewed the implementation of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014.

“HAL Chairman Ravi K., and Director (HR), M.G. Balasubrahmanya, and other senior officials were present during the interaction, which provided an opportunity to showcase the HAL’s contributions to indigenous aerospace development and its commitment to impactful and sustainable CSR initiatives,” the HAL said.

The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies.

“The committee got a closer look at India’s satellite capabilities and discussed the future of our space sector from liberalisation and reusable rockets to Chandrayaan missions, space debris and e-waste regulations. While India’s space ambitions are reaching new heights, our sustainability game must keep up. Innovation and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” Mr. Deora posted on X.
The committee also held meetings with officials of the Reserve Bank of India and leading Public Sector Unit (PSU) banks to discuss the future of digital payment security.

articles.title: Over 7,000 books removed from District Central Libraries in Vellore, nearby districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications

As many as 7,995 books published by the controversial Agalvilakku and Phoenix Publications were removed from the racks of District Central Library in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday.

The action comes against the backdrop of allegations of fake and AI-generated books being procured from these publishers for public libraries including Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore. “The identified books of the two publications were removed from the other books. The books, which are meant for distribution to branch libraries in the district for 2025-26, are stored in a separate room,” S. Valli, District Library Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu.

Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications, followed by Tiruvannamalai (2,209 books), and Vellore (984 books). “Books on competitive examinations are a big attraction in District Central library as the facility has a large collection of books related to general knowledge,” said G. Satish, a reader.

Officials said District Central Library in these districts have books on subjects including history, politics, law, economics, philosophy, agriculture, computer and mathematics. Reference books, especially for examinations conducted by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), UPSC, and other competitive exams are available.

As per norms, around 60,000 to 70,000 books are procured for each district library annually based on feedback provided by local librarians and readers. These books then distributed branch libraries in the district. As per estimates, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai have at least 120 branch libraries each whereas Ranipet and Tirupattur have around 50 branch libraries each.

articles.title: Turkiye, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, Turkish presidency says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow, a statement from the Turkish presidency quoted President Erdogan as saying

Turkiye and ​Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday (November 13, 2026), ‌the office of President Tayyip Erdogan said, ​as the Turkish leader ⁠met the Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani in Istanbul.

“President Erdogan stated that we ‌would continue working together to prevent the resurgence of war in ‌the Gulf region and establish a ‌basis ⁠for dialogue and achieve peace,” ⁠the presidency said in a statement on X, which did not provide details on the defence accord.
The ​statement cited ‌him as saying that Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow.
“President Erdogan stated that the Mutual Defence Agreement signed today ⁠by Turkey and Qatar would add another dimension to our brotherhood,” it added.
In August, ‌Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, bringing together the Sunni Muslim U.S. allies at a time of conflict across the region.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the ‌so-called Mecca Joint Defence Agreement last week, clearing ​the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which ⁠has been struggling to fend off attacks ⁠by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi militants.
Under the agreement, signed by the three ‌regional powers in August, an attack on one party constitutes an attack ​on all.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Disruption to Microsoft’s cloud-based email service affects business operations and airline customer support in India; public services in several countries also report problems

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Around 8 p.m. IST on Friday (November 13, 2026), Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform at Microsoft, said, "We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure. We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward."

The company said it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the disruption and promised that it would publish a detailed report on the root cause and corrective measures after services were restored.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.

At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.

The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Around 8 p.m. IST on Friday (November 13, 2026), Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform at Microsoft, said, "We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure. We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward."

The company said it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the disruption and promised that it would publish a detailed report on the root cause and corrective measures after services were restored.

articles.title: The challenge of holding the Quad together
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The big ticket question confronting the Quad, however, is how Donald Trump engages with the group and the broader Indo-Pacific geography

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the U.S. Secretary of State announced that the leaders of the four Quad countries — India, Australia, Japan and the U.S. — are expected to meet in Manila in November, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. The announcement is significant, as this would be the first summit-level meeting of the Quad leaders since Donald Trump began his second term as U.S. President. It would also be the first such summit attended by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi since she assumed office. The last Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

While India was expected to host the subsequent Quad Leaders’ Summit, the grouping underwent a period of intense strategic turbulence in 2025, on account of Washington’s shifting geopolitical priorities and changing political dynamics in its bilateral relations with Quad members, especially India. However, this did not result in complete collapse of the grouping. Apart from the leader-level summit, the group has remained successful in continuing its operational synergies in its various initiatives. This was most evident in the elevation of the Quad’s Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness initiative to the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration framework, launched in New Delhi in May 2026, following the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

articles.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: NPPA directs State drug controllers to strictly monitor prices
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs

The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%.

Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said.

All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites.

The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients.
Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted.

Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A.P. government will implement Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024, says Chief Minister Naidu

The Andhra Pradesh government would implement the Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024 and initiate the provision of clearances to industries in real time based on self-certification to encourage investors, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has said, adding that the proposed law would be passed in the coming session of the Legislative Assembly.

Addressing the media after the valedictory of the 31st CII Partnership Summit here on Friday, Mr. Naidu said there was a pressing need for good governance and that investors needed to be reassured about the safety of their investments in the event of a regime change. This was “keeping in view the ruin caused between 2019 and 2024”, which aggravated the impact of State bifurcation.

The government would be liberal in facilitating businesses, but not be lenient in ensuring accountability for the support being availed, Mr. Naidu said, noting that while mobilising investments with due sense of urgency, it was ensuring that they would take tangible shape as per the committed timelines.

Besides, the compliance burden was being reduced to make doing business far more easier. Due focus was being laid on making the agriculture sector resilient, as the government could not afford to lay the whole emphasis on the industrial sector only. Both sectors are crucial to increase the Gross State Domestic Product, he said.

The Chief Minister said that the State attracted investments of nearly ₹9.88 lakh crore through 303 MoUs during the current edition of the CII Partnership Summit and that they have the potential to generate approximately 3.49 lakh jobs across sectors. The cumulative investments that have been tied up since June 2024 have reached ₹32.49 lakh crore.
“Andhra Pradesh is hogging the limelight, with its distinct advantages for investors and the potential of the three economic regions of Amaravati, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam,” he said.

The government was extending all possible support for businesses in emerging sectors to thrive, and a priority has been accorded to development of the space sector around India’s only spaceport at Sriharikota, he said.

Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu; MPs T. Krishna Prasad and M. Sribharat; Ministers T.G. Bharat, K. Atchannaidu, P. Narayana, Kollu Ravindra, Kondapalli Srinivas, Kolusu Parthasarathy and Satya Kumar Yadav were present.

articles.title: Manipur probe panel gets sixth extension; no sign of report yet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The report is awaited even as the ethnic conflict has now spread to Kuki and Naga communities
The three-member Commission of Inquiry, set up by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to probe the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence, was given a sixth extension on Friday.
The Ministry notified that the commission, which was constituted on June 4, 2023, “shall submit its report to the Central government as soon as possible but not later than May 20, 2027”.
More than 300 people have been killed in the ethnic violence that erupted between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people on May 3, 2023. Around 60,000 people have been displaced from their homes.
The probe panel’s report is awaited even as the ethnic conflict has now spread to the Kuki and Naga communities. Since February this year, more than 60 people have been killed in Naga-Kuki clashes.

The commission is now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, after Ajai Lamba, the former Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court, resigned as the chairperson of the panel in February this year. The panel is yet to finalise its report.

Justice (retd.) Chauhan is also heading the judicial inquiry into an incident of violence that occurred in Ladakh’s Leh city on September 24, 2025 where four civilians, including a Kargil war veteran, were killed in police firing. The Ladakh report is yet to be submitted to the government.
Manipur’s Commission of Inquiry has received around 11,000 affidavits.
President’s rule was imposed in the State on February 13, 2025 and on February 4 this year, a new Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh took oath, ending Central rule.

The inquiry commission is mandated to probe the causes, extent of violence and riots targeting members of different communities, the sequence of events, and whether there were any lapses or dereliction of duty on the part of any of the responsible authorities and individuals.

articles.title: Four-day Chhath festival begins in Bihar with Nahay Khay
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Out of 103 ghats in Patna, 90 have been declared safe for devotees, while 13 have been termed unsafe

Bihar’s famous Chhath festival began on Friday (November 13, 2026) with Nahay Khay on the first of four days of festivities. A large number of devotees gathered at ghats by rivers, including the Ganga, to collect water and bathe.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A rescue operation was underway, local media reported citing port authorities; images showed the cruise boat, the American Heritage operated by American Cruise Lines, listing and partially underwater

A tanker ship collided with an American Cruise Lines passenger ship ​that was docked in New Orleans on the ‌Mississippi River on Friday (November 13, 2026), and local ​TV showed passengers with life ⁠vests in the water.
The U.S. Coast Guard said in an emailed statement that it had responded ‌to the collision and that all river traffic was closed in ‌the vicinity. It provided no ‌other ⁠details.
Local TV also showed videos of ⁠the cruise ship listing on its side, while CBS News reported that at least 14 people ​had been rescued from ‌the water.
The cruise ship has a capacity for 150 people and was built in 2015, American Cruise Lines said ‌on its website.

The Advocate newspaper, citing ​unnamed Port of New Orleans officials, reported that 129 passengers were ⁠aboard the American Heritage cruise ship when it was hit by the Atlantic Asphalt, ‌a tanker, at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time (1830 GMT). There was no immediate word on any deaths or injuries.
The Port of New Orleans did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
American Cruise Lines ‌said in an emailed statement that it could ​confirm that its riverboat was involved in a collision.

“We are in ⁠close coordination with the US Coast Guard ⁠and local authorities. Guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned ‌for everyone involved. We will share more information as it becomes available,” the ​company said.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: No ETA yet on full recovery, company says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.
The company said its teams are reviewing the incident and working to prevent similar disruptions in the future.

Microsoft says service availability is improving, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels. However, some users may continue to face intermittent access issues and delayed email delivery as the company restores affected infrastructure and monitors recovery.
Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America and across much of Europe.

articles.title: CRPF removes jawan from service for posting death threat to Commander on social media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The battalion’s Commanding Officer conducted an inquiry, following which the jawan was terminated from service on Friday (November 13, 2026)

The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has terminated a jawan from service for allegedly posting messages on social media threatening to kill his Commander, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Officials told PTI that the accused was identified as probationary Constable Pinak Nath from Assam who belonged to the Alpha Company of the CRPF's 33rd battalion based in Doda, Jammu and Kashmir. He had joined the force recently, they said.

The jawan allegedly posted on a social media platform that he would kill his Company Commander and then himself, citing a recent incident in another force in which a jawan killed his senior and other colleagues using a service weapon, officials said.

The battalion's Commanding Officer conducted an inquiry, following which Mr. Nath was terminated from service on Friday (November 13, 2026) under the provisions of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1965, they said.

articles.title: Assam accident: Autopsy of 26 bodies on November 14; CM to visit injured, meet families of deceased
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Twenty-six people died in a head-on collision between the two vehicles at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on November 13

The postmortem of the bodies of 26 people who died in a collision between a minibus and a container truck in Assam 's Kaziranga will be conducted on Saturday (November 14, 2026), Minister Ranoj Pegu said.

The condition of seven of the 18 injured people remained critical, said Mr. Pegu, who was deputed by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to visit the accident site and the hospitals where the injured are receiving treatment.
Mr. Sarma is scheduled to visit the families of the deceased and the injured under treatment in hospitals in Golaghat district on Saturday and take stock of the situation.

Twenty-six people died in a head-on collision between the two vehicles at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on Friday (Novembe 13, 2026). Many of the victims were college students who were returning from their classes.
"The postmortem will be conducted at Swahid Kushal Konwar Civil Hospital in Golaghat, after which ambulances will take the bodies to their residence," Mr. Pegu told reporters.
Mr. Pegu said 20 people had been admitted to hospitals in Jorhat and Golaghat and two of them had succumbed.
"Seven of the 18 injured are in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) in Jorhat Medical College Hospital, and their condition remains critical," he said.
The 11 others admitted at the two hospitals are stable, the Minister said, adding that the state government will bear all costs for the injured's treatment.
Mr. Pegu said that the state government will make necessary arrangements if any of the injured need to be shifted to specialised hospitals for advanced treatment.
Doctors from Gauhati Medical College Hospital and Assam Medical College Hospital, Dibrugarh have reached Jorhat and Golghat to assist in treating the injured and conducting the postmortem.
He said investigations are underway to ascertain the cause of the accident and strict action will be taken against those who had flouted speeding norms, if found guilty.

The Golaghat district authorities on Friday (November 13, 2026) said a thorough inquiry would be conducted to determine how the accident occurred and whether either or both of the vehicles violated traffic norms, such as carrying more passengers than their seating capacity allowed and exceeding the speed limit near Kaziranga National Park.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi promises social security, insurance cover for gig workers in Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi announced a series of social security measures for gig workers in Telangana, including accident insurance of ₹5 lakh, health insurance of ₹10 lakh, dedicated Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones and a mechanism to ensure that 1% of every transaction is credited towards their social security.

Addressing gig workers, Mr. Gandhi said the Congress government in Telangana was fulfilling its promise to protect workers engaged in the platform-based economy and ensure that they received their fair share of the benefits generated by their labour.

Describing the 21st century as the age of data, Mr. Gandhi pointed out that while companies such as Google, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Uber operated on data, gig workers had so far been denied access to information about their own work.

Under the proposed legislation, workers would be able to access complete details of their transactions, deliveries, working hours, and payments through their mobile phones. “The data belongs to you, the labour is yours, but you were not even allowed to see your own data,” he said.

He said the government would also establish dedicated, Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones in Hyderabad and other cities to enable delivery personnel and other gig workers to park their vehicles, rest and relax during working hours.

Announcing insurance benefits, Mr Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security.
The amount would be collected from companies and routed through the Gig Workers’ Board before being transferred directly to the workers’ bank accounts, he said.

Drawing a political distinction between the Congress and the BJP-RSS, Mr. Gandhi alleged that the latter wanted to turn gig workers into bonded labourers while allowing large corporate houses and platform companies to reap the benefits. In contrast, the Congress believed that workers were the foundation of the country’s economy and should be treated as partners.
“Do not be afraid. The Telangana Government, Rahul Gandhi, Revanth Reddy, and the Congress team stand with you. We want to make you partners and ensure protection for you and your families,” he said.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said the Congress government had fulfilled the promise made by Rahul Gandhi to gig workers in Telangana by bringing in legislation to protect their rights and provide them with social security.

Speaking at an event in the presence of Mr. Rahul Gandhi, the Chief Minister recalled that during the Bharat Jodo Yatra from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2023, which covered nearly 4,000 km, Mr. Gandhi had understood the difficulties faced by people from different sections of society.
“The Gandhi family stands by its word. A promise made by Rahul Gandhi is as good as a commitment written in golden letters. For us, his word is an instruction,” the Chief Minister said.

articles.title: India supports UNGA resolution on permanent sovereignty of Palestinian people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan

India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly draft resolution that reaffirms the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources and demands that Israel cease the exploitation and damage of these resources.

The 193-Member UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in favour of the resolution ‘Permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and of the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources’ proposed by Uruguay.
India voted in favour of the resolution along with 150 other UN Member States, while Israel and the U.S. were among the seven nations that voted against the draft, which got 11 abstentions.
The resolution reaffirmed the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and of the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources, including land, water and energy resources.

It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan.

It stressed that the wall and settlements being constructed by Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including in and around East Jerusalem, are contrary to international law and seriously deprive the Palestinian people of their natural resources.
It also called for full compliance with the legal obligations affirmed in the July 2004 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice and relevant UN resolutions.

The resolution called upon Israel to comply strictly with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and immediately and completely cease all policies and measures aimed at altering the character and status of the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.

It further called upon Israel to halt all actions, including those perpetrated by Israeli settlers, that harm the environment, including the dumping of waste materials in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and the occupied Syrian Golan.

It also called upon Israel to cease its destruction of vital infrastructure, including water pipelines, sewage networks and electricity networks, and to cease its demolition and confiscation of Palestinian homes and civilian infrastructure, agricultural lands and water wells.
It also stressed the urgent need to advance reconstruction and development projects in this regard, including in the Gaza Strip, and called for support for the necessary efforts in this regard.

articles.title: Low pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into cyclonic storm around Nov. 16
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dry weather is likely to prevail over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema till November 16, with light to moderate rain likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 17

A low pressure area formed over the Southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday morning and is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal around the evening of November 16 (Monday), according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the system is very likely to move northwestwards, and become a well-marked low pressure area on Saturday and intensify into a depression around Sunday morning, before moving north-northwestwards.

Dry weather is likely to prevail over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema till November 16, with light to moderate rain likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 17.
Squally weather with wind speeds of 45-55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, is likely along and off the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 17. Fishermen at sea have been advised to return by Sunday.

Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain said that, as per current forecasts, the system is likely to move towards north Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts. However, there is no clarity yet on its exact track, intensity or place of landfall, he said.

Mr. Jain cautioned fishermen against venturing into the sea, which is likely to be rough from Sunday, and appealed to the public to rely only on official information and not on rumours circulating on social media.

Meanwhile, Kurnool recorded the highest maximum temperature among the IMD stations in the State on Friday at 34°C, followed by Nandyal (33.8°C) and Tuni (33.4°C). Visakhapatnam recorded 32°C, which is 1.6°C above normal, and Amaravati 32.1°C. Tirupati airport received 2 mm of rainfall and Kavali 0.6 mm.

articles.title: ABVP condemns sexual assault on Haldwani minor girl by its student leader and three others
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a statement, the RSS-affiliated student organisation said it viewed the incident with "utmost seriousness" and would make every possible effort to ensure justice for the victim
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) has condemned the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl in Haldwani, Uttarakhand , and demanded strict legal action against those responsible.
In a statement, the RSS-affiliated student organisation said it viewed the incident with "utmost seriousness" and would make every possible effort to ensure justice for the victim.

A 16-year-old girl was allegedly raped at a hotel in the Mukhani area on Thursday night (November 13, 2026), following which police arrested four men, including an ABVP leader. Police said that all four suspects were reportedly members of the city's well-known ITI Gang.
The ABVP leader has been identified as Dheeraj Bisht, while three others are Nitin Pal, Ansh Khatri, and Himanshu Goni, according to police.

"A serious incident of sexual assault against a minor girl in Haldwani has come to light through media and social media reports. ABVP strongly condemns this heinous incident and demands the strictest legal action against those responsible to ensure speedy justice for the victim," the statement read.

ABVP Uttarakhand State Secretary Yashwant Panwar said, "ABVP will extend all possible assistance to the victim to ensure justice in this serious matter. ABVP demands that the administration take the strictest possible action against those responsible so that the victim receives speedy justice."
The student organisation said it remained committed to ensuring the safety, dignity and honour of female students and called for speedy justice for the victim.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The student organisation said it remained committed to ensuring the safety, dignity and honour of female students and called for speedy justice for the victim.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Tech giant restores services across all affected systems after global outage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: After nearly 200,000 user reports of issues, massive global outage comes to an end as Microsoft announces a full restoration of services
Microsoft reports consumer services fully recovered, ongoing recovery for Microsoft 365 enterprise services, and monitoring for potential further issues.
Microsoft said efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident have been completed. It added that services to remaining impacted customers and regions have also been restored.
Microsoft’s service health page showed all products became operational on Saturday.
The page read “All products are operational” on Saturday morning, including Microsoft 365 (business or enterprise) and consumer products.
Microsoft said it was “monitoring the backlog of email messages ‌accrued during this event” before considering the issue with ⁠the enterprise services resolved.

“Due to ‌the severity of impact this incident caused, we’re monitoring for an extended period to ‌ensure no additional mitigative actions are required,” Microsoft said in ⁠an update on its ⁠service status page.

Microsoft ⁠said ⁠on Friday its consumer products ‌services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC ‌on Friday (1610 GMT), ‌while it was seeing some ⁠sustained recovery ‌for its Microsoft 365 enterprise services.
The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which continued late into Friday, affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.
Microsoft outage disrupts global services, hitting Indian businesses, airlines, public sectors, with recovery underway and security advisories issued.

Microsoft said on Saturday that services across Teams, Outlook, Copilot and other applications had fully recovered, bringing an end to a massive global outage that disrupted online communication for businesses and government agencies for more than 24 hours.

During the disruption, Downdetector recorded a peak of nearly 200,000 user reports of issues across Microsoft services shortly after 1 pm New York time. While fresh reports of problems involving Outlook and Copilot subsequently declined, this did not initially indicate that services had been fully restored.
Microsoft says services are seeing widespread recovery after a major outage caused by a network capacity upgrade issue.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.
The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

He will also interact with leading business representatives and hold meetings with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association and participate in the Egypt-India Startups Forum.

Both countries have significant opportunities to expand cooperation in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles, chemicals, engineering goods, food processing, renewable energy, logistics and emerging technologies, it added.

articles.title: No locus standi: Indian envoy hits back at USCIRF for remarks on Sharjeel Imam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X, describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”

Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra has asked an American advisory body to introspect on its own prejudices and stop lecturing others, after the bipartisan agency flagged arrests in India allegedly on religious grounds.

Mr. Kwatra’s sharp retort on Friday (November 13, 2026) came after the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X , describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”.

Former Jawaharlal Nehru University scholar Imam has been booked under UAPA (Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act) on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.
The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.
“USCIRF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens,” Kwatra said
“Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths,” he said.

He said India flourishes, defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. “Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others,” Mr. Kwatra said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

articles.title: Trump administration blames ‘overloaded’ systems for ground stop after FAA lets flights resume
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.
Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to take off from airports in the U.S. after 4 p.m. EST.
At the time of the ground stoppage, 3,500 airplanes were in the sky, Mr. Duffy said.
“And last time I looked, we had less than 400 in the airspace,” he said. He said it's going to be slow getting air traffic back to normal.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Trump administration rules out foul play, Transportation Secretary says major communications outage caused by decades old technology

Tens of thousands of fliers were forced to change their plans when the FAA issued a ground stop ‌that lasted four hours and led to the cancellations of more than 6,600 flights, with 8,600 delayed, according to FlightRadar24.
It was just the third nationwide stop issued by ‌the Federal Aviation Administration this century.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the problems not on malicious actors ‌but ⁠on a failure of aging network technology in the radar and communications system used ⁠for air traffic control.

At the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, where information displays were almost completely filled with flights marked “Delayed” or “Cancelled,” some travellers appeared resigned as they wondered how long the delays would last and how their travel plans would be affected.

NBA, NHL and college teams were left stranded as they tried to reach their destinations. Meanwhile, NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time to travel to their games this weekend.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said NCAA teams will be prioritised ahead of football games on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

articles.title: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Continuous glucose monitors and automated insulin delivery systems drastically improve glycaemic control and cut hospitalisations, yet steep out-of-pocket costs and socioeconomic disparities leave a massive adoption gap

Diabetes management is moving beyond periodic finger-prick tests and clinic visits, with technologies such as continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps and mobile applications providing more detailed information on glucose levels and helping patients make day-to-day decisions about their care.

CGMs use a sensor placed on the arm or abdomen to measure glucose levels at regular intervals, offering a picture of fluctuations through the day and night. Insulin pumps deliver insulin continuously, while automated insulin delivery systems combine CGM readings with algorithms to adjust insulin delivery. Mobile applications can bring together information on glucose levels, food intake, physical activity and medication.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.
