articles.title: Samsung announces Google co-developed pricing and sale details of its smart glasses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Equipped with a high-definition camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them

Samsung has officially unveiled its new lineup of intelligent eyewear , bringing hands-free artificial intelligence into everyday fashion. Developed in partnership with Google, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the smart glasses integrate Google’s Gemini AI directly into stylish frames built for daily wear.

Set to launch on December 10, 2026, in the U.S. and South Korea, with pre-orders starting today, the collection features 30 distinct frame styles. Weighing around 41 grams, the frames combine Warby Parker’s classic look with Gentle Monster’s bold design aesthetics.

The smart glasses run on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform. Equipped with a 12 MP HD camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them. Wearers can ask Gemini to identify objects and landmarks, translate menus instantly or follow step-by-step navigation via Google Maps.

For workplace efficiency, the glasses can capture meeting whiteboards, generate key summaries and automatically sync them into Samsung Notes. The system also organises, summarises, and reads aloud incoming notifications.

To address privacy concerns, the eyewear design includes visible recording lights and audio chimes whenever the camera captures images or video. Additionally, the software claims to automatically blur bystanders’ faces during visual queries, while open-ear speakers are tuned to limit sound leakage.
The eyewear claims up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, extending up to 72 hours with its charging case.
The U.S. pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models, while Gentle Monster frames range from $449 to $489.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Starship expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for ​Saturday afternoon; the Super Heavy booster was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) on a mission the company hopes will ‌be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, ​a key test of Elon Musk’s effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship’s uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter ⁠the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and “chopstick”-arm technology to recover Starship’s lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within ‌minutes of the launch. But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface.
The booster for SpaceX's mega rocket Starship explodes after a catch attempt was aborted during a test flight from Starbase, Texas. | Photo Credit: AP

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship’s upper stage back to home base at the ‌end ⁠of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

Bringing the top portion ⁠of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its ​launch pad from SpaceX’s South Texas Starbase complex along the ‌Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship’s 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX’s satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take ‌less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk’s space and AI business ​views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

SpaceX last launched Starship ⁠in September, taking the rocket and a payload of satellites to orbit for the first time despite some rocket engines shutting down mid-flight. That mission, planned to last 10 hours, ended after roughly three hours with an upper stage splashing down intact into the Pacific Ocean before bursting into flames.

For Friday’s (November 13, 2026) mission, the company was aiming for both the lower-stage Super Heavy and the upper-stage Starship to return to the spacecraft’s Texas launch site for safe landing and recovery. Plans called for the orbital cruise vessel to touch down about 22 hours after launch. SpaceX has said it would be a “breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket” if that feat is achieved.

fullParagraphs: While 84% of the 502 adults surveyed in India felt a diabetes risk check was worthwhile even if they were healthy, only 14% believed they were likely to develop Type 2 Diabetes

fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
“We have no indication that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services,” Microsoft said in an update on social media.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.
The company said its teams are reviewing the incident and working to prevent similar disruptions in the future.

Microsoft says service availability is improving, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels. However, some users may continue to face intermittent access issues and delayed email delivery as the company restores affected infrastructure and monitors recovery.

articles.title: Series of security lapses led to burglary at Tanishq showroom in Madurai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A burglary attempt was made earlier this month as well, but it went unnoticed by the showroom authorities

A series of security lapses by those manning the newly inaugurated Tanishq showroom in Madurai led to the nocturnal burglary of gold and diamond jewellery worth several crores , which went unnoticed for a while, on the intervening night of Wednesday (November 11, 2026) and Thursday (November 12).

While many jewellery showrooms adopt the practice of emptying their showcases and securing the valuables inside safety lockers after working hours, in this showroom, the ornaments were left in the display cases, even during the night, as the locker facility was still under construction.
This allowed a lone burglar to lay his hands on the valuables without much difficulty.
The biggest lapse was the failure to turn on the anti-burglary alarm that could have alerted officials about the intruder in the dead of the night.

“The log showed that the alarm was switched off on Wednesday morning as the employees reported for duty. It should have been switched on again [on Wednesday night] before the employees locked the shutters,” the Commissioner of Police, S. Rajenthiran, said.
The police were also critical of the urgency with which the showroom was inaugurated, even as construction work on the building was incomplete.
The showroom operator had wanted to commence sales before Deepavali to tap the potential of the festive season.
However, the incomplete work left the iron scaffolding intact on the outside wall even as high-value ornaments were kept in the showroom.
“It is the scaffolding that had facilitated the burglar in gaining quick and easy access to the terrace of the tall, three-storey building,” the Commissioner added.

The officials also failed to take note of the vulnerability posed by an opening near the terrace, through which someone could easily sneak into the lift shaft. The burglar had breached it with ease by removing some screws, the police said.

The entire burglary was made possible because the two security personnel deployed on night duty had failed to secure the scaffolding. Their negligence had emboldened the burglar to make a second attempt to enter the showroom using the same scaffolding this week, after his first burglary bid on November 5, the police said.
“Even during the first attempt, the burglar’s movement was caught by cameras in the CCTV network, but it had not been noticed by the showroom officials,” a police officer said.

articles.title: CFTRI initiative aims to standardise micronutrient testing in fortified rice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: NutriQA-2026 focuses on reducing variations in laboratory results and strengthening quality assurance across the country

A one-day national colloquium on “Harmonization of Micronutrient Testing and Laboratory Quality Assurance for Food Fortification (NutriQA–2026)” was organised at CSIR-Central Food Technological Research Institute (CSIR-CFTRI), Mysuru, on Friday (November 13, 2026). The colloquium brought together eminent technical experts, representatives from Technical Support Units (TSUs), National Food Laboratories (NFLs), private testing laboratories, scientists and laboratory professionals to deliberate on strengthening analytical capabilities and harmonizing laboratory practices for food fortification.
Dr. Giridhar Parvatam, Director, CSIR-CFTRI; Prof. Jatindra Kumar Sahu, IIT Delhi; and Dr. S. Nagarajan, Head, Food Safety and Analytical Quality Control Laboratory (FSAQCL), CSIR-CFTRI were present.

In his address, Dr. Giridhar Parvatam highlighted the importance of strengthening analytical quality control and quality assurance systems to ensure the reliability of micronutrient testing in fortified foods. He emphasised the need for harmonised analytical methods, standardised laboratory protocols, competency-based training and collaborative efforts among laboratories to minimise inter-laboratory variations and generate accurate and reproducible results.

CSIR-CFTRI, in association with NIFTEM-Kundli, has been actively involved in capacity-building initiatives over the past three years to strengthen analytical competencies in the determination of vitamin B9, vitamin B12 and iron in fortified rice. The initiative is supported by IIT Delhi through funding from the Gates Foundation. Through these efforts, the institute has been contributing to strengthening the quality assurance framework for rice fortification by imparting technical training and promoting standardized analytical practices among government and private laboratory personnel across the country, a press release said.

The colloquium featured three technical sessions delivered by eminent experts in the field. Dr. Lalitha R. Gowda, former Chief Scientist and former Head, FSAQCL, CSIR-CFTRI; Dr. A. Jayadeep, former Chief Scientist and former Head, FSAQCL, CSIR-CFTRI; and Prof. Sirimavo Nair, The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (MSU), Vadodara, Gujarat, shared their technical expertise and insights on various aspects of micronutrient testing, laboratory quality assurance, and qualitative performance criteria.

A significant component of NutriQA–2026 was the pre-consultation workshop on Quality Assurance – Fine-Tuning the Training of Trainers (ToT) Training Guide. The workshop facilitated group discussions among experts and participants on different thematic areas related to laboratory quality assurance. The deliberations focused on reviewing and refining the Master Trainer Guide and Training Toolkit Checklist to ensure uniformity in training delivery, practical demonstrations, analytical procedures and competency assessment across participating laboratories, it said.

The discussions also addressed practical challenges associated with the determination of iron, vitamin B9 and vitamin B12 in premixes, fortified rice kernels (FRK) and fortified rice. The participants deliberated on harmonising sampling and analytical protocols, standardising quantitative testing procedures and strengthening competency assessment mechanisms.

The colloquium provided an important platform for knowledge exchange, technical deliberations and collaborative recommendations towards establishing a robust and sustainable network of competent laboratories across India. The initiative aims to minimise inter-laboratory variability and ensure accurate, reproducible and comparable analytical results, thereby strengthening confidence in the country’s food fortification programmes, according to the CSIR-CFTRI.

articles.title: TMC’s Abhishek appears at police station for questioning over social media post
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An FIR was registered against the TMC MP following a complaint about his social media post in May that allegedly targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Gujaratis during the Assembly poll period

TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee appeared before the police in Kolkata on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for questioning in connection with a case concerning an old social media post, an officer said.

An FIR was registered against the TMC MP following a complaint about his social media post in May that allegedly targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Gujaratis during the Assembly poll period.
The complaint, filed on May 27, alleged that the remarks were irresponsible and could potentially hurt community sentiments.
Police served Mr. Banerjee a notice directing him to appear for questioning.
The MP is being questioned at Bhowanipur police station, the officer said.
He has also been summoned by Girish Park police station in the city on November 20 in connection with another social media post.

articles.title: IIT Roorkee student death: 70 exams postponed, to be held on November 22
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Following the death of a 20-year-old student, allegedly by suicide, at IIT Roorkee , the institute has postponed 70 examinations to November 22, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
The exams were originally scheduled to be held on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The deceased, Ayush Rajauria, was a second-year student of the institute’s BS-MS programme in Mathematics and Computing and hailed from Raj Nagar Extension in Ghaziabad.

According to police, the incident came to light around midnight on Thursday after Kuldeep Singh Negi, a security officer at IIT Roorkee, informed the Kotwali Roorkee police that a student was found dead in room number BS 10 on the second floor of Govind Bhawan hostel.
A purported note left by the deceased was found in his room, in which he allegedly wrote about suffering from depression and being distressed about his life, according to officials.
Officials said Rajauria had been receiving counselling on campus for the past year to cope with mental stress.

Speaking to PTI , Sonika Srivastava, in-charge of the IIT Roorkee's media cell, said the student was being counselled at the campus wellness centre — a facility dedicated to supporting students who may be experiencing depression or other psychological challenges.
She also said that all the students and their families have been informed about the postponement of the exams and the revised scheduled date, November 22.
Police said on Friday (November 13, 2026) that the student's family had been informed and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death was underway.
In a statement, IIT Roorkee has expressed grief over the student's death and extended condolences to his family.

The death has sent shockwaves through students and parents, bringing the focus back on the mental health of IIT students across the country and the rising number of student suicides on campuses of the prestigious institutes.
(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050 and Speak2Us helpline at 9375493754.)

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 14 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

IIT Roorkee student death: 70 exams postponed, to be held on November 22

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Following the death of a 20-year-old student, allegedly by suicide, at IIT Roorkee , the institute has postponed 70 examinations to November 22, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The exams were originally scheduled to be held on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The deceased, Ayush Rajauria, was a second-year student of the institute’s BS-MS programme in Mathematics and Computing and hailed from Raj Nagar Extension in Ghaziabad.

According to police, the incident came to light around midnight on Thursday after Kuldeep Singh Negi, a security officer at IIT Roorkee, informed the Kotwali Roorkee police that a student was found dead in room number BS 10 on the second floor of Govind Bhawan hostel.

A purported note left by the deceased was found in his room, in which he allegedly wrote about suffering from depression and being distressed about his life, according to officials.

Officials said Rajauria had been receiving counselling on campus for the past year to cope with mental stress.

Speaking to PTI , Sonika Srivastava, in-charge of the IIT Roorkee's media cell, said the student was being counselled at the campus wellness centre — a facility dedicated to supporting students who may be experiencing depression or other psychological challenges.

She also said that all the students and their families have been informed about the postponement of the exams and the revised scheduled date, November 22.

Police said on Friday (November 13, 2026) that the student's family had been informed and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death was underway.

In a statement, IIT Roorkee has expressed grief over the student's death and extended condolences to his family.

The death has sent shockwaves through students and parents, bringing the focus back on the mental health of IIT students across the country and the rising number of student suicides on campuses of the prestigious institutes.

(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050 and Speak2Us helpline at 9375493754.)

articles.title: Three phase gram panchayat polls in Bapatla district from November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Elections would be held for 3,362 wards through 3,770 polling stations. The district has 8,67,954 voters, including 4,23,910 men, 4,43,995 women and 49 others

Elections to 351 gram panchayats in Bapatla district will be conducted in three phases, with the first phase scheduled for November 26, District Collector V. Vinod Kumar announced on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
Addressing a media conference, he said elections would be held for 3,362 wards through 3,770 polling stations. The district has 8,67,954 voters, including 4,23,910 men, 4,43,995 women and 49 others.

The first phase will cover six mandals in the Parchur constituency, while the second will cover seven mandals in the Vemuru and Chirala constituencies. The third phase will cover seven mandals in the Bapatla and Repalle constituencies.

For the first phase, nominations will be accepted from November 15 to 17, followed by scrutiny on November 18. Appeals against rejected nominations can be filed on November 19 and will be resolved the next day. Candidates can withdraw nominations on November 21, when the final list will be published. Polling and counting will take place on November 26, followed by the election of deputy sarpanches.
Under G.O. No. 11, unanimous gram panchayat elections will attract development incentives of ₹15 lakh, ₹25 lakh and ₹50 lakh, depending on population.
The Collector also announced Bapatla municipality elections on November 26. He urged voters to verify their names in the electoral rolls and exercise their franchise.

articles.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The existing 13-metre carriageway will be widened to 22 metres, allowing four-way traffic movement, with an additional three metres of road space sought at Karbala Maidan to facilitate one-way movement during diversions.

For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Women must get adequate representation in Parliament, legislatures: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Government to extend full support to Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians’ India region conference in Bengaluru

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 14, 2026) stressed the need for adequate representation of women in Parliament and State legislatures, expressing hope that the Women’s Reservation Bill would be implemented soon. Incidentally, Karnataka is yet to have a woman representative in its Cabinet.

“The Women’s Reservation Bill has been passed in the Rajya Sabha and is yet to be approved by the Lok Sabha. I am hopeful that it will become a reality in the coming Parliament session. Women must get adequate representation in Parliament and State legislatures,” he said.
He was speaking after unveiling the logo of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region conference, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru on November 17 and 18.

Recalling former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s contribution to women’s political empowerment, Mr. Shivakumar said it was his government that had brought in legislation providing 50% reservation for women in local bodies, from panchayats to district-level administration. He said he believed that all political parties supported women’s reservation.

Highlighting women’s presence in important constitutional and administrative positions in Karnataka, he said the Governor, Chief Secretary, Karnataka Legislative Assembly Secretary, Legislative Council Secretary and Deputy Chairperson of the Legislative Council were all women.
“It is a matter of satisfaction that women are holding key positions in the State’s administration. Women are the eyes of a family. When women are empowered, men too become empowered,” he said.

Describing the CWP conference as a historic milestone for Karnataka, Mr. Shivakumar said the State government would extend all support to the first independent CWP India Region conference being held in Bengaluru.

The conference, being organised under the leadership of CWP India Region president D. Purandeswari, is expected to bring together more than 150 women parliamentarians, legislators and presiding officers from India and abroad.
The participants are expected to deliberate on the country’s development and protection of women’s rights, he said.

The government would extend all necessary assistance through Legislative Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed to ensure the successful conduct of the conference, he said.

Mr. Shivakumar also recalled the contributions of former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sucheta Kripalani, the country’s first woman Chief Minister, and President Droupadi Murmu.
Their achievements demonstrated that women could accomplish anything they set their minds to, he added.

articles.title: Four earthquakes recorded in J-K, Ladakh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Of the four tremors, three were recorded in the Chenab Valley region of Jammu and Kashmir, while one struck Leh in the Union Territory of Ladakh, according to NCS updates shared on X

Four earthquakes with magnitudes ranging from 2.9 to 3.9 were recorded across Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh within a span of 11 hours on Saturday (November 14, 2026), the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said.
Of the four tremors, three were recorded in the Chenab Valley region of Jammu and Kashmir, while one struck Leh in the Union Territory of Ladakh, according to NCS updates shared on X .
There were no reports of damage from the earthquake hit areas, police said.
An earthquake of 3.3 magnitude struck Kishtwar district at 2:38 a.m., with the epicentre located at a depth of 15 km.
Another tremor of 3.8 magnitude hit Doda district at 8:48 a.m. The epicentre was identified at a depth of 5 km.
Another 2.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Doda at 1:09 p.m., at a depth of 10 km.
A 3.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Leh, Ladakh, at 10:29 a.m., at a depth of 10 km.

articles.title: No Indians onboard in carrier involved in Mississippi mishap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The bitumen carrier, Atlantic Asphalt, that rammed into riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans does not have Indian crew onboard.

The tanker that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with about 180 people aboard on Friday (November 13, 2026). All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River.
As per government records, on Atlantic Asphalt that can carry some 17,500 tonnes of bitumen used in laying roads, there were no Indians onboard, sources said.
The ship registered in Marshall Islands and owned by a company formally registered in Liberia is manned by a Singapore ship management company which does employ Indian seafarers on its ships.
It is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation, a sprawling Chinese state-owned conglomerate, according to the website MarineTraffic.

The Chinese company overseeing the asphalt tanker in 2022 accounted for nearly a quarter of the global commercial shipbuilding market, according to a report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. It was also the largest military shipbuilder in the world at the time.

Onsite videos show that the ship seemed to have lost control of its steering, if not power, that led to the accident. The boat took in water, tilted and sank along the jetty. Passengers who were thrown into the water were seen wearing lifejackets that would have helped save lives.

In March 2024, container ship Dali, with mostly Indian crew, rammed into a bridge in Baltimore that led to loss of six lives and property damaged leading to the largest marine insurance settlements running to billions of dollars. Dali lost power as well as steering leading to the accident.
Ever Given that blocked Suez Canal traffic for nearly six days in 2021 had 25 Indian crew onboard.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ‌technology giant said it was “monitoring the backlog of email messages ‌accrued during this ​event” before considering the issue with ⁠the enterprise services resolved.
Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.
Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.
The Redmond, Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.
It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

articles.title: Riots in France: How anti-Government protests spiralled out of control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The French authorities’ heavy-handed response, including thousands of arrests, police beatings and curbs on marches, has added to the volatile mix of grievances fuelling an anti-Government groundswell that shows no sign of abating before next year’s presidential election
Smashed windows and ransacked shops. Bloodied teenage protesters. A city hall on fire.
Such scenes shocked France as rioting erupted last month during nationwide protests over high living costs and strained public services.

Government officials have repeatedly blamed far-left radicals and “opportunistic delinquents,” who they say took advantage of mostly peaceful demonstrations ​to attack symbols of State authority and capitalism across France.

But the authorities’ heavy-handed response, including thousands of arrests, police beatings and curbs on marches, has added to the volatile mix of grievances fuelling an anti-Government groundswell that shows no sign of abating before next year’s presidential election, Reuters found.

Reuters journalists reviewed dozens of videos of the violence, attended ‌the court hearings of 26 people accused of taking part and interviewed over 50 Government officials, police officers, attorneys, protesters and witnesses to understand how a movement that began in September with small protests over conditions in State schools spiralled ​into some of the worst civil unrest in years.

Police tactics have faced scrutiny since the start due to the life-changing injuries suffered by some young people, including blown-off hands and lost eyes. United Nations and other human rights experts have also raised concerns about ⁠the arrest of nearly 7,000 minors during sometimes-violent school blockades, which they said was disproportionate.

Images of riot police baton-charging teenagers fanned support for the students from a diverse array of protesters, including parents, teachers, left-wing politicians and trade unionists, who joined their marches.

“We have rights,” said Emilie Berthier de Grandry, 42, who has attended four demonstrations in Paris with her 15-year-old son, Aaron, dressed in an inflatable shark costume. “We’re not going to let ourselves be pushed around.”

Nationwide demonstrations on October 17 also brought a resurgence of so-called yellow-vest protesters, an anti-establishment movement that faced off against President Emmanuel Macron’s Government in 2018-2019 over high fuel prices.

The violent outbursts were so intense that day that police lost control of ‌entire neighbourhoods to rioters and looters in France’s three largest cities: Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Every week since then, people have taken to the streets across France to voice their anger at police and the Government.

While the protests after October 17 were calmer, clashes erupted when police sought to disperse demonstrators as marches wound down. Officers repeatedly fired tear gas and charged groups of protesters who pelted them with bottles, paving stones and mortar-style fireworks. On October 24, far-right gangs entered the fray saying they wanted to protect businesses ‌and clashed with protesters in several cities, authorities said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Millions of customers, abruptly, lost access to their savings accounts and pension payments after regulators seized the bank, setting off a sequence of events that culminated in a change of political leadership

The story so far: Following impeachment proceedings initiated against President Santiago Pena in connection with the collapse of a private lender holding savings for nearly half of the country’s population, Paraguay’s Senate voted to remove him for misconduct in office and placed him under house arrest on November 6. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as President.

The development comes just a day after Mr. Pena announced his resignation amid angry protests across the country over a financial crisis triggered by the collapse of a Ueno, a prominent digital lender-turned-bank that catered to nearly three million people and held about $800 million in public funds. Around 60% of the country’s adult population, abruptly, lost access to their savings accounts and pension payments after regulators took control of the bank, setting off a sequence of events that culminated in a change of political leadership.

articles.title: South Sudan postpones first national elections until February
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict
South Sudan, the world’s newest country, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) postponed its first national elections from December to February amid growing ethnic and political battles.
The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict.
The electoral commission issued a new calendar on social media, giving a new voting date of February 11, with results to be announced four days later.
Commission secretary general Ahon Malou Lueth confirmed the change to AFP but would not give a reason or other details.
President Salva Kiir’s government forces and followers of detained former Vice President Riek Machar have been involved in escalating, deadly confrontations in recent months.
Other ethnic tensions and cattle-rustling battles have also complicated the picture in one of the world’s poorest countries.
South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011, but Mr. Kiir’s and Mr. Machar’s forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that killed at least 400,000 people.
Mr. Machar has been under house arrest since March 2025, accused of “crimes against humanity”.

The new election date was announced on the day that voter registration was due to start, with more than 3,100 centres set up across the country. Not all the necessary equipment had arrived at the centres, officials said.

The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan has issued several warnings about conditions in the country, including the displacement of tens of thousands of people, the deadly battles and the disruption of international humanitarian operations.
The commission has said that the tensions of recent months heighten “the risk of renewed conflict and atrocity crimes” while in October it said holding an election could spark renewed conflict.

🌐 International Affairs 📅 14 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

South Sudan postpones first national elections until February

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict

South Sudan, the world’s newest country, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) postponed its first national elections from December to February amid growing ethnic and political battles.

The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict.

The electoral commission issued a new calendar on social media, giving a new voting date of February 11, with results to be announced four days later.

Commission secretary general Ahon Malou Lueth confirmed the change to AFP but would not give a reason or other details.

President Salva Kiir’s government forces and followers of detained former Vice President Riek Machar have been involved in escalating, deadly confrontations in recent months.

Other ethnic tensions and cattle-rustling battles have also complicated the picture in one of the world’s poorest countries.

South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011, but Mr. Kiir’s and Mr. Machar’s forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that killed at least 400,000 people.

Mr. Machar has been under house arrest since March 2025, accused of “crimes against humanity”.

The new election date was announced on the day that voter registration was due to start, with more than 3,100 centres set up across the country. Not all the necessary equipment had arrived at the centres, officials said.

The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan has issued several warnings about conditions in the country, including the displacement of tens of thousands of people, the deadly battles and the disruption of international humanitarian operations.

The commission has said that the tensions of recent months heighten “the risk of renewed conflict and atrocity crimes” while in October it said holding an election could spark renewed conflict.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: South Sudan, the world’s newest country, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) postponed its first national elections from December to February amid growing ethnic and political battles.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The commission has said that the tensions of recent months heighten “the risk of renewed conflict and atrocity crimes” while in October it said holding an election could spark renewed conflict.

articles.title: Avian influenza confirmed in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore; over 1,500 chickens culled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1) has been confirmed in chicken samples collected from a poultry farm at Kattiyankuppam village in Kurinjipadi taluk of Cuddalore district.

“The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, had confirmed the H5N1 avian influenza virus in samples collected from a poultry carcass on November 5, 2026,” District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar told The Hindu .

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre.

According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.”
He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.”

As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai.
On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said.
Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease.

“Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.
The carcasses are being disposed of through deep burial in designated pits, with bleaching powder applied and biosecurity measures in place.
An official said that movement of birds to and from the affected farms has been strictly restricted.

articles.title: Who pays for the AI boom? Texas communities are asking tough questions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Behind America’s race to build data centres is a growing concern over electricity, water and land use. It’s a warning for countries, including India, that want to become AI powerhouses

“Hey, what do you think of the data centre that’s coming up right across the street from here? I see a lot of construction happening around us all the time,” I ask my colleague Kevin, sounding innocent and naïve, for my Swedish friends had warned me — when I was moving to the U.S. earlier this year — not to touch politics or any sensitive topic at the workplace in America. Instead, talk about family, they had recommended. I didn’t know where data centres fell on that spectrum.

Kevin stiffens. We are having lunch. He carefully places his fork down and looks past me through the window, where a dusty haze from the construction is floating in the hot Texan air, and starts talking softly.

articles.title: Samsung announces Google co-developed smart glasses pricing and sale details
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Equipped with a high-definition camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them

Samsung has officially unveiled its new lineup of intelligent eyewear , bringing hands-free artificial intelligence into everyday fashion. Developed in partnership with Google, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the smart glasses integrate Google’s Gemini AI directly into stylish frames built for daily wear.

Set to launch on December 10, 2026, in the U.S. and South Korea, with pre-orders starting today, the collection features 30 distinct frame styles. Weighing around 41 grams, the frames combine Warby Parker’s classic look with Gentle Monster’s bold design aesthetics.

The smart glasses run on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform. Equipped with a 12 MP HD camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them. Wearers can ask Gemini to identify objects and landmarks, translate menus instantly or follow step-by-step navigation via Google Maps.

For workplace efficiency, the glasses can capture meeting whiteboards, generate key summaries and automatically sync them into Samsung Notes. The system also organises, summarises, and reads aloud incoming notifications.

To address privacy concerns, the eyewear design includes visible recording lights and audio chimes whenever the camera captures images or video. Additionally, the software claims to automatically blur bystanders’ faces during visual queries, while open-ear speakers are tuned to limit sound leakage.
The eyewear claims up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, extending up to 72 hours with its charging case.
The U.S. pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models, while Gentle Monster frames range from $449 to $489.

articles.title: KLE Society’s 111th Foundation Day celebrated by collecting 300 units of blood
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: KLE Technological University celebrated the 111th Foundation Day of KLE Society in Hubballi on Friday, by paying tribute to its founders and organising a voluntary blood donation camp in which over 300 units of blood were collected.

KLE Technological University celebrated the 111th Foundation Day of KLE Society in Hubballi on Friday (November 13, 2026), by paying tribute to its founders and organising a voluntary blood donation camp in which over 300 units of blood were collected.

Addressing the gathering, Vice-Chancellor Prakash G. Tewari recalled the founding of the society and lauded the vision and dedication of its founders in expanding access to education. He said their contribution to society continued to inspire generations.

The celebrations were attended by Registrar Basavaraj Anami, Executive Dean B.L. Desai deans Uma Mudengudi and Sanjay Kotabagi and Coordinator of the C&M Cell M.R. Patil, besides heads of departments, faculty members, administrators, staff and student representatives.

In the blood donation camp organised in association with Rashtrotthana Blood Bank and Karnataka Medical College and Research Institute (KMCRI), with the support of HDFC Bank, Hubballi, 300 units of blood were donated by faculty members and students.

Rashtrotthana Blood Bank administrator Dattamurthy Kulkarni, KMCRI Blood Bank Officer Anil Kumar and HDFC Bank Circle Head Madhusudhan Radhakrishna were present along with Sports Activities Coordinator Vijayakumar Nimbagal.
Medical teams from the partner institutions supervised the donation process, while student volunteers coordinated the arrangements.

articles.title: Government is committed to supporting startups in Kalyana Karnataka: Priyank Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kalaburagi aims to increase its contribution to State GDP from 1.9% to 3%

The Karnataka government will extend all necessary support to entrepreneurs in Kalyana Karnataka to establish and expand startups by facilitating access to investment, mentorship, technology and market linkages, Minister for Home, Information Technology and Biotechnology (IT-BT) and E-Governance and Kalaburagi District In-charge Priyank Kharge said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
Speaking at the ‘Kalyana Karnataka Startup Dialogue-2026’ in Kalaburagi, he urged young entrepreneurs to come forward with innovative ideas and pursue their business ventures with determination.

Referring to his government’s policies and schemes for encouraging start-ups, Mr. Kharge urged the young entrepreneurs to study the initiatives and identify the support available for their ventures. “If existing policies do not address their specific requirements, they should bring the gaps to the government’s notice. We are ready to formulate suitable new schemes and stand by young entrepreneurs,” he said.

Pointing out that Bengaluru contributed around 41% to the State’s GDP, he said Kalaburagi’s contribution was estimated at 1.9%. “The government aimed to increase this to 3%, which would require concerted efforts across sectors, including education, agriculture and manufacturing. Startups would play a significant role in accelerating the economic growth of Kalyana Karnataka,” he added.

Mr. Kharge said the State government’s ELEVATE programme had supported the establishment of around 1,500 startups over the past 10 years. “Selected startups were eligible for financial assistance of up to ₹50 lakh. Startups based outside Bengaluru currently accounted for around 28% of the total, and the government was working to increase this proportion by encouraging entrepreneurship across the State,” he said and added that a scheme was also being planned to provide selected entrepreneurs working in the deep-tech sector with financial assistance of up to ₹1 crore over the next 10 years.

Emphasising that startups should not remain confined to Bengaluru but expand to tier-II and tier-III cities, Mr. Kharge said the government had introduced the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP) to strengthen local economies and encourage young people to become job creators rather than job seekers.

“Young entrepreneurs needed to understand market demand, business management, product positioning and customer outreach. Having an innovative idea alone was not be sufficient; they also needed the skills to turn it into a sustainable business. Interaction and mentoring programmes involving entrepreneurs and industry experts are being organised to help them acquire these skills,” Mr. Kharge said.

The minister said that the government was also taking up several initiatives to promote artificial intelligence (AI) in Kalyana Karnataka and incubation centres were being established to encourage startups.

Medical Education Minister Dr. Sharan Prakash Patil, Srikrishna Sridhar Murthy of Sattva Consulting and Prashanth Prakash, Founding Partner of Accel India, shared their views and experiences at the interaction. KrishiKalpa Foundation CEO C.M. Patil moderated the discussion.
Earlier, K. Ullas Kamath, founder of UK&Co, delivered a special address on the growth of local entrepreneurship and the skills required to build successful businesses.

articles.title: Will R&AW’s overseas operations affect ties? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Why have the U.S., Canada, Australia and Pakistan brought up allegations that the agency has spearheaded targeted killings and surveillance of separatists on their soil? What is the Indian government’s stand? Do these operations follow certain norms, especially if it’s a friendly country?

The story so far: India’s external intelligence agency R&AW (Research and Analysis Wing) was in the spotlight this week, as reports came in from the U.S., Canada, Australia and Pakistan of the alleged targeting and killing of Indian-origin Khalistani separatist operatives around the world, spearheaded by the agency.

The charges, that are yet to be proven in court, pertain to a number of investigations in different countries. This week, the U.S.-based Washington Post claimed that American officials believe that the R&AW’s previous chief Samant Goel had approved an assassination operation, that was foiled last year, against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a Khalistani activist lawyer of U.S. and Canadian nationality on India’s most-wanted UAPA (Unlawful Activities Prevention Act) terror list. It also revealed the name of a security official, Vikash Yadav, believed to have been at R&AW at the time, and said U.S. officials had discussed whether to indict him for ordering Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta to hire a hitman for the job. In the indictment filed by the U.S. New York Southern District Attorney’s office last November, message transcripts indicated Mr. Gupta had also enquired about ordering a “hit” on a Khalistani activist in Canada, just days before the killing of Canadian Hardeep Singh Nijjar outside Toronto in June 2023.

articles.title: Indian Railways to connect Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya through weekly train service
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations
Indian Railways is going to operate a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.

The Ministry of Railways stated in a statement on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the initiative is to link two places which are associated with “the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace Lord Ram.”
The route will cover approximately 604 kilometres, connecting Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.
Railways Ministry said that the service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.

Citing the role of railway connectivity on bilateral cooperation, the Ministry said in a statement, “India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.”
India and Nepal have held discussions on cross-border railway links, including passenger train services on the Janakpur-Ayodhya section, and bilateral cooperation in the sector in June this year.

articles.title: U.S. media names Indian official who allegedly ordered plot on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

U.S. authorities believe the alleged plot to kill Khalistani activist, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, who is wanted on terror charges in India, was ordered by the previous chief of the Indian Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), and had official sanction from senior intelligence officials with “with ties to [Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inner circle”, the Washington Post, a U.S.-national daily, reported .

The report in the Washington Post newspaper identified, for the first time, an R&AW officer whose name had been withheld in the case papers made available by the Justice Department in New York in November 2023. In a separate press release, the Post said, on the basis of interviews with “more than three dozen current and former senior officials in the United States, India, Canada, Britain, Germany and Australia”, that other R&AW officers have faced “arrest, expulsion and reprimand” in recent months, indicating that there was more international coordination about what it called “escalating campaign of aggression” against Indian diaspora members by India’s intelligence operatives.

The Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the latest story in the Washington Post report on Monday. Last week, in response to a question on the allegations, the MEA spokesperson said that a “high-level committee is looking into information that was shared by the American side with us, because [it] also equally impacts our national security. In recent weeks, the government has also blocked the broadcast of documentaries by Canadian and Australian public broadcasters CBC and ABC that focussed on the allegations against Indian agencies for targeting Khalistani activists abroad.

“In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence officials have assessed that the operation targeting Pannun was approved by the RAW chief at the time, Samant Goel,” said the report. “U.S. spy agencies have more tentatively assessed that Mr. Modi’s National Security Adviser, Ajit Doval, was probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists,” it added.

According to the story, the R&AW official identified as Vikash Yadav had directed Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic pending extradition to the U.S. to stand trial in the case, to hire a hitman to kill GS Pannun outside his New York residence. Mr. Yadav, believed to be a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) official on deputation to the R&AW, has subsequently been repatriated to the paramilitary forces, other U.S. media have reported.

While the MEA Ministry of External Affairs has maintained that such killings are not Indian policy, and has denied Canadian allegations of a similar hit on Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, the government has agreed to an enquiry on the U.S. allegations.
The Washington Post story also dwells at length on differences between the U.S. White House administration and the Justice Department that oversaw the FBI-DEA investigation in the case.

The evidence cited had included an undercover American agent who was hired for the Pannun killing by Mr. Gupta, under direct orders from Mr. Yadav, surveillance of messages purportedly exchanged between them, as well as a photograph allegedly showing three Indian intelligence officials who gave the green signal for the plot during a video-call.

However, the report stated while the Justice Department pushed for an indictment against both Mr. Gupta and Mr. Yadav, Biden administration officials prevailed in ensuring the indictment is against only Mr. Gupta at present, ostensibly so as not to “rupture” ties with India.

The matter was thrashed out a series of meetings which included U.S. Deputy NSA Jon Finer, U.S. Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Deputy CIA Director David Cohen, the report said. It also stated Mr. President Biden had discussed the issue with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting in September 2023, calling for accountability for the case.

articles.title: What are the legal compulsions and political hurdles in Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it

The story so far: Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport and a national identity card from the Government of Bangladesh on Monday (November 9, 2026). In response, Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said that Bangladesh seeks her extradition under an “acceptable prisoner transfer process”. This is the latest episode in the Hasina saga that began when she came to India on August 5, 2024, after the student-led uprising toppled her government.

Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024 by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka, which has sentenced her to death for it. Her challenge is now to return to face justice and yet emerge as a leader of her country. She has refused to apologise for the crackdown, saying the police did not take her orders, but responded to angry agitators and militants who had provoked them.

articles.title: YSRCP leaders complain to Andhra DGP over ‘offensive’ remarks on Jagan’s family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Accusing JSP supporters of making obscene remarks on social media, they allege that the police failed to register an FIR even 60 hours after receiveing a complaint

A group of YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leaders lodged a complaint with Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta on Saturday, accusing Jana Sena Party (JSP) supporters of making obscene and derogatory remarks against party president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s family members on social media platform X. They also demanded that stringent action be taken.

A YSRCP delegation comprising former Minister Vellampalli Srinivas, MLC Kalpalatha Reddy, former MLA Malladi Vishnu and other senior leaders submitted a pen drive containing evidence to the officials at the DGP’s office, as Mr. Gupta was not available.
Addressing the media, the YSRCP leaders alleged that the Vijayawada cybercrime police did not register an FIR even 60 hours after receiving a complaint, along with evidence in this regard.

Mr. Srinivas questioned the silence of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha over the issue. Ms. Kalpalatha Reddy condemned the alleged remarks against women in Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s family.
Mr. Vishnu alleged that the police were acting selectively, registering cases against the YSRCP activists even at midnight but failing to act on their complaint.
The YSRCP leaders warned that they would pursue legal action if the police failed to register cases against those responsible.

articles.title: Bengaluru family murders: Did accused take victims’ thumbprints to claim property?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police are now probing a property angle in the ghastly murder of seven persons of the same family in Rajajinagar, Bengaluru.

Cab driver-turned-YouTuber and tabloid editor Indushekhar allegedly killed his wife, mother-in-law, and family members of his brothers-in-law. He was assisted by his minor daughter. He allegedly claimed the family had been insulting him, pushing him to kill them. However, the police are now probing whether the accused took the thumb impressions of the deceased on stamp papers after he killed them. He is suspected of having collected the impressions to establish his claim over the property.
According to the police, the accused was allegedly eyeing a 30x40 site in Srirampura owned by his mother-in-law, Roopavathi.

The police suspect that Indushekhar’s minor daughter actively assisted him in the crime in the hope of inheriting the Srirampura property. Indushekhar had allegedly promised to transfer the house in her name, after which she agreed to help him, investigators suspect.

Meanwhile, forensic teams have collected scientific evidence from Indushekhar’s house, the scene of the crime. Investigators suspect that bloodstains from the hall, bathroom and the alleged murder weapon, a grinding stone, were wiped off after the killings.

A luminol test was conducted to identify traces of blood that may have remained despite the cleaning. The samples collected by the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) and Scene of Crime Officer (SOCO) teams have been sent for further examination.
Luminol is a forensic chemical that reacts with haemoglobin in blood and produces a blue glow, helping investigators detect possible blood traces that are invisible to the naked eye.

Bengaluru family murders: Did accused take victims’ thumbprints to claim property?

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The police are now probing a property angle in the ghastly murder of seven persons of the same family in Rajajinagar, Bengaluru.

Cab driver-turned-YouTuber and tabloid editor Indushekhar allegedly killed his wife, mother-in-law, and family members of his brothers-in-law. He was assisted by his minor daughter. He allegedly claimed the family had been insulting him, pushing him to kill them. However, the police are now probing whether the accused took the thumb impressions of the deceased on stamp papers after he killed them. He is suspected of having collected the impressions to establish his claim over the property.

According to the police, the accused was allegedly eyeing a 30x40 site in Srirampura owned by his mother-in-law, Roopavathi.

The police suspect that Indushekhar’s minor daughter actively assisted him in the crime in the hope of inheriting the Srirampura property. Indushekhar had allegedly promised to transfer the house in her name, after which she agreed to help him, investigators suspect.

Meanwhile, forensic teams have collected scientific evidence from Indushekhar’s house, the scene of the crime. Investigators suspect that bloodstains from the hall, bathroom and the alleged murder weapon, a grinding stone, were wiped off after the killings.

A luminol test was conducted to identify traces of blood that may have remained despite the cleaning. The samples collected by the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) and Scene of Crime Officer (SOCO) teams have been sent for further examination.

Luminol is a forensic chemical that reacts with haemoglobin in blood and produces a blue glow, helping investigators detect possible blood traces that are invisible to the naked eye.

articles.title: KDA chairman expresses displeasure over ineffective implementation of govt. orders and closure of Kannada medium schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kannada Development Authority (KDA) Chairman Purushottama Bilimale has expressed displeasure over the ineffective implementation of government orders aimed at developing the Kannada language and literature.
Mr. Bilimale was also concerned about the closure of government Kannada-medium schools.

​Inaugurating a two-day 12th Raichur District Kannada Sahitya Sammelana at the Pandit Siddarama Jambaladinni Rangamandira, Mr. Bilimale noted that while the Chief Minister, Deputy Chief Minister, and Education Minister possess the political will to promote the language and the government has passed 2,800 orders since the unification of the State, only 40% of them have been effectively implemented due to a lack of enthusiasm among officials.

​He stated that he had visited 24 districts and interacted with over 1,800 officials across various departments, including Deputy Commissioners and university authorities, only to find poor execution of pro-Kannada directives.

​Highlighting the three primary challenges facing the language – internal administrative issues, education, and employment – Mr. Bilimale expressed concern over the closure of Kannada-medium schools. He attributed the dwindling student strength partly to the Karnataka’s Total Fertility Rate dropping from 2.9 to 1.6 over the last four decades.

​On the employment front, he flagged the declining participation of Kannadigas in the labour market. From Greater Bengaluru’s construction and hospitality sectors to areca nut plantations, workers from outside the State now dominate the workforce, he said.

Mr. Bilimale stressed the need to introspect on whether Kannadigas are reluctant to take up such jobs or are being denied opportunities. Calling upon literary conferences to go beyond mere discussions and pass concrete resolutions, Mr. Bilimale urged collective efforts to make Kannada the “language of livelihood” ( annada bhashe ).

District in-charge Minister Ajay Singh, MLC and reception committee chairman N.S. Boseraju, MLA Shivaraj Patil, MP G. Kumar Naik, Adikavi Sri Maharshi Valmiki University Vice-Chancellor Shivanand Kelaginamani, Parishat district president Ranganna Patil Allundi, former president Veerahanuman, Karnataka State Information Commission (Kalaburagi Bench) Commissioner B. Venkatasingh, journalists Basavaraj Swamy and Aravind Kulkarni, Working Journalists’ Association district president R. Gurunath, Government Employees’ Association district president Krishna Shavantagera, Superintendent of Police Arunangshu Giri, Corporation Commissioner Jubeen Mohapatra, and others were present.

articles.title: On board Bengaluru’s Pink Line: First-day excitement meets commuter scepticism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The first day of commercial operations on the elevated section of Namma Metro’s Pink Line on Saturday, November 14, saw a mix of curiosity and cautious optimism among commuters, with several passengers welcoming the new connectivity while questioning the usefulness of opening only a part of the corridor.

While the newly opened stretch offered a glimpse of the long-awaited metro connectivity along Bannerghatta Road, many commuters felt that its full potential would be realised only after the underground section becomes operational, connecting south Bengaluru with the Central Business District (CBD) and northern parts of the city.

As The Hindu took a ride on the Pink Line on its first day of commercial operations, several passengers on board had come with their families, particularly children, to experience the newly inaugurated metro service. With Saturday being a weekend, some passengers treated the journey as a family outing, taking selfies and exploring the new stations and trains rather than using the service solely for their commute.

The Pink Line, part of Namma Metro’s Phase 2 network, will connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in the north. The 21.25-km corridor comprises a 7.5-km elevated section and a 13.76-km underground stretch. However, only the elevated portion, serving six stations along Bannerghatta Road, has been opened for commercial operations.

The newly introduced Pink Line trains, manufactured by BEML Limited, are equipped with several modern passenger amenities. The trains are driverless-capable and compatible with Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) technology. Inside the coaches, passengers can access USB charging ports, ergonomically designed seating, and modern interiors. Upgraded passenger information display systems provide details of stations and upcoming stops, while improved emergency communication buttons are among the other noticeable features.

Mahesh Rao, a commuter from BTM Layout, travelled with his granddaughter to experience the new metro service. He took a ride between N.S. Palya and J.P. Nagar 4th Phase and Kalena Agrahara before returning.

“The ride was good. Everything is new, and it feels great to finally see this stretch open for the public. We have been watching the construction of this metro line for several years, and it is satisfying to see it become operational. I hope this stretch benefits many people and helps reduce traffic congestion in the area,” he said.

However, not all commuters were convinced about the immediate usefulness of the partial opening. Vinil S., a resident of Bilekahalli, said that although his first experience on the Pink Line was good, the initial enthusiasm among passengers might not necessarily translate into sustained ridership. “The government and BMRCL could have prioritised opening the entire corridor instead of operating only a part of it. Running trains on a limited stretch, without the larger network in place, may not attract the expected number of commuters and could result in underutilisation of resources,” he added.
