articles.title: Private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep soon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As part of the trial, the ship, capable of accommodating 250 passengers, anchored safely at the port wharf. Maiden commercial run anticipated in November
A private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep is set to commence operations following the arrival of the vessel Theja at the Beypore port on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The initiative aims to restore maritime connectivity that has faced prolonged interruptions. As part of the trial, the ship, capable of accommodating 250 passengers, anchored safely at the port wharf in the morning. Official clearance procedures and regulatory approvals are in progress, with the maiden commercial run anticipated this month.

According to port officials, the initiative aligns with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s ‘Mission Samudra’ development framework, which seeks to leverage Keralam’s extensive coastline and port infrastructure to catalyse new economic and commercial prospects. Representatives of the operating company had recently met the Chief Minister to brief him about the project’s progress and strategic importance, they said.

Stakeholders noted that beyond streamlining passenger transit, the service would give a fresh momentum for maritime tourism at the historically significant Beypore port, while strengthening socio-economic and commercial ties between Keralam and the archipelago.

articles.title: Eye donation awareness programme organised at Ernakulam MCH
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The event was held ahead of the hospital’s application for a licence to perform corneal transplantation

The Government Medical College Hospital (MCH), Ernakulam, and the Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (K-SOTTO) jointly organised an eye donation awareness programme at the hospital on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
The event was held ahead of the hospital’s application for a licence to perform corneal transplantation, according to a communication.

A special internal counselling team was formed as part of the programme to streamline eye donation and corneal transplantation activities at the hospital. The team will be responsible for communicating with the relatives of deceased patients and explaining the importance of eye donation. Its members will also receive specialised training in the technical and legal aspects of corneal donation and transplantation.

articles.title: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The U.K.-India climate partnership shows what delivery can look like in practice. Both our countries recognise that the shift to cleaner growth is not separate from the pursuit of prosperity

Next week, Mumbai will become the stage for one of the world’s boldest climate ideas. The largest ever Earthshot Prize edition will bring together innovators, investors, businesses, policymakers and young people to turn environmental solutions into impact at scale. Five winners will each receive £1 million to accelerate their work.

It all began with a simple but powerful idea: that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair our planet. Founded by His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales, The Earthshot Prize seeks solutions capable of delivering transformative environmental impact. Since the Prize was launched in 2020, India has produced more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country (nine finalists including four winners). This year two of the 15 finalists are based in India. As the Prize arrives in Mumbai, India’s growing influence in clean growth and climate innovation will be on full display.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula
Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile".
He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations.
Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage.
A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack".
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night of having intercepted a drone in the Riyadh area.

It previously said it had knocked down several other missiles and drones from Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night through Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, though it was unclear whether they were the ones mentioned by the Iran-backed group.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said it had intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region and another in Saudi Arabia's east.
It also said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night that it had destroyed two ballistic missiles targeting western Saudi Arabia.
Two more drones were destroyed in the country's south and the region around the holy city of Mecca, it added late Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

articles.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”; it determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks

A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.
Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

articles.title: Modi in Bengaluru: PM flags off elevated stretch of Namma Metro Pink Line | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: PM Modi is also scheduled to inaugurate the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express

The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.
Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the elevated section of Bengaluru’s Pink Line Metro at S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, in the presence of Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

The Pink Line is part of Namma Metro’s Phase II and is designed to connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in north Bengaluru. The 21.25-km corridor comprises a 7.5-km elevated section and a 13.76-km underground section.
Once fully operational, the corridor is projected to carry approximately 3.76 lakh passengers daily, according to the Detailed Project Report (DPR).

Mr. Modi later travelled by Metro to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station accompanied by Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya.
Before entering the platform, Mr Modi purchased a Metro ticket. BMRCL officials briefed him on the project before he boarded the train, a BMRCL source told The Hindu .

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav have arrived by helicopter at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Training Centre campus near Dairy Circle on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru.

Modi will proceed to S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, where he, along with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, will flag off the Pink Line Metro service and undertake a ride to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.

The PM will also unveil plaques marking the foundation stone-laying of three projects, including a compressed biogas plant at Haralakunte village in Bengaluru South and two power transmission projects.
He will also inaugurate renewable energy transmission schemes in Koppal, Gadag and Bidar.
The programme also includes dedication of an 80 TMT LPG cavern developed by HPCL, the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of MRPL, railway doubling and electrification projects.

articles.title: Central Railway to run four special Mumbai-Nagpur trains between November 13-15
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is intended to help accommodate additional passenger traffic during the ongoing festive season
The Central Railway has announced four special train services between Mumbai and Nagpur from November 13 to 15 to accommodate additional passenger traffic during the festive season.

According to a press release issued on Thursday (November 12, 2026), two services will operate between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Nagpur, while two others will run between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) and Nagpur.

Train No. 01125 will depart from CSMT at 3.25 p.m. on November 13 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. On its return journey, Train No. 01126 will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 14 and arrive at CSMT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The CSMT-Nagpur special will halt at Dadar, Thane, Kalyan, Igatpuri, Nashik Road, Chalisgaon, Jalgaon, Bhusaval, Malkapur, Shegaon, Akola, Badnera, Dhamangaon and Wardha.

Similarly, Train No. 01129 will depart from LTT at 3.25 p.m. on November 14 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. The return service, Train No. 01130, will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 15 and arrive at LTT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The LTT-Nagpur special will stop at the same stations as the CSMT service, except Dadar.
Both special trains will have AC, sleeper and general-class coaches.
The CSMT-Nagpur service will also include AC three-tier economy coaches.

Central Railway said bookings for the reserved coaches are open at computerised reservation centres and through the IRCTC website. Tickets for unreserved coaches can be booked through the UTS system or the RailOne app at normal charges.
Passengers can check detailed schedules and stoppage timings through the National Train Enquiry System website or mobile application.

articles.title: Gig and platform workers’ strike call in Hyderabad on November 14, plan major rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: TGPWU office-bearer Shaik Salauddin said on Thursday that Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to join the rally

Gig and platform workers have called for a strike in the city on November 14 to demand social security, workers’ rights, and welfare measures, according to the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers’ Union (TGPWU).

TGPWU office-bearer Shaik Salauddin said on Thursday that Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to join the rally with the union extending gratitude to him for “his advocacy and action for the welfare of gig and platform workers”, especially against the backdrop of the 2023 Bharat Jodo Yatra.

“The Telangana Gig and Platform Workers Act 2026 provides a vital legal framework for worker rights, centered on mandatory registration, social security benefits, a dedicated welfare board, and an effective grievance redressal mechanism. The state government has formulated the rules for implementing the Act, initiating steps to constitute the Welfare Board and launching a dedicated app to register workers and resolve grievances ,” Mr. Salauddin said.

articles.title: Andhra to bring in Investment Protection Act to ease doing business, says Naidu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 303 MoUs worth ₹9.89 lakh crore will be signed at the CII Partnership Summit, the Chief Minister says

Addressing the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 on Thursday (November 12, 2026), Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said Andhra Pradesh was working towards becoming a major manufacturing and technology hub in areas such as rare earth minerals, steel production, solar wafers, solar energy and battery energy storage.

He said that Asia’s first 120-qubit quantum computer in Amaravati would be inaugurated on February 3, 2027 and the Google Data Centre in Visakhapatnam on August 15, 2028, and that 303 MoUs involving proposed investments to the tune of ₹9.89 lakh crore would be signed at the ongoing summit. This would take the value of the investment proposals attracted by A.P. since June 2024 to ₹32.49 lakh crore, he said.

He stated that Asia’s first 120 qubit quantum computer in Amaravati would be inaugurated on February 3, 2027 and the Google Data Centre in Visakhapatnam on August 15, 2028, and that 303 MoUs involving proposed investments to the tune of ₹9.89 lakh crore would be signed at the ongoing Summit. With this, the value of the investment proposals attracted by A.P. reached ₹32.49 lakh crore since June 2024.

Emphasising the State’s commitment to speedy clearances, Mr. Naidu said A.P. was granting approvals at a speed that was unmatched by others and it was clear from the record time in which the government had facilitated the establishment of the Kia car manufacturing plant in Sri Sathya Sai district.

The grant of approvals to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft project which was also coming up in Sri Sathya Sai district was another shining example of the priority attached to speedy clearances. LG Electronics was preparing to commence production in Sri City within 19 months.

The Chief Minister outlined ambitious targets across key sectors: renewable energy 160 GW, annual electronics production ₹4.20 lakh crore, and aerospace and defence sector ₹50,000 crore. He observed that Amaravati was being developed as a blue-green capital city and it offered tremendous opportunities as it was poised to emerge as one of the most livable cities.

Highlighting the State’s strategic geographical advantage, Mr. Naidu said the State was emerging as a leading logistics destination with six operational ports, airports, high-speed rail connectivity and an extensive road network. Comprehensive plans were drawn up to ensure water availability for agriculture, drinking water and industrial requirements through interlinking of rivers, of which the Polavaram project was a major component.

The State government was committed to the Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 and a clear roadmap had been prepared for it, Mr. Naidu said, and called upon global investors, industrialists and technology leaders to partner with the State in realising that vision.

articles.title: The SIR exercise is also a technology failure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: When code changes but the user manuals have not yet been updated, the software becomes the rulebook

Much of the public argument over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of India’s electoral rolls is around law, power and politics. The autonomy of the Election Commission of India (ECI), the list of acceptable documents, and the burden placed on voters to prove eligibility are the key focus issues. There is, of course, no doubt that these questions matter. But a quieter, less spoken-about story runs underneath them. The 2025-26 SIR is the first revision of this scale to be run through a centralised digital platform, and the technology itself has become a source of exclusion. Viewed as a nationwide digital transformation project, the SIR fails on several counts that any student of technology would immediately recognise.

The irony stares right at us. India presents itself, with ample reasons to do so, as a leader in digital public infrastructure. From the IRCTC’s (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) ticketing system and the income tax department’s e-filing to Aadhaar authentication, UPI, DigiLocker etc., India holds up proof, at home and abroad, that it can build technology that works at scale.

articles.title: MHA declares Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation unlawful for another five years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the third time that the ban against IRF has been extended. The outfit was first banned in 2016
The Ministry of Home Affairs on Friday (November 13, 2026) declared Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) an unlawful association under UAPA for another five years.
This is the third time that the ban against IRF has been extended. The outfit was first banned in 2016 .

Further, the Central Government said it believes that if the unlawful activities of the IRF were not curbed and controlled immediately, the organisation would “take the opportunity to continue its subversive activities and re-organise its activists who are still absconding; disrupt the secular fabric of the country by polluting the minds of the people by creating communal disharmony; propagate anti-national sentiments; escalate secessionism by supporting militancy and undertake activities which are prejudicial to the sovereignty, integrity and security of the country,” according to a government notification.
File picture of Mumbai Police standing guard in front of the Islamic Research Foundation's (IRF) office in 2016 | Photo Credit: Vivek Bendre

The notification further said, “In exercise of the powers by Sub-sections (1) and (3) of Section 3 of the UAPA, 1967 (37 of 1967), the Central Government hereby declares the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) as an unlawful association and directs that this notification shall, subject to any order that may be made under Section 4 of the said Act, have effect for a period of five years from the date of its publication in the official Gazette.”
Naik, who is currently abroad, is being probed by the National Investigation Agency for alleged terror activities.

Naik was born in Mumbai, but he fled India in the wake of the July 1, 2016, bombing at a cafe in Dhaka, Bangladesh. He is accused of spreading hatred among different communities through his Peace TV and social media networks, where he has over 20 million followers.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the ₹2,50,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%

India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: COP31: Himalayan flash floods should push all to act ‘faster and fairer’ on climate change: UN climate chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year are a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be, particularly the Hindu Kush Himalayas,” UNFCCC Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said
The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year should push everyone to act "faster and fairer" on climate change, a top United Nations official said.

Responding to a question on the issue of the Himalayas on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya,Turkiye, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Executive Secretary Simon Stiell told PTI that transitioning away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner, along with tripling adaptation finance, are key to resolving the crisis.

“The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year are a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be, particularly the Hindu Kush Himalayas. For years, scientists and local communities have been warning that the Himalayas are at huge risk from climate change. What is happening in the Himalayas should push us to act faster and fairer on climate change,” he said.
Proposals by Nepal and Bhutan, and separately by Kyrgyzstan, to secure formal agenda items on mountain-related issues at the 31st UN failed to secure the backing of major negotiating blocs.
COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing

Highlighting that global heating is caused by humanity still burning huge amounts of coal, oil and gas and destroying forests, the UNFCCC Executive Secretary recalled COP28 in the UAE, where all countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner.

He stated that the agreement must be delivered in full, and that it is equally essential to make faster progress on helping nations adapt to climate impacts and build their resilience, especially vulnerable nations that did practically nothing to contribute to the climate crisis.

“That means delivering in full on the tripling of adaptation finance agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year. Full delivery on all existing financial commitments by developed economies is also essential, as is boosting access to finance for those who need it most, especially those vulnerable developing nations who did the least to cause the global crisis,” Mr. Stiell told PTI .

When asked how climate-vulnerable nations can trust a platform like COP given that the agenda on tripling adaptation finance failed to be formally adopted, he said that the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has been set up to provide support to vulnerable developing countries, adding that the crisis in the Himalayas shows why the COP process is critical.

“FRLD has been in its establishment phase; it has raised and received funds. The fund is now moving into delivery with an initial provisional allocation of $21.6 million for Nepal, which is a very positive step. It's essential that FRLD continues to be capitalised and deployed to the fullest extent possible,” Mr. Stiell said, adding that FRLD alone cannot meet the scale of loss and damage.
A standalone agenda item on tripling adaptation finance was not formally adopted on the official conference agenda, as consensus could not be reached during the opening plenary on November 9.

articles.title: U.S. lawmakers summon Nvidia former CEO after affair with suspected spy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was also called to testify before Senate Banking Committee

U.S. lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters.
“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote on Thursday (November 12, 2026) on X.
Mr. Scott said he was requesting mR. Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs.
Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's new interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s exit
Former Nvidia CEO Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say
Untangling Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s Chinese spy connection
It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena.

Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
U.S. intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations.
On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.

articles.title: Europe pushes for seat at Ukraine peace talks but lacks unified voice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukraine is eager for backup from its European allies, as it's reluctant to leave the talks solely in the hands of a U.S. administration that has often seemed to lean toward Moscow's views

European nations are seeking an envoy to represent them in talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war, concerned that a U.S.-backed process will leave them sidelined as Moscow and Washington decide the fate of a conflict that has roiled the continent.

Whether that should be one individual or more, and who it might be, is being debated as leaders from the 27-nation European Union meet Friday (November 13, 2026) at a summit in Dublin. Senior EU officials and politicians have been suggested, but there is not yet a consensus.

What the job might entail is also unclear and contested. But there is broad agreement among governments from the U.K. to Ukraine on the need for Europe to join the ongoing negotiations involving Moscow, Kyiv and Washington.

Ukraine is eager for backup from its European allies, as it's reluctant to leave the talks solely in the hands of a U.S. administration that has often seemed to lean toward Moscow's views. Russia does not want European countries involved in direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's military effort.
And the Europeans do not trust U.S. President Donald Trump to negotiate on their behalf after a series of tense standoffs over trade, Greenland and conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.
“Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine,” French President Emmanuel Macron said at the European Political Community meeting in Dublin. “There is no more U.S. support."
“At the end of the day, we will be the ones to define and decide for our future security as Europeans,” he said.

European leaders fear Russian President Vladimir Putin will press Mr. Trump to back a peace settlement that weakens not just Ukraine but broader European security. Putin has demanded that NATO troops be pulled back from Russia's borders and that no European forces be deployed in Ukraine.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham rejected the idea that Europe was being sidelined during peace negotiations, saying “there are European voices in the room.”

“All the leaders I've spoken to today are determined to put a bit of a ring of steel around Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as part of all of this to back him up to the hilt, and that's what we will do,” he said.
As envoys from Washington, Moscow and Kyiv met in Abu Dhabi, several European countries, including the U.K., France and Germany, attended discussions nearby.
Supporters of a single envoy, like Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, argue that their absence has let individual countries or small groups engage in freelance diplomacy.

articles.title: As election nears, Spain's Sanchez struggles to rally disillusioned left
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Interviews and ‌polls suggest that many potential supporters are too furious about the status quo and the perceived failings of Pedro Sanchez incumbent government to oblige

When Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election ​last month, he was betting that anger over housing and fear of the far right would rally all shades of the left behind his Socialists.
But interviews and ‌polls suggest that many potential supporters are too furious about the status quo and the perceived failings of his ​own incumbent government to oblige.

The eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in September and her subsequent death triggered protests against a ⁠housing crisis that culminated in a general strike which unions said brought more than 3 million onto the streets on Wednesday (November 12, 2026).
"Every generation has its own struggle — for us, that struggle is housing," Mr. Sanchez said at his first rally after calling the vote.
His challenge as he prepares to face the electorate on November 29 is ‌that the protests led by movements even further to his left have moved well beyond accommodation.
"We're really tired of so many things," said Maria Torrena Perez, a 40-year-old primary school teacher at a march in ‌Madrid on Wednesday (November 11, 2026)night.

"We need decent housing. We need a quality public education system. We need a decent healthcare system. Ultimately, they're not ‌investing ⁠in what they should be investing in. And we're fed up with the policies being implemented across the board."
Two deadly ⁠train crashes, corruption convictions in Mr. Sanchez's inner circle and a rush of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta have all taken their toll on Sanchez's support.
For all his campaigning, polls show backing for his party is still hovering around the 26%-29% level recorded before he called the election.

Without a shift in the next two weeks, an alliance between the ​conservative People's Party and far-right Vox, a hardline nationalist party ‌championing tighter borders and deregulation, is seen as the most likely next government.
Interviews with left-of-centre politicians, activists and voters suggested that for many, disillusionment with the status quo outweighs the urge to keep the far right out.

The "lesser evil" pitch of a centrist government standing between them and an ever-harder right is wearing thin, echoing discontent with incumbents that has spilled into social unrest across Europe in recent months.

At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days ‌of November, after 37 attacks in October, ​which was the highest monthly tally since the conflict ⁠began in late February, according ⁠to data from the Washington Institute for Near East ‌Policy.

fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
Microsoft said Thursday (November 13, 2026) that it was not aware of any “malicious activity” behind the hours-long disruption of its Outlook services.
“As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident. We will continue to treat this incident with urgency and priority until full resolution,” Microsoft said.

“For a city whose economy runs on serving global clients, [the outage] is no minor inconvenience,” Sambratha Shetty, Chief Operating Officer (COO), Synergia Foundation, said. “Bengaluru’s IT firms, startups and global capability centres coordinate across time zones through email, Teams calls and shared files. When those stop, client deliveries slip, support queues pile up, and teams sit idle. For outsourcing contracts bound by strict service-level agreements, even a few hours of downtime can mean penalties and strained client trust.”

“Bengaluru’s tech leaders should treat cloud failure as certain, not hypothetical. That means backup communication channels, multi-vendor setups and regularly tested continuity plans. The city that builds resilient systems for the world must build them for itself,” the COO said.
Downdetector said that Microsoft’s outage reports on November 12 reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour, in a post on X.
“Reports about Microsoft 365, Copilot, Teams and OneDrive each rose more than a hundredfold, and Azure about a hundredfold. Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also Microsoft’s, rose far less,” the post said.
“We are closely monitoring the ongoing Microsoft outage,” Air India posted on X. “Our flight operations remain unaffected.”
Cartier-owner Richemont’s first half results ⁠announcement, due ‌at ‌0600GMT, ‌has been ⁠delayed ⁠due to the global ‌disruption of Microsoft services, the ‌luxury company said ⁠on Friday.
It ‌is unclear when the ‌issue will be resolved, ⁠Richemont said.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” IndiGo airlines posted on X.

articles.title: EU leaders seek to tackle challenges at first ever AI summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The meeting comes amid mounting ⁠worries about a technology that promises to transform industries and societies but in recent months has caused alarm after a series of incidents involving rogue ‌AI agents

European Union leaders gather in Dublin on Friday (November 13, 2026) for their first ​ever summit on Artificial Intelligence (AI), to debate how the bloc can catch ‌up with the United States and China and tackle ​funding issues and other problems.

The meeting comes amid mounting ⁠worries about a technology that promises to transform industries and societies but in recent months has caused alarm after a series of incidents involving rogue ‌AI agents. There was further turmoil this week with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , leaving the industry ‌without its biggest champion.
Leaders in Dublin will also ‌assess ⁠how to overcome other problems such as red tape and ⁠set guardrails.

“Given the rapid pace of AI development, I believe that a first dedicated discussion, at leaders’ level, is now needed on the opportunities presented by ​AI, as well as ‌on its transformative effect on our economies and societies,” European Council President Antonio Costa wrote in an invitation letter to EU leaders last week.
Mistral AI chief executive Arthur Mensch and Nobel Prize-winning ‌AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton will brief EU leaders.

Europe will ​have to ramp up its efforts if it is to be an AI player. An initiative known ⁠as the Chips Act, implemented three years ago looks likely to fall short of its goal to attract advanced manufacturing and double the ‌bloc’s share of the global chip market to 20% by 2030.

A plan to build seven AI gigafactories to house advanced AI processors, software, cloud technology, high-speed connectivity and data centres under one roof has yet to fully take off due to the fight among EU countries over spending on competitiveness in the ‌bloc’s 2028-2034 budget.

In addition to AI, leaders are also set to discuss ​Ukraine, which has since been added as a second major topic to the agenda, a day after U.S. ⁠envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner flew into Dublin to meet Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskiy following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
EU leaders are likely to discuss European ‌involvement in peace negotiations and potential security guarantees the EU could offer in the event of a ceasefire, a senior EU ​official said.

articles.title: Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's new interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A 13-year Nvidia veteran, Colette Kress will lead the chipmaker whose processors power cutting-edge AI data centers and supercomputers, as the board weighs a longer-term successor.

Nvidia co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (November 13, 2026), following reports of two extramarital affairs, one involving an Nvidia executive who reported to him and another involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. While Mr. Huang apologised for being unfaithful and Nvidia investigates whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence, the chipmaker’s shares have tumbled more than 30% from their October peak.

In a bid to reclaim control, Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, will assume the role of interim CEO, taking over from Mr. Huang, the company announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026). This will put her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors ​power the world’s most advanced supercomputers and AI data centers.

Ms. Kress is far from an outsider to the $4 trillion AI mammoth in the artificial intelligence industry. She joined Nvidia in September 2013 ​as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. ​She has appeared alongside Mr. Huang on the company’s quarterly earnings calls. Prior to joining Nvidia, Ms. Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.
Nvidia’s ⁠revenue was $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined and $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026.

Before Nvidia, Ms. Kress spent nearly 25 years building her career at some of the tech sector’s biggest giants. She started out with an eight-year stint in finance roles at Texas Instruments before moving to Microsoft, where she worked from 1997 to 2010 and became CFO of the server amd Tools division.

She moved to Cisco (CSCO.O) in 2010 as senior vice president ​and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation, where she was ​responsible for financial strategy and business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013, eventhough Nvidia was the smallest company she had ever worked for.
She holds a bachelor’s degree finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Nvidia’s stock rise over the past decade made Ms. Kress one fo the wealthiest executives in the world. Forbes ranked her No. 32 on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. At the stock’s October peak, her Nvidia holdings pushed her personal net worth past $1 billion, though the recent market slide reduced her company shares to roughly $750 million. She was awarded a pay package worth $14 million for Nvidia’s fiscal 2026, according to Nvidia’s proxy statement. This also includes restricted stock units.

Executive officers at Nvidia are employed at will and have no ​individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company’s proxy ​statement. Nvidia ⁠has said in earlier filings that many of its peer companies offer such agreements.
In a statement on Thursday, Ms. Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she would build on the “extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
Nvidia hasn't provided any notable new updates in its internal review. Moreover, the company didn’t address either of Mr. Huang’s relationships in its Thursday announcement.
Market watchers believe the board may still look externally for a permanent succesort t lrad the AI linchpin forward.

articles.title: What are the findings of the 2024 Hindu Kush Himalayas snow update? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What does the report by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development highlight? How important is snow persistence? How much of a role does climate change play in river basins receiving low levels of snowmelt this year?

T he Ganga river basin — India’s largest — reached a record low snow persistence in 2024, the Hindu Kush Himalaya snow update of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has reported. The Brahmaputra and the Indus basins have suffered similarly, threatening water supply to millions of people. “Tragically this is yet another postcard from the frontlines of a climate crisis that is accelerating even beyond scientists’ projections and causing huge challenges in one of the most populated regions of the world,” Miriam Jackson, Cryosphere Lead at ICIMOD and a contributor to reports of the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, told The Hindu .

Snow persistence is the fraction of time snow is on the ground. When this snow melts, it provides water to people and ecosystems. In the river basins of the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH), snowmelt is the biggest source of water in the streams. Overall, it contributes 23% of the runoff to the region’s 12 major river basins every year. The HKH mountains extend around 3,500 km over eight countries — Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, Myanmar, and Pakistan. These mountains are also called the “water towers of Asia” because they are the origins of 10 crucial river systems on the continent — Amu Darya, Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, Irrawaddy, Salween, Mekong, Yangtse, Yellow river, and Tarim. These river basins provide water to almost one-fourth of the world’s population and are a significant freshwater source for 240 million people in the HKH region.

The authors of the 2024 HKH snow update analysed data from 2003 to 2024 and found significant fluctuations in snow persistence between November and April every year, when snow accumulates above ground. Based on this, they made grim predictions of lasting impact on the people in the region as well as those downstream of the river basins.

In India, snow persistence in the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus river basins dropped significantly in 2024. The Ganga river basin noted its lowest snow persistence in 22 years, 17% below the long-term historical average (also known as ‘normal’). The previous holder of this dubious distinction was 2018, when it was 15.2% below normal. In 2015, on the other hand, snow persistence was 25.6% above normal.

Similarly, snow persistence in the Brahmaputra basin was 14.6% below normal in 2024. It was worse in 2021, when the average persistence was 15.5% below normal. In the Indus river basin, snow persistence fell 23.3% below normal this year although this was offset by excesses in parts of the lower altitudes.

Outside India, the basin of the Amu Darya river — which flows through Central Asia — recorded its lowest snow persistence in 2024: 28.2% below normal. The figure for the Helmand river, an important source of drinking water for Iran and Afghanistan, was almost 32% below normal in 2024, beating a record set in 2018. Persistence in the part where the Mekong river originates in the Himalaya was only slightly below normal this time. (This river’s delta is Vietnam’s “rice bowl”.)
The primary reason for the lower persistence in 2024 was weak western disturbances, ICIMOD remote sensing specialist and author of the report Sher Muhammad told The Hindu .

“Due to changing climate and global warming, this pattern is becoming increasingly unstable. Although the exact mechanisms are not fully understood, global warming is thought to exacerbate prolonged and intense La Niña–El Niño conditions. These phases of a recurring climate pattern across the tropical Pacific Ocean significantly influence global weather patterns, including western disturbances,” he added.

Western disturbances are low-pressure systems that originate over the Mediterranean Sea, the Caspian, and the Black Seas and bring rain and snow to the HKH region in winter. “The region where these storms originate experienced persistently high sea-surface temperatures,” Mr. Muhammad explained. “This disruption weakened and delayed the arrival of the western disturbance, resulting in reduced winter precipitation and snowfall in the HKH region. The pattern of high temperatures and altered weather systems explains both the record low snow persistence in 2024 and similar historical records.”

“We have warned for years that the 1.5 degrees Celsius limit that governments signed up to in the Paris Agreement is not ambitious enough to protect the snow and ice, people and nature of the Hindu Kush Himalayas because the target is a global average, and the real temperature increase will be far higher here,” Ms. Jackson added.

The persistence of snow in China’s Yellow River basin exceeded the normal value by 20.2% in 2024. “The Yellow river basin is an area where the East Asian winter monsoon brings cold, dry air from Siberia and Mongolia,” Mr. Muhammad said. “When this cold air mass interacts with moist air from other regions, particularly the Pacific Ocean, it can result in snowfall over the higher altitudes of the upper Yellow River basin.”

“When the cold air from the east Asian winter monsoon systems interacts with moist air masses from the Pacific Ocean, it can result in snowfall at higher elevations in the eastern Himalaya,” Mr. Muhammad added.

articles.title: Jewellery and souvenir made from plastic discarded in the Himalayas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Plastic bottle caps left by climbers in the Himalayas are repurposed by Moware into mini Himalayan models, rocks of Himalayas, jewellery, and more

Have you ever wondered what happens to discarded plastic bottle caps? At best, they transform into wheels in DIY toy projects; or so we think. In Nepal, they are recycled into souvenirs, jewellery and everyday utility items by Nepal-based Moware. This design intervention enterprise Eva Villardon Grande gives a new meaning to waste left behind in the Himalayas.

Launched in 2013, Moware which stands for ‘Mountain Waste Repurpose’, employs innovative ways to reduce our footprint by upcycling and creatively transforming waste into useful products. The initiative was kickstarted to promote paper waste management in offices, even as it generated employment for low-income women from Lalitpur, Kathmandu. Over the years, they diversified, experimenting extensively with waste aluminium, wrappers, and glass bottles.
The Himalayan stones - Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Among their collectables, the most talked about is the From the Himalayas collection including a miniature model of the mountains that shows its most iconic peaks — Shartse, Lhotse, Mount Everest, Nuptse, Changtise Peak, Khumbutse Peak, and Mount Lingtren. The collection also includes ornamental rocks, jewellery and candle stand, all made from plastic bottle caps discarded by trekkers in the Himalayas.
Plastic bottle caps at Moware’s workshop | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

The glass in the collection are made from recycled alcohol bottles that are left behind by tourists. These are collected from hotels by Waste management companies. Moware sources these and turns them into utility items. An average trekker uses approximately 38 water bottles during the climb. Moware decided to see what could be done with the plastic instead of sending it to landfills, or having it incinerated. Towards this end, they set out to collaborate with two like-minded waste product resource management companies, Blue Waste and Sagarmatha Next., based out of Nepal, to find a solution.

Carry Me Back was the first initiative of Sagarmatha Next to address the waste management challenge in the Sagarmatha National Park and the Khumbu region (Nepalese side of Mount Everest). When the pilot project of the crowdsourced waste removal system was initiated in 2019, 2,500 tourists transported about 4,000 kilograms of waste. The waste is segregated, packed in specially made bags and left at a pick-up station located by the stupa in Namche Bazaar.
Eva and her team members at Moware | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Why bottle caps? Eva explains, “While a plastic bottle without the cap may have a lot of takers, the plastic cap itself — made from High-Density Polyethylene (HDP) — finds no takers, so they eventually end up in landfills.”

Moware then collaborated with Pim and Luc of Super Local, a team of Dutch designers based in Nepal. The duo devoted themselves to reducing waste and creating sustainable products hand-in-hand with local communities. “After a few months of brainstorming, they devised the Himalayan model design and Himalayan stones. The Himalayan stone are assortment of three mani stones — Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La. These stones represent the awe-inspiring three passes of the Khumbu region. We just loved it and saw a beautiful chance to give the caps a new life,” says Eva who has made Nepal her home for now, to work on similar projects.

Why Himalayan stones? Eva continued, “We discovered trekkers and hikers pick stones as reminder of the trip when they visit the Everest. Many do not know that this is forbidden. This is how we decided on assortment of three mani stones — Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La. They are made of 8, 10 and 16 bottle caps respectively.”

“With the help from our sister concern Sagarmatha Next (the first project of Himalayan Museum and Sustainability Park) we have collected and transformed 60,000 kilograms of waste generated in Kathmandu Valley and the Khumbu region,” she explains, adding that about 5,40,000 tonnes of solid waste are generated every year in Nepal. “Despite the efforts made to improve waste management practices, the country lacks a formal system for reusing and recycling. Consequently, many valuable resources are thrown away without recovery and treatment,” says Eva.

fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

articles.title: Theatre personality Prasanna resigns from special cell to promote rural industries in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter to Karnataka’s Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Prasanna highlighted closure of the Handloom Development Corporation and demolition of the Gandhi Ashram of the Badanavalu Khadi Kendra

Noted theatre personality Prasanna , who is also the founder of Charaka Multipurpose Industrial Co-operative Society, has resigned as head of the Mahatma Gandhi Vastrodyama Kosha, a special cell under the Department of Textiles and Handloom of Karnataka, which was set up to promote Gandhi-inspired rural industries. He cited recent developments concerning rural institutions.

In a letter to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar dated November 12, Mr. Prasanna said he was hurt by what he described as a series of setbacks to the rural development sector at a time when villagers were migrating to cities.

At Heggodu in Sagar taluk, he said, officials demolished a pedestal built to mark the dedication of a tank rejuvenated by Charaka, and the organisation was ‘unnecessarily accused of encroaching on the tank’. The tank had been dedicated by local MLA Belur Gopalakrishna after Ganga Pooja.

At Badanavalu in Mysuru district, he said, officials demolished the Gandhi Ashram of the Badanavalu Khadi Kendra about two months ago, against a Gram Sabha decision. He also said the government of Karnataka had closed the Handloom Development Corporation.

He told The Hindu that the Constitution envisaged village administration being carried out at the village level. Gram Sabhas were intended to function on par with legislative assemblies, and this principle had been recognised in the Constitution itself. However, it was not being implemented in letter and spirit, he said.

He was also upset that gram panchayat employees and officers were being treated as servants by tahsildars, deputy commissioners and ministers. Their opinions were neither sought nor respected, and the views of people living in the respective areas were not given due consideration.

Mr. Prasanna said the cell was conceived after then chief minister Siddaramaiah announced it in his Budget (2023-24) with a grant of ₹1 crore. It was to be a Section 8 company (under the Companies Act), with 51% of the shares held by participating institutions and 49% by the State Government. He said there had been no progress since then.
He said he would go on a hunger strike if the Chief Minister did not respond positively to the concerns raised in his resignation letter.

articles.title: Attack on CRPF post: Several suspects picked up for questioning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Immediately after the attack, security forces launched a massive cordon and search operation in the area to track down the terrorists
Several suspects have been picked up for questioning in the aftermath of the Kulgam attack in which three CRPF personnel were injured, officials said on Friday (November 13, 2026).
Terrorists opened fire at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) post in the South Kashmir district on Wednesday (November 11).
Immediately after the attack, security forces launched a massive cordon and search operation in the area to track down the terrorists.
The search operation continued on the third day, on Friday (November 13). The forces have erected barricades and deployed armoured vehicles at several places in the district.
Checking and frisking of vehicles is being undertaken at the security check-points as a tight vigil is being maintained, they added.
The security agencies are using human and technical intelligence to aid the operation, the officials said.
They said several suspects have been picked up for questioning by the police.
Senior officers of the police and other security agencies have visited the spot of the attack and reviewed security measures, the officials said.
Security has also been beefed up elsewhere in the valley as police and paramilitary forces conducted random searches of vehicles in Srinagar city and other districts of Kashmir.

articles.title: Civil society group urges Government to delink welfare benefits from electoral roll status
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens for Fraternity Forum urged the Government to issue a clear public assurance that electoral-roll status will not become a condition for receiving welfare benefits and that adequate safeguards will be established to prevent the exclusion of eligible beneficiaries

A civil society group has written to Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh over his reported remarks that voter ID will replace Aadhaar for identifying beneficiaries of social welfare programmes, urging the Government to assure the public that electoral-roll status will not become a condition for receiving welfare benefits.

Citizens for Fraternity Forum (CFF-Bharat) said it welcomed measures to improve transparency and accountability and prevent the misuse of public welfare schemes, but sought clarification on the use of EPIC/Voter ID and biometric authentication in beneficiary-related processes.

"We strongly believe that no eligible citizen should be denied welfare benefits merely because they do not possess a voter ID, their name is not included in the electoral rolls, or biometric authentication fails," the letter said.
The letter dated November 12 was signed by former Delhi Lieutenant Governor Najeeb Jung, ex-AMU vice chancellor Zameer Uddin Shah and former diplomat Ashok Kumar Sharma, among others.

"Welfare entitlements must remain linked to the eligibility criteria of the respective schemes. Accessible alternative methods of identification and effective grievance-redressal mechanisms must be ensured, particularly for elderly persons, women, persons with disabilities, migrants and other vulnerable citizens," it said

The group urged the Government to issue a clear public assurance that electoral-roll status will not become a condition for receiving welfare benefits and that adequate safeguards will be established to prevent the exclusion of eligible beneficiaries.

Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lallan Singh had reportedly said that access to financial benefits and welfare payments under schemes of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj will now require an Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number along with mandatory biometric authentication.

articles.title: CPI(M) to boost its legal cell in Keralam to counter ‘fake news, misinformation’ targeting party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though CPI(M) already has a legal cell, it feels the need to further strengthen its activities considering 'the volume of misinformation being spread against the party' in recent times, says a party leader

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has decided to step up the activities of its legal cell in Keralam to counter what it perceives as fake news and targeted spreading of misinformation in social media platforms and public forums to discredit the party and its leaders.

A senior CPI(M) leader, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told The Hindu that though the party already has a legal cell, it felt the need to further strengthen its activities considering “the volume of misinformation being spread against the party” in recent times.

“Till now, we used to ignore many of these attempts to spread fake news and misinformation targeting the party. However, now we have decided that legal action has to be taken in all instances where it warrants one because there is such a constant flow of misinformation against the party on a daily basis these days,” said the leader.
The legal cell will have the active participation of senior High Court advocates as well as left lawyers’ collectives formed in all districts.

The extended Kerala State Committee meeting of the CPI(M) in September this year had discussed the issue and suggested corrective measures. Speaking at the meeting, CPI(M) General Secretary M.A. Baby had said that the “deliberate creation of a false perception against Left democratic forces” among the masses had played a key role in the reverses suffered by the party in Keralam in recent times. He also admitted that the Left should have been more alert in responding to the construction of this false perception.

Earlier this year, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan had also come out strongly against a section of “corporate-controlled right-wing media”, accusing them of spreading false narratives and fake news to undermine the party as well as to scuttle the corrective measures being initiated within it following the Assembly election defeat.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Microsoft outage enters second day; company says not aware of malicious activity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

“When essential tools become unavailable, employees naturally look for ways to keep working,” Ben Mudie, field CTO of APAC Tenable, said. “The security risk is that temporary workarounds, such as personal email accounts or unapproved file-sharing services, can move sensitive business information beyond an organisation’s visibility and control. Disruption can also create opportunities for impersonation. An urgent request arriving through an unfamiliar channel, or a message offering to restore access, deserves extra scrutiny.”
He said that an outage alone does not establish that a cyberattack has occurred.

“But it does underline why business continuity and cybersecurity need to work together. Employees need clear, approved alternatives so they can remain productive without exposing company data or bypassing security checks,” he said.

“We’re seeing positive results for service stability and increased capacity as a result of our latest traffic optimization actions. We’re implementing these actions more broadly across affected regions as we seek to attain persistent recovery. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, as well as http://status.cloud.microsoft if the admin centre is not available to you,” the company said in a statement.

From Asia to the U.S., Microsoft’s outage involving services like Outlook and Teams has dragged on for hours and impacted many users, companies and some government operations as the technology giant struggled with fixing the issue.
More than 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook earlier on Thursday although new reports have since fallen from that peak.
Singapore’s Government Technology Agency said that government emails were down and that the agency is working with Microsoft to resolve the issue.
The Philippines’ Supreme Court said in a statement on X that the ongoing Microsoft 365 service outage has affected some of its operations, including email responses.
In Japan, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki said the outage impacted the government’s IT infrastructure and that they were “keeping a close eye on the developments.”

Microsoft’s workplace services, including Outlook and Teams, remained disrupted for users in India and elsewhere on Friday (November 13, 2026), a day after a global outage began, with the company saying it was still working to pinpoint the cause and is not aware of any malicious activity behind it.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV denounces ‘machismo,’ demands women be protected in emotional return to Peru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pope Leo called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice

Pope Leo XIV on Thursday (November 12, 2026) denounced widespread “machismo” and violence against women in Peru, demanding that women be protected and respected as he set out marching orders for his beloved Peruvian church and people.
After his emotional homecoming Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Peruvian Pope got down to business and turned to the challenges facing a church and country he knows well.

He called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice. He also met with six survivors, including from an abusive sect-like group that Pope Francis suppressed last year.
Pope meets survivors of clergy abuse in Argentina as it reckons with legacy and ongoing cases
Pope Leo’s Argentina visit brings renewed scrutiny of clergy abuse scandals
But the 71-year-old Pope also showed himself to be positively overjoyed to be home and as relaxed as he has been in public since his 2025 election.

The Pope sang along enthusiastically as 40,000 people in Lima's Plaza Mayor serenaded him with “Contigo Peru,” a famous song from Peru's Pacific coast that celebrates national unity. He sang along later to another hymn, Alma Misionera (Missionary Soul), in Lima's stadium during a vigil along with 60,000 people inside and another 300,000 outside, according to Vatican estimates.
How can Pope Leo vote in U.S. elections while serving as the sovereign of Vatican City? | Explained

“It's a blessing not only for us Chiclayans but for all of Peru,” said Angel Esquives, a craftsman originally from Pope Leo's former diocese in Chiclayo who now lives in Lima. He said he left his home at 3 a.m. local time to go to the historic centre and stand in line to get as close as possible to the Pope.

Zozimo Perez came in a self-designed costume he named “the Inca Warrior,” with the pontiff's image on his chest and back. He was in tears as he saw Pope Leo stroll around the square. “This is a gift from heaven,” he said.

As he showed in the first two legs of his South American trip, the Pope was in fine form despite having undergone lung cancer surgery last month . He bounded up a steep flight of stairs Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning without any apparent problems and joked with the bishops that some “doubting Thomases” had predicted he wouldn't be able to come.
“But God is great and his grace is bigger than all of us and I'm very happy to be here with you,” he said to applause.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay must be wary of ‘untrustworthy’ ally Congress: BJP leader Ram Madhav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party,” the BJP leader said, referring to the Congress

BJP national vice-president Ram Madhav on Friday (November 13, 2026) extended a word of caution to TVK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay regarding his ally, the Congress, saying it was the “most untrustworthy party” and that Mr. Vijay must “be careful.”

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Madhav said: “The leadership here [in Tamil Nadu] must remember that you are patronising a party, which is a party of anarchy, which is a party of liars. They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party.”

The people and politicians of Tamil Nadu were aware of the “untrustworthiness” of the Congress, Mr. Madhav said and added that DMK president M.K. Stalin “got to know about the Congress” six months ago and how “foolish” it was to depend on the party.

“Mr. Vijay also will get to know. He probably has some happiness now. All that is there. But, he must be careful... [if and when they see] greener pastures, they [the Congress] will immediately jump. Because they don’t have anything of their own. So, they will always survive on other parties.”

Mr. Madhav further said the people of Tamil Nadu have not forgotten what happened to veteran Congress leader and former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj of the Congress. The BJP leader said Kamaraj was instrumental in the bringing former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi to prominence, but she eventually “threw him out.”

Although the Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi were trying to make it look as though the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was the target of the [ongoing] protests [in New Delhi and elsewhere in the country], Mr. Madhav contended that the “real target is Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” by propagating that elections were conducted in “wrongful manner.”

Replying to a query about the BJP’s advice to the TVK government about its alliance with the Congress, Mr. Madhav said: “The TVK is our adversary. We don’t give any advice. We will fight them politically.”

BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran reiterated there was “no difference between the [erstwhile] DMK government and the TVK government now”, pointing to the incidents of murder, dacoity, and rape in the State.

Referring to an issue allegedly involving TVK MLA and a District Collector , Mr. Nagenthran questioned: “If the Chief Minister is maintaining silence even for an issue like this, then for what will he speak out for?” Pointing to the Children’s Day celebrations organised by the TVK government, Mr. Nagenthran said: “Only his [Mr. Vijay] photograph is being publicised. How is it justified?”

articles.title: CM Vijay inaugurates distribution of cakes, greeting cards and sweet pongal to children
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Initiative marks Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14

Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (November 13, 2026) inaugurated the distribution of cakes and greeting cards to children studying in government and government-aided schools, and sweet pongal to children attending anganwadi centres to mark Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14.

As many as 61,84,566 beneficiaries, comprising students, teachers and non-teaching staff of government and government-aided primary, middle, high and higher secondary schools, received the cakes at a total cost of ₹9.27 crore. Sweet pongal was distributed to 11,11,022 children aged between two and six, who are receiving pre-school education at anganwadi centres across the State.

An official press release said Mr. Vijay visited the Chennai Middle School in his Assembly constituency of Perambur and distributed cakes and greeting cards to 537 students (from LKG to Class VIII), and sweet pongal to 40 children attending anganwadi centres functioning within the premises. He also interacted with the students and the staff.

In Mayiladuthurai, Salem, Thanjavur, Madurai, Tiruvannamalai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, the Nilgiris, Erode, Namakkal, and Karur, students were provided two packets of cake each, weighing 45 grams. In the remaining districts, each student received a 45-gram packet of cake.

The distribution was carried out in coordination with the Chief Educational Officers, District Educational Officers, Block Educational Officers and Regional Managers of the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation. The quality of the cakes was assessed by the Food Safety Department before they were distributed to schools.

Mr. Vijay was accompanied by Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity A. Rajmohan, Minister for Social Welfare and Women Empowerment K. Jagadeeswari, Minister for Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Srinath, MLAs M.R. Pallavi and Revanth Charan, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, IAS officers and other officials.
