articles.title: Telangana approves 2,000 affordable houses for auto-rickshaw workers in & around Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu

Telangana government approved a proposal for taking up an affordable housing scheme exclusively for auto-rickshaw workers, in four areas in and around Hyderabad, on the lines of affordable flats at Indiramma Housing towers in Core Urban Region Economy (CURE).

Permission was given for construction of a total of 2,000 Economically Weaker Section (EWS) houses, with 500 each in Bandlaguda (LIG Colony) in Nagole; Gandamguda; Petbasheerbad and Jalpally or Laxmiguda. The societies would be titled ‘Auto Nagar Colony’, as per a government order (G.O.) issued on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The State Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, reservation provisions, selection and allotment procedures and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu , with a specific condition that the beneficiaries shall be auto-rickshaw workers.

The Board would take up the scheme with an indicative project cost of ₹22 crore. It was directed to submit necessary detailed project reports and finance proposals after verification of land availability, site suitability and technical feasibility.

The State Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said the project would be implemented through the Telangana Housing Board, with four housing complexes coming up at an estimated cost of ₹220 crore.

Mr. Reddy said the Housing Board had been directed to examine land availability, technical requirements and geographical suitability at the proposed locations and prepare detailed project reports (DPRs) along with financial proposals. The government would expedite the process to ensure that eligible auto-rickshaw workers could get houses at the earliest.

The Minister said the government was committed to providing housing security to every eligible poor family in the State. Under the Indiramma housing scheme, the government was extending financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to eligible poor families for construction of houses.

Describing a house as a source of dignity, financial security and confidence in the future for poor families, he said the Auto Nagar initiative was part of the government’s efforts to address the housing needs of specific occupational groups.
The government would continue its efforts until every eligible poor family in the State has a house, he said.

articles.title: India's Paytm gets preliminary RBI nod for wallet licence; shares hit record high
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, says company

India’s Paytm ​on Friday (November 13, 2026) received preliminary central ‌bank approval for its payments ​services unit to ⁠issue prepaid payment products, including digital wallets, sending its ‌shares to a record high of 1,960 ‌rupees.
Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, the company said in a filing.
The unit can offer these services ‌to customers after receiving ​the RBI’s final authorisation.

The approval comes ⁠more than two years after the RBI barred Paytm ‌Payments Bank from accepting fresh deposits and wallet top-ups over persistent regulatory non-compliance and supervisory concerns, effectively halting its ‌normal wallet operations.
Earlier, this year ​the RBI cancelled the banking licence issued to ⁠Paytm Payments Bank.
The latest ⁠approval allows Paytm’s wholly owned subsidiary to ‌move towards restarting wallet services.

articles.title: Modi in Mysuru: COSMOS Planetarium a new chapter in India’s scientific journey, says PM | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: PM Modi to address students who have arrived to witness the inauguration of COSMOS LED Dome Planetarium

The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.
Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.

India has seen many great astronomers, such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technology we have today did not exist back then. Despite this, they made major discoveries and carried out difficult calculations, said PM Modi after inaugurating the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru.

The facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels and 4.2 crore individual LEDs. It includes a Sky Theatre, exhibition halls, an astronomy museum and training facilities, with the aim of promoting astronomy education and public outreach.
As India achieves one scientific breakthrough after another, Mysuru is also adding a new chapter to India’s scientific journey with this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, he added.
Our government opened up the space sector. This has created new opportunities for the private sector. India’s startups have also been given an opportunity to showcase their potential.

Underscoring Karnataka’s contribution to India’s space programme, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the country’s space journey was incomplete without the State’s contributions, from Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, to Chandrayaan, Aditya-L1 and the ambitious Gaganyaan mission.
Recalling the contributions of the Mysore Maharajas to scientific development, the CM cited their vision that had resulted in the establishment of top institutions including the IISc.

Karnataka government is ready to support the Centre in establishment of new centres of excellence. We are ready to support and encourage young minds and develop skills to our engineering graduates, Mr. Shivakumar said.

Seeking PM’s support in bringing the Mekedatu project to life, Mr. Shivakumar also reiterated the State’s concerns over the Kasturirangan Committee report on the ecologically sensitive areas of the Western Ghats.

Raising concerns over primary education and migration to urban centres, the Chief Minister said economic migration for education and employment was leading to a significant shift in population patterns.

To address this challenge, he requested the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to issue advisories aligning corporate CSR initiatives with Karnataka’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CCSR) Guidelines. This, he said, would help upgrade 1,000 government schools into Karnataka Public Schools and strengthen the public education system.

articles.title: Special Summary Revision draft roll records 5.26 crore voters in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajasthan has more than 5.26 crore voters as per the draft electoral roll published following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, according to figures released by the state election department.
The draft roll, published on Thursday (November 12, 2026), contains names of more than 5.26 crore voters -- with over 2.75 crore men, 2.51 crore women and 584 transgender voters.
The State election office on February 21 published the final roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), recording the names of more than 5.15 crore voters.

The two published figures show a numerical difference of 11.47 lakh. However, the SIR figure covered 199 Assembly constituencies, excluding Anta, while the latest draft has been released as a statewide total.
Rajasthan Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan said SSR 2027 is being conducted according to the Election Commission's schedule, keeping January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligibility.

According to the schedule, voters can submit claims and objections from November 12 to December 11. Electoral registration officers will dispose of the applications by December 28, and the final roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
Ms. Mahajan urged voters to check their names in the draft roll and submit applications if their names are missing or any corrections are required.

The department said copies of the draft roll have been provided free of cost to recognised political parties during meetings convened by electoral registration officers across assembly constituencies.
Political parties were given soft copies of the roll without photographs and hard copies for verification.
Voters can check their names on the election department's website or contact booth-level officers, who have been provided booth-wise copies of the draft roll.

During the claims and objections period, applications received will be compiled every week and displayed outside the offices of the electoral registration officers. The lists will also be uploaded on the department's website and shared with recognised political parties.
The department said Form 6 can be submitted for inclusion of names, Form 7 for objections to inclusion or deletion of names and Form 8 for corrections in electoral entries.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 13 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Special Summary Revision draft roll records 5.26 crore voters in Rajasthan

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Rajasthan has more than 5.26 crore voters as per the draft electoral roll published following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, according to figures released by the state election department.

The draft roll, published on Thursday (November 12, 2026), contains names of more than 5.26 crore voters -- with over 2.75 crore men, 2.51 crore women and 584 transgender voters.

The State election office on February 21 published the final roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), recording the names of more than 5.15 crore voters.

The two published figures show a numerical difference of 11.47 lakh. However, the SIR figure covered 199 Assembly constituencies, excluding Anta, while the latest draft has been released as a statewide total.

Rajasthan Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan said SSR 2027 is being conducted according to the Election Commission's schedule, keeping January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligibility.

According to the schedule, voters can submit claims and objections from November 12 to December 11. Electoral registration officers will dispose of the applications by December 28, and the final roll will be published on January 4, 2027.

Ms. Mahajan urged voters to check their names in the draft roll and submit applications if their names are missing or any corrections are required.

The department said copies of the draft roll have been provided free of cost to recognised political parties during meetings convened by electoral registration officers across assembly constituencies.

Political parties were given soft copies of the roll without photographs and hard copies for verification.

Voters can check their names on the election department's website or contact booth-level officers, who have been provided booth-wise copies of the draft roll.

During the claims and objections period, applications received will be compiled every week and displayed outside the offices of the electoral registration officers. The lists will also be uploaded on the department's website and shared with recognised political parties.

The department said Form 6 can be submitted for inclusion of names, Form 7 for objections to inclusion or deletion of names and Form 8 for corrections in electoral entries.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Chinese company linked to Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips: report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Alice Huang, mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub

A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang , the alleged spy for Beijing at the centre of the scandal surrounding Nvidia , obtained banned AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Friday (November 13, 2026).
Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to having extramarital affairs, including one reportedly with Alice Huang. China denies that she is a spy.
The scandal has raised concerns that high-end Nvidia microchips might have found their way to China, the United States' main AI rival, in circumvention of Washington's export restrictions.
Alice Huang is mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company that has drawn scrutiny over allegedly steering Nvidia chips to China.
However, she also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub.

Bloomberg reported, citing an unnamed source, that Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia partner headquartered in Singapore, purchased servers containing Nvidia's H800 chips from Dell Technologies.
Those servers later ended up in the hands of Shanghai Longteng, the financial news outlet said, citing documents submitted to the Chinese government.
It was not clear how the hardware was obtained or whether Alice Huang was involved in the deal, according to Bloomberg .
The United States banned the export of H800 chips to China in 2023, part of an effort to slow the development of AI technology by Beijing.

Megaspeed said on Thursday it was investigating whether it had complied with export controls on sensitive microchips. Malaysia has said it is probing a Megaspeed subsidiary over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.
Few public details are available about Ms. Huang, also known as Huang Le. She reportedly held a senior position at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Microsoft extends mail timeout to 48 hours as outage hits governments, organisations worldwide
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.
Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. It said the focus was now on extending recovery across affected infrastructure in other regions.

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.
Citing Germany’s approach, FOSS United CEO Poruri said the country had allowed individual regions to choose their email service providers, many of which use established free and open-source software.

India should adopt a similar approach instead of relying on a single provider, he said. Referring to the migration of government email services from the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to Zoho, he cautioned against replacing dependence on one provider with dependence on another.
Such diversification could also support domestic micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strengthen the government’s Make in India initiative, he added.
The latest Microsoft outage should serve as a wake-up call for India to reduce its dependence on external technology service providers, Sai Rahul Poruri, CEO of FOSS United, told The Hindu.
Disruptions to email services, a cornerstone of professional communication, could result in significant financial losses for businesses, he said.

Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.

Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir: ‘More the bhakts comment, better it would do,’ says Rahul Gandhi on BJP’s criticisms

fullParagraphs: Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram, Rahul Gandhi said, “It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can’t resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it”

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday took a swipe at the BJP leaders over their criticism of former AICC chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir, saying the more the "Bhakts" comment on the book, the better it would do.
He also claimed that a lot of the BJP leaders secretly like his mother and think she is fantastic "but unfortunately can't say it".

Responding to a question during an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram as to why the BJP is talking so much about Sonia Gandhi's just-released book "Belonging: A Journey Of Love", Gandhi said, "It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can't resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it."

"A lot of them actually secretly like her and they think she is fantastic, but unfortunately they can't say it. The other thing is - all you Bhakts, please please keep commenting on the book because the more you comment, the better it does. Ok guys," the Leader Of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.
"Push it hard, be aggressive, be nasty, because that is what is helping her, Ok. Thanks guys," he said.
The book was released on Tuesday to a lot of enthusiasm from readers as they lined up at prominent bookstores in central Delhi to pick up copies of the memoir.

The BJP on Tuesday accused Congress leader Sonia Gandhi of trying to "justify" the imposition of the Emergency in 1975 and giving a "clean chit" to her husband Rajiv Gandhi on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in her memoir, and said her book "Belonging" should instead have been named "whitewashing".
Congress leaders have hailed the book for being candid and lauded Sonia Gandhi for her achievements.

articles.title: UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take 'steps' towards inspections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The International Atomic Energy Agency has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the U.S. launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites

The UN's nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take "incremental steps" to allow inspectors to return to key nuclear facilities in the Islamic republic, adding such access was "critical" in a report seen by AFP on Friday (Novemeber 13, 2026).

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on February 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
In its report, the agency said that it was "critical" for it to conduct "verification activities in Iran without further delay".
"The director general encourages Iran to consider technical and gradual measures by which conditions are achieved that allow for the return of agency inspectors to Iran," the report said.
The IAEA "acknowledged that the military attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities and sites created an unprecedented situation".

But because of a lack of cooperation "the agency is not able to conclude that there has been no diversion of declared nuclear material from peaceful nuclear activities in Iran", the report said, raising "serious proliferation concern" that "needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency".

The IAEA board in September referred Iran to the UN Security Council, marking the first time Iran has been referred to the UN top body in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.

Before the June 2025 strikes, the IAEA calculated that Iran possessed approximately 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, nearing the 90% needed to make a bomb and well above the 3.67% limit set by a now-defunct 2015 agreement with Iran.
Since June 2025, the fate Iran's nuclear stockpile has remained uncertain.
Iran has long denied striving to develop a nuclear bomb.
IAEA head Rafael Grossi said in June that the "widespread impression" was that the stockpile remains where it was before June 2025 near to the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: IAEA head Rafael Grossi said in June that the "widespread impression" was that the stockpile remains where it was before June 2025 near to the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP).

articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa

Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.

The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.
Outage reports have since declined, with about 37,000 users reporting experiencing issues with Outlook as of 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT).
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

articles.title: Major gambling gang busted in Kozhikode
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, the gang had deliberately chosen a secluded, peaceful residential locality to organise high-stakes card games without drawing public attention

In a joint midnight operation, the District Anti-Narcotic Special Action Force (DANSAF) and the Chevayur police busted a major gambling racket allegedly operating out of a rented house in a quiet residential neighbourhood near Malaparamba here, arresting 12 persons and seizing ₹4,96,050 in cash.

Acting on a tip-off, a special police team led by Narcotic Cell Assistant Commissioner Jeevan George conducted a surprise raid around 11.30 p.m. on Thursday (November 12) at the house located on Gurudev Road near Malaparamba Junction. According to the police, the gang had deliberately chosen the secluded residential locality to organise high-stakes card games without drawing public attention.

The arrested are Muhammed Rafi, 52, of Kakkodi, Sivamani, 40, of Karuvissery, Anil Kumar, 49, of Ulliyeri, Abdul Latheef, 50, of Parambil Bazar, Balakrishnan, 56, of Chemancheri, Saleem, 58, of Karaparamba, Abdul Najeeb, 62, of Vengeri, Muhammed Riyas, 41, of Vazhakkad in Malappuram, Poulose, 51, of Kuthiravattom, Anil Kumar, 41, of Elathur, Shamnas, 40, of Chelannur, and Satheesh Kumar of Palazhi.
Playing cards and other gambling gadgets were also seized. The Chevayur police have registered a case against the accused under Sections 7 and 8 of the Kerala Gaming Act.

Senior police officers said that strict surveillance and stringent action against such illegal activities would continue in the coming days. The investigation team comprised Chevayur sub inspectors Rafeeq and Abdul Muneer and DANSAF sub inspector E. Manoj.

articles.title: Shashi Tharoor alleges 115 Bharat Summit speakers barred entry to India, their visas cancelled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The senior Congress leader said the summit would also focus on establishing a think tank ‘Our World Institute’, and creating a platform for dialogue and cooperation between the Global South and the Global North

Senior Congress leader and MP Shashi Tharoor has alleged that 115 of the 315 speakers invited to the second edition of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry into India or had their visas cancelled, “apparently on the instructions of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs”.

Mr. Tharoor, who is in Hyderabad for the Bharat Summit, in a post on social media platforms, questioned the legal basis for the action and said it was unclear under which provision of law the government had taken such a step. He pointed out that the summit would conclude on Saturday (November 14, 2026), making it impossible to reverse the decision in time for the affected participants to attend.
“What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!” he wrote.

His allegations came in the wake of a Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng claiming that she had been advised by the Indian Embassy not to travel to India despite holding a valid visa to participate in the summit. She works for the Oslo-based newspaper Dagsavisen.

Earlier, Congress MP and Telangana Congress media in-charge Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy had also alleged that nearly 30% of the invitees could not travel to India because of visa-related issues. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to participate in the valedictory session on Saturday.

The controversy has raised questions over the participation of international delegates at the two-day summit, which seeks to bring together nearly 1,000 participants from India and around 70 countries. The event is being held against the backdrop of the 80th year of India’s Independence and the 137th birth anniversary of the country’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
Mr. Tharoor said the summit would also focus on establishing a think tank, ‘Our World Institute’, and creating a platform for dialogue and cooperation between the Global South and the Global North.

When Ministry of External Affairs was asked about Mr. Tharoor’s tweet on visas rejection, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “Visa matters are sovereign functions of any country or any government.”

The allegations come amid political controversy over the event, with the BJP calling it an “anti-India summit” and accusing Mr. Gandhi of giving a platform to forces opposed to the country’s interests. BJP leaders in Telangana have announced plans to protest against his visit to Hyderabad.

Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy, addressing a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday, termed the Bharat Summit an “anti-India summit”. The BJP alleged the event was meant to bring together forces critical of India and questioned the Congress leadership’s motives for organising it.

Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao questioned the rationale behind holding such an event in the State when the government was facing financial constraints. He accused Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of spending public money to sponsor what he described as anti-India forces, in order to please Mr. Rahul Gandhi.

The BJP’s criticism has added a political dimension to the controversy surrounding the summit, particularly following allegations that several international speakers and invitees were unable to travel to India because of visa-related issues.

articles.title: Modi in Karnataka: COSMOS Mysuru Planetarium a new chapter in India’s scientific journey, says PM | HIGHLIGHTS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Earlier, he flagged off the Pink Line Metro and the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express

​ D.K. Shivakumar seeks fairer Centre-state cost sharing for Bengaluru Metro, faster clearances Shivakumar calls for fair Centre–state Metro funding, faster clearances, drought relief, and policy reforms to boost Bengaluru’s growth. ​
Shivakumar calls for fair Centre–state Metro funding, faster clearances, drought relief, and policy reforms to boost Bengaluru’s growth.
PM Narendra Modi highlights 100-km milestone of Namma Metro expansion at Pink Line inauguration.
The event also marked the birth centenary of former RSS general secretary H.V. Sheshadri.
Union Minister Vaishnaw also said that a DPR is being prepared for a new double line between Hassan and Mangaluru, for which the final location survey had been conducted.

India has seen many great astronomers, such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technology we have today did not exist back then. Despite this, they made major discoveries and carried out difficult calculations, said PM Modi after inaugurating the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru.

The facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels and 4.2 crore individual LEDs. It includes a Sky Theatre, exhibition halls, an astronomy museum and training facilities, with the aim of promoting astronomy education and public outreach.
As India achieves one scientific breakthrough after another, Mysuru is also adding a new chapter to India’s scientific journey with this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, he added.
Our government opened up the space sector. This has created new opportunities for the private sector. India’s startups have also been given an opportunity to showcase their potential.

Underscoring Karnataka’s contribution to India’s space programme, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the country’s space journey was incomplete without the State’s contributions, from Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, to Chandrayaan, Aditya-L1 and the ambitious Gaganyaan mission.
Recalling the contributions of the Mysore Maharajas to scientific development, the CM cited their vision that had resulted in the establishment of top institutions including the IISc.

Karnataka government is ready to support the Centre in establishment of new centres of excellence. We are ready to support and encourage young minds and develop skills to our engineering graduates, Mr. Shivakumar said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “The death toll is rising very fast. As per the latest information, doctors have confirmed that 23 people have died in the accident. The identities of the dead are being ascertained now,” said an Executive Magistrate of Golaghat district
At least 23 people died and 20 others were injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), officials said.
Out of the deceased, two were women, and many were college students who were returning from their classes, a police officer said.
The accident occurred at Rangajan near Hathikuli Tea Estate in Kohora range on National Highway 715 when the passenger vehicle collided with the truck, a senior officer said.

“The death toll is rising very fast. As per the latest information, doctors have confirmed that 23 people have died in the accident. The identities of the dead are being ascertained now,” an Executive Magistrate of Golaghat district told reporters here.
“Already nine ambulances have been operating to ferry the injured people. Doctors here have referred 20 people to Jorhat for advanced treatment,” the official said.
Assam Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Atul Bora, who is also the local MLA, reached the site immediately and was supervising the relief and rescue operations.
The injured people were taken to the Kohora Model Hospital, and most of the critically injured were referred to the Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

"The bus was running at very high speed, violating restrictions imposed near the park. We think that the accident took place when the driver of the minibus lost control, and the vehicle collided with the container truck," he added.
In a social media post, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he is deeply distressed by the tragic accident in Kaziranga earlier during the day.

“The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one. No words can ease their pain, but I want them to know that they are not alone. All of Assam stands with them in this hour of grief,” he added.
Mr. Sarma said the foremost priority now is ensuring the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay.
“Hon’ble Minister Shri @ATULBORA2 is at the site and personally overseeing the relief arrangements. I pray for the swift recovery of the injured and for strength for the bereaved families,” he added.

articles.title: Trees misidentified, misjudged, wrongly marked and felled to facilitate civil projects in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Over 1800 trees are being felled for an access road to the Cherlapally Railway Station, most of them not the species identified in permission copy; field inspection reveals serious irregularities

Grave irregularities mark the tree felling/translocation permissions accorded by the Hyderabad District Tree Protection Committee, as discovered in two sample cases of field inspection, respectively at Falaknuma and Cherlapally railway stations, casting a deep shadow on the whole process.

Healthy trees with woody stems and high survival rate marked for felling, dead trees or trees with no canopy permitted for translocation, wrong marking of trees on the ground, and multiple trees marked with the same number: these are only a few examples of how careless and compromised the Forest department is in granting permissions for tree felling/translocation in the age of aggravating climate crisis.

In the first instance, a rain tree which had anchored itself on the Falaknuma railway over bridge years ago, and grown with full canopy, was marked for translocation by the Tree Protection Committee to make way for the Metro Rail expansion project. Uprooting the tree means demolition of the flyover, yet this detail escaped the notice of the members who reportedly conducted field inspections before according permissions.
A rain tree anchored on Falaknuma railway bridge is recommended for translocation to facilitate Metro Rail expansion. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

On the same stretch, the letter ‘T’ is painted in red on a row of median palm trees, indicating translocation. Several of them are bare trunks devoid of crown, and practically dead, which makes them unlikely candidates for translocation. The rationale for translocation was not explained, and attempts to reach the forest officials have failed.

In the second, more flagrant instance, the proposed access road to Charlapally Railway Station by Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) is replete with glaring errors in identification of species and their demarcation, besides absolute callousness in execution. For this project, a total 2,519 trees are going, of which a whopping 1,883 are permitted to be felled, and 636 are to be translocated.

Several copper pod trees with thickly wooded trunks were hacked and piled in an open forested plot, where trees with negligible girth, and even dead trees were tied with a red ribbon isolating them for translocation. Their number and species do not match with the permission accorded by the TPC even in a single instance. Several such anomalies could be observed with regard to the avenue trees too.
A thick and healthy copper pod tree is axed down, but several trees much smaller in the background are tied with ribbons for translocation at Cherlapally | Photo Credit: Swathi Vadlamudi

For instance, the avenue tree with the number 158 is marked for translocation on the permission copy, with the species was mentioned as ‘China Are’. On the ground, it is a dead tree with no canopy at all.

The trees with the numbers 160 and 161 painted on them are ‘Moduga’ (Flame of the Forest) and ‘Vepa’ (Neem) respectively on the ground, while it is reverse on the paper. There were two trees painted with the number 39-- one Peepal and another Mango-- while on paper, the number is associated with a mango tree marked for felling. The reason mentioned was termite infestation, but the tree is found in a healthy condition.

Most glaring instance is the tree with the number 141, which is mentioned as ‘Subabul’ in the permission copy, with a recommendation for felling on the grounds of termite infestation. Upon field inspection, the tree with the same number turned out to be a large peepal with close to two metre girth and vast canopy.
A large peepal tree, perfect in health, is misidentified as Subabul and recommended for felling at Cherlapally | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

articles.title: Over 43,000 students in the Nilgiris receive cakes, greeting cards ahead of Children’s Day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu Forest Minister R.V. Ranjithkumar on Friday (November 13) distributed cakes and greeting cards to students at Udhagamandalam in the Nilgiris district, ahead of Children’s Day.

Speaking at the government higher secondary school in Udhagamandalam, the Minister said that 43,668 students studying in 516 government and government-aided primary schools, middle schools, high schools, and higher secondary schools in the Nilgiris will receive cakes and greeting cards to mark Children’s Day.

Tenders were invited through the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation for the procurement of cakes. Based on the tender process, cakes meeting FSSAI standards were procured exclusively through four companies, he said, adding that samples of the cakes were subjected to inspection by officials from the Food Safety Department and the Drug Administration Department.
The Minister also visited the Government Higher Secondary School for Children with Hearing Impairments, located near the Government Botanical Garden.
Earlier, Mr. Ranjithkumar distributed pongal to children at the Vannarapettai anganwadi centre. They were among 6,150 children at 490 anganwadis in the Nilgiris who were given pongal on Friday.

The Minister also took part in a programme in the Nilgiris where he distributed bank credit linked assistance worth ₹41.54 crore to 368 women self-help groups for undertaking entrepreneurial activities. Also present at the events was the Nilgiris Collector, Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru

articles.title: Europe warned against falling for Russia's 'traps' on Ukraine talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The hawkish former Prime Minister of Estonia Kaja Kallas said it was not up to Russia to decide who would represent Europe

European Union (EU) foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) that Europe must not walk into Russian “traps” over Ukraine talks, saying reaching a ceasefire needed to be the priority, not broader security negotiations.

U.S. envoys said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) after talks with Vladimir Putin that Europe would join future negotiations — but the Kremlin appeared to slam the brakes on that plan saying no decision had been made.
After pushing for months to be involved, Europe is now asking itself who should represent it and what it is willing to discuss with the Kremlin.
Moscow has pushed to renegotiate Europe’s broader security architecture as part of any talks — and appears to be reviving hardline demands to roll back NATO.

“First we need a ceasefire. If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us, which is that we divert the attention away from that there is no ceasefire,” Ms. Kallas told reporters at an EU summit in Dublin.
U.S. envoy and Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner said that getting Europe onboard will “allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements”.
The new push has set alarm bells ringing among U.S. allies in Europe who have long rejected the Kremlin’s desire to overhaul the continent’s security framework.
European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen insisted it was “self-explanatory that Europe is included in the peace talks to safeguard our interests, but also to support Ukraine”.
At the same time, there are calls for Europe to decide soon on who will represent it — with EU leaders set to debate the issue in Dublin.
“This needs to be resolved,” said Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin.
“In my view, finally decided upon within the next week or two.”
This week officials from Britain, France, and Germany, along with the EU, were present on the sidelines of talks in Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: HC directs State Police Chief to ensure that Patriarch of Antioch does not violate court orders or visa conditions on Keralam visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Orthodox Syrian Church members petition HC that the Patriarch may violate previous Supreme Court orders and indulge in religious activities during his visit to Keralam

The Kerala High Court has directed the State Police Chief to ensure that Moran Mor Ignatius Aphrem III, the Patriarch of Antioch, does not violate previous court orders relating to the Orthodox-Jacobite Church dispute or his visa conditions.

Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan was considering a petition by parishioners of the Orthodox Syrian Church alleging that the Patriarch may violate previous Supreme Court orders and indulge in religious activities, including performing Holy Qurbana in St.Mary’s Church, Manarcaud, or in any of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Churches during his visit to Keralam. The petitioner also sought to ensure that the Patriarch did not violate his visa conditions and the governing provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act.

Previously, the court had issued notice to the Patriarch, the Jacobaya Suriyani Christiani Sabha, and Thomas Mar Themothios, the Metropolitan of the Kottayam Diocese in the petition. However, the court was informed that the Special Messenger was not able to serve the notice and was allegedly threatened by an unknown person that a case would be filed against the Messenger before the court. In this regard, the court directed the jurisdictional Station House Officer to register a case against the authority concerned and do the needful. It directed the Registrar to forward the Messenger’s complaint as well.

The petitioner had referred to a 2019 order by the apex court, which held that the Patriarch could not interfere in the administration of parish churches by appointing vicars, priests, deacons or prelates in violation of the 1934 constitution of the Church.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 13 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

HC directs State Police Chief to ensure that Patriarch of Antioch does not violate court orders or visa conditions on Keralam visit

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Orthodox Syrian Church members petition HC that the Patriarch may violate previous Supreme Court orders and indulge in religious activities during his visit to Keralam

The Kerala High Court has directed the State Police Chief to ensure that Moran Mor Ignatius Aphrem III, the Patriarch of Antioch, does not violate previous court orders relating to the Orthodox-Jacobite Church dispute or his visa conditions.

Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan was considering a petition by parishioners of the Orthodox Syrian Church alleging that the Patriarch may violate previous Supreme Court orders and indulge in religious activities, including performing Holy Qurbana in St.Mary’s Church, Manarcaud, or in any of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Churches during his visit to Keralam. The petitioner also sought to ensure that the Patriarch did not violate his visa conditions and the governing provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act.

Previously, the court had issued notice to the Patriarch, the Jacobaya Suriyani Christiani Sabha, and Thomas Mar Themothios, the Metropolitan of the Kottayam Diocese in the petition. However, the court was informed that the Special Messenger was not able to serve the notice and was allegedly threatened by an unknown person that a case would be filed against the Messenger before the court. In this regard, the court directed the jurisdictional Station House Officer to register a case against the authority concerned and do the needful. It directed the Registrar to forward the Messenger’s complaint as well.

The petitioner had referred to a 2019 order by the apex court, which held that the Patriarch could not interfere in the administration of parish churches by appointing vicars, priests, deacons or prelates in violation of the 1934 constitution of the Church.

articles.title: Mysuru hosts Modi for second time in four months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Mysuru twice within a span of four months.

During his previous visit in August, he inaugurated Viveka Smaraka – Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre, developed by Ramakrishna Ashrama, Mysuru, to preserve and celebrate Swami Vivekananda’s association with the city during his historic journey across the country.

On Friday, Mr. Modi returned to Mysuru to inaugurate India’s first LED Dome Planetarium, developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in collaboration with the University of Mysore, at the foothills of Chamundi Hill.

Security had been tightened in the city ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit. Entry to the inaugural programme was restricted to people holding valid passes. Seating arrangements were made for nearly 10,000 people, with a large number of students attending the event.
Mr. Modi received a rousing welcome as he arrived at the venue for the public programme after inaugurating the planetarium. Several dignitaries were present on the occasion.

In his address, Mr. Modi recalled his previous visit to Mysuru to inaugurate Viveka Smaraka. Drawing a comparison between the two institutions, he said they reflected India’s traditions of spirituality and science. While Viveka Smaraka encouraged people to look within, the planetarium inspired them to look at the skies and learn about the universe.
Earlier, Mr. Modi was received at the Lalith Mahal helipad by Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and other dignitaries.

articles.title: Satavahana University students launch signature campaign to protect greenery in campus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students of Satavahana University, led by the Joint Action Committee (JAC-SU), organised a signature campaign at the main entrance of the university building in Karimnagar on Friday, seeking protection of the campus greenery and biodiversity, according to a press release.
The campaign was organised to oppose the alleged felling of dozens of trees and excavation of soil on the sprawling campus in the name of development works.
The JAC said the activities were posing a threat to the campus’s biodiversity and natural habitat.

Apart from students, several morning walkers and nature lovers, also signed a large banner put up at the university entrance, expressing their support for the conservation of trees and natural habitats, the release said.

articles.title: 31st IFFK International Competition and Indian film selections announced, new Critics Discovery section introduced
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The main objective of the new Critics Discovery section is to introduce notable and artistically distinctive films in Malayalam to prominent figures and critics in the international film industry and to provide them with more international audience attention and representation at film festivals

The Kerala State Chalachitra Academy on Friday announced the list of films for the International Competition section of the 31st International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK), to be held in December this year.

The chosen films include Chinese film Embers directed by Aoqian Sun, Brazilian film Gugu’s World directed by Allan Deberton, Mexican film I am Mario directed by Sharon Kleinberg, Filipino film Silenced Nights directed by Lawrence Fajardo, Iranian film Slumber directed by Mani Moghaddam, Uzbek-Kazakh co-production Ouroboros directed by Tatiana Lyutaeva, Iranian film People’s Child directed by Mahmoud Karimi, Uruguayan film Sweet Violence directed by Jeremias Segovia, Bangladeshi film Bonolata Sen directed by Masud Jassan Ujjal and Mexican film The Silent Virgin directed by Xavi Sala.

The Indian films in the competition are Padayaatra directed by Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Chevittorma directed by Leo Thaddeus, Selvi directed by Sailesh Rethnakumar and Members of the Problematic Family directed by Ramalingam Gowtham.

The academy also announced the list of films in the Malayalam Cinema Today section. The films are A Duck Tale directed by Arun Verghese, Ottanjaavalmaram directed by Shruthi Sharanyam, Domestic Circus directed by Ajmal Hamsa, Metro Paramo directed by Shinos Rahman and Sajas Rahman, Eko directed by Dinjith Ayyathan, Leftover directed by Salim Ahamad, Moscow directed by Nainan Anto, Not a Cinema directed by Manu Viswambharam, Ekadesham directed by Don Palathara, Rivo Rukaiah directed by Jaachii I, Kallalan directed by Ajai Prasad and Trace of Wind directed by Sharon Manuel Joy.

The official selections in the Indian Cinema Now section are Hunter’s Moon directed by Ridham Janve, Master Bantoo directed by Arsh Jain, Urmi directed by Deba Prasad Behera, An Evening Ballad directed by Bishal Swargiary, The Ink Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb directed by Yashasvi Juval, Rehmat directed by Gurvinder Singh and Whispers of the Shadow directed by Romi Meitei.

The academy also announced a new Critics Discovery section to strengthen international representation of Malayalam cinema. The main objective of the project is to introduce notable and artistically distinctive films in Malayalam to prominent figures and critics in the international film industry and to provide them with more international audience attention and representation at film festivals.

The films in the Critics Discovery section are Vasara directed by Lekshmi Pushpa, Sudeeptham directed by Deepesh T., Ezhu Niramulla Swapnam directed by Priyanandanan T.R., Tharkam directed by Sajin Baabu and Nebula directed by Mithun Narayan.

articles.title: Kerala HC summons KSEB engineer over delay in relieving traffic congestion at Pachalam in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi Corporation had sanctioned ₹1.60 lakh for the proposed works, but the KSEB’s application to the railway authorities had defects that required correction

The Kerala High Court has summoned the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) assistant executive engineer, Ernakulam Central sub division, to explain the delay in filing an application to the railway authorities regarding the relocation of electric poles near the Pachalam overbridge.

A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V.M. Syam Kumar was considering a public interest litigation seeking measures to ease traffic congestion at Pachalam Junction. The plea had alleged that the KSEB electrical installations at the junction of Chathiyath Road and Mathai Manjooran Road were causing the congestion, and that removing them would ease the situation.

The Kochi Corporation had earlier informed the court that ₹1.60 lakh was sanctioned and handed over to the KSEB for the proposed works. The KSEB had filed an application requesting to shift the electric posts onto the railway property, but it had certain defects that needed correction. The court had then directed the KSEB to file the application again to the railway authorities to facilitate smooth traffic movement. The matter will be considered again on November 18.

articles.title: Pakistan calls for 'immediate' end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at UN
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: UN Security Council renewed targeted sanctions under its Yemen sanctions regime for another year

Pakistan has called for the “immediate and unconditional” cessation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as the UN Security Council renewed targeted sanctions under its Yemen sanctions regime for another year.
The Security Council unanimously adopted the resolution on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

According to a report in Dawn , Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, while explaining his country's vote in favour of the resolution, said that Islamabad “condemns in the strongest terms” the continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.

The Iran-backed Houthis have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, claiming strikes on oil infrastructure and military facilities, while Saudi air defences have intercepted several missiles and drones, including those targeting Riyadh.

“We stand in full and unwavering solidarity with the leadership, government, and brotherly people of Saudi Arabia. Our support for the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability is resolute,” Mr. Shah said.

“Consistent with the United Nations Charter and international law, we support its legitimate right to defend its territory and protect its citizens and residents. We demand an immediate and unconditional cessation of these reprehensible Houthi attacks,” he said.
Mr. Shah described accountability for individuals and entities threatening Yemen’s peace, security, and stability as essential to creating conditions for lasting peace.

The resolution condemns Houthi military escalation inside Yemen, cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, and threats to commercial shipping, and seeks to address the group's access to dual-use components and precursor chemicals used in weapons production, the report said.

Pakistan backed stronger international action against the Houthis but stressed that the conflict required a political settlement respecting Yemen's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

Mr. Shah called for an inclusive political process under UN leadership, saying an “inclusive political process that is Yemeni-owned and Yemeni-led” was necessary to advance peace and stability, as he reaffirmed Pakistan's readiness to support international efforts to restore peace and stability and address Yemen's humanitarian suffering.

The Iran-backed Houthis seized Yemen's capital Sanaa in September 2014 amid a prolonged political crisis and expanded their control over parts of the country, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

Negotiations on the resolution involved disagreements over language describing the Houthis as a terrorist group, with Britain initially seeking to restore the designation used in some previous sanctions resolutions but dropping the effort after Russia objected that it could hamper political negotiations.

articles.title: Iran says it struck U.S. military radar in Bahrain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The IRGC says the strait is closed, while the U.S. Navy claims that it has opened a southern route for commercial vessels to exit and enter the critical waterway, while maintaining its “ironclad blockade” of Iranian ports

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Friday (November 13, 2026) said it had “destroyed” a U.S. military early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for a U.S. strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, southern Iran.

“An hour ago, in response to the enemy’s air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, the IRGC’s aerospace fighters targeted and destroyed the early-warning radar of the American aggressors on the island of Bahrain,” the IRGC said in its statement.
It added that the attack was “a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end air mischief and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz”.
The U.S. military in recent days had carried out limited air strikes on Qeshm island and other parts of southern Iran near the strait, which it said were “defensive in nature”.

October saw a record spike in maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz with nearly three dozen tankers being hit. The IRGC says the strait is closed, while the U.S. Navy claims that it has opened a southern route for commercial vessels to exit and enter the critical waterway, while maintaining its “ironclad blockade” of Iranian ports. In the first week of November, at least six vessels came under attack in the strait, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). The U.S. says its strikes in southern Iran were aimed at neutralising the threats the IRGC posed to maritime traffic.
“In case of repeated violations and aggressions, the IRGC’s air force is on full alert for borderless confrontation,” the Guards said in the statement.

The latest confrontation comes hours after U.S. President Donald Trump pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off talks with Iran, saying the U.S. did not want a deal with Iran. “Those days have long since passed. We have got their money, hundreds of billions of dollars, and we have got their strait,” he wrote in a social media post, after diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar failed to reach any breakthrough.

Iran wants the U.S. to meet its conditions, including removal of the blockade, unfreezing of its assets and war reparation, to reopen the strait and bring the nuclear issue back to the table. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said earlier this week that Iran’s demands were “outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”.

Before the November 3 U.S. midterm elections, Mr. Trump had said that he would decide whether he should “destroy” Iran based on the outcome of the diplomatic outcomes. But after the midterm, in which his Republican party suffered a massive defeat, Mr. Trump signalled that he was stepping back from renewed conflict.

Immediately after the results, Vice President J.D. Vance had blamed the war on Iran as the main reason for the Republican rout. On November 10, Mr. Trump said he would maintain the status quo on Iran — no immediate military escalation — but added that the naval blockade would stay in place. Tehran, on the other side, vowed to break the status quo.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Iran’s chief of the general staff Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi said any miscalculation by the U.S. and Israel will be met with “devastating strikes”. “We warn the United States and the Zionist regime once again that the previous slaps were only the beginning of the story, and in the event of any new miscalculation, far more lethal blows await them,” he stated.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Microsoft begins restoring Outlook, Teams and other services after global outage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.
The company said its teams are reviewing the incident and working to prevent similar disruptions in the future.

Microsoft says service availability is improving, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels. However, some users may continue to face intermittent access issues and delayed email delivery as the company restores affected infrastructure and monitors recovery.
Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America and across much of Europe.

Microsoft said service availability and email delivery were improving across a growing portion of the affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure, though some users may still face intermittent issues. It is prioritising reducing the email queue and backlog, and the extended 48-hour email timeout window stays in place to protect delayed messages.

An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.
Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. It said the focus was now on extending recovery across affected infrastructure in other regions.

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.

articles.title: Megaspeed: Gaming company to chips linchpin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: How Megaspeed, a little-known firm started by Alice Huang, became a linchpin in the chips trade

At the centre of the scandal surrounding Nvidia, which led to the resignation of founder-CEO Jensen Huang on November 12, is a little-known Singapore-based business founded by Chinese tech executive Alice Huang that came to play a vital role in the global chips trade.

Set up in 2023, with no background in AI or semiconductors, Megaspeed grew within the span of a few months into a linchpin of the semiconductors and data centre business in Asia, connecting Chinese tech companies with valuable Nvidia chips amid tightening U.S. export controls. Over the course of a couple of years, the new company would purchase between $4-5 billion of Nvidia technology according to reports, marking a rapid ascent.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Megaspeed: Gaming company to chips linchpin. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Experts call for coordinated action across sectors to tackle antimicrobial resistance
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Ahead of World AMR Awareness Week, global health experts stress the need for stronger surveillance, prevention, sustainable financing and a One Health approach to address antimicrobial resistance

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was associated with more than 4.7 million deaths in 2021, highlighting the need for coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, experts said at the sixth Global Media Forum on AMR.

Speaking ahead of World AMR Awareness Week (November 18-24), Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, Director ai-AMR Department, World Health Organization (WHO), and Director, Quadripartite Joint Secretariat on AMR, said gaps in financing, surveillance, and coordination continued to hamper global efforts. “Behind these numbers are patients, families, farmers, and communities,” he said, stressing that global commitments should translate into results on the ground.

The updated Global Action Plan on AMR for 2026-2036 seeks to strengthen prevention, surveillance, responsible antimicrobial use and sustainable financing. World leaders have committed to reducing bacterial AMR-associated deaths by 10% by 2030.

Junxia Song, deputy chief veterinarian and chief of the One Health and Disease Control Branch, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), said antibiotic use in livestock could increase by nearly 30% by 2040 without intervention. Better animal health and farm management practices could reduce use by up to 57%.

Aitziber Echeverria, AMR coordinator, Chemicals and Health Branch, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), called for action against environmental pollution, including antimicrobial residues in wastewater.

Kefas Samson, senior technical officer and lead of multisectoral coordination, AMR Department, WHO headquarters, highlighted gaps in diagnostics, surveillance and access to quality-assured antimicrobials. Jane Lwoyero, programme officer, World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), stressed the importance of vaccination and farm biosecurity.
Shobha Shukla, chairperson, Global AMR Media Alliance (GAMA), and host of the forum, called for a person-centred, rights-based and gender-transformative approach to tackling AMR.
The forum also recognised 56 journalists and media professionals as Global AMR Media Awardees 2026 for their contributions to reporting on antimicrobial resistance.
