articles.title: Keralam ration dealers seek GPS tracking of lorries to prevent foodgrain diversion from NFSA godowns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demand comes against backdrop of Keralam govt’s decision to install CCTV cameras in ration shops and integrate e-PoS machines with weighing scales to ensure accuracy in distribution of ration commodities. Dealers point out that monitoring should extend to every stage of supply chain

Ration dealers in Keralam have demanded the installation of GPS tracking devices in lorries transporting foodgrains from National Food Security Act (NFSA) godowns to ration shops to prevent the diversion of essential commodities into the black market and ensure transparency in the public distribution system.

The demand comes against the backdrop of the State Government’s decision to install CCTV cameras in ration shops and integrate electronic Point of Sale (e-PoS) machines with weighing scales to ensure accuracy in the distribution of ration commodities. While welcoming the move, dealers have pointed out that monitoring should extend to every stage of the supply chain, particularly the transportation and storage of foodgrains.

They have called for GPS-enabled tracking of all lorries carrying ration commodities from godowns to retail outlets. The system would enable authorities to monitor vehicle movements, verify delivery routes and identify possible diversion of foodgrains before they reach the designated ration shops. It would also help establish accountability in the transportation of essential commodities.

The dealers have further demanded the installation of CCTV cameras at NFSA godowns to monitor the loading and dispatch of foodgrains. They said the weighing systems at godowns should also be linked with those at ration shops to ensure that the quantity dispatched matches the quantity received.

According to T. Mohammed Ali, State General Secretary of the All-Kerala Retail Ration Dealers Association, the e-PoS machines at ration shops should be connected to the weighing systems at NFSA godowns as well. This would help eliminate discrepancies in weight and ensure that beneficiaries receive their full entitlement.

The association has urged the government to hold discussions with dealer representatives and address the shortcomings in the existing distribution system. It maintains that installing CCTV cameras only at ration shops would not be sufficient to prevent irregularities unless the movement of commodities from godowns is also effectively monitored.

The dealers have also raised concerns over the financial viability of ration shops, citing rising operating expenses and declining income. Nearly eight ration shops have reportedly closed in the Kozhikode city limits over the past three years, while more than 500 shops are said to have shut down across the State.

The dealers have disputed the authorities’ claim that a ration shop generates around ₹30,000 in monthly income, arguing that the amount does not adequately cover expenses such as rent and electricity charges. They said it was high time the government prevented leakages, strengthen accountability and restore public confidence in the State’s ration distribution network.

articles.title: Sunita Williams serves as Grand Marshal at 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The parade brought together veterans, military families, service members, marching bands, community organisations, and supporters to “recognise the courage, service, and sacrifice of America's military heroes”
Indian-origin NASA astronaut Sunita ‘Suni’ Williams has served as the Grand Marshal for the 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade.

Ms. Williams, a U.S. Navy veteran, was joined by thousands of American veterans, active-duty military personnel, marching bands, patriotic organisations, military vehicles, and participants at the annual parade honouring those who served the country through the years.
Addressing the gathering, which included Indian-descent New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Ms. Williams said she is “humbly honoured” to be at the 107th New York Veterans Day Parade.

“When I joined the military, I never thought for a moment that I would actually be a veteran...thinking you're so young and how you're going to conduct your life. But my first steps in the military showed me the foundation with which I led my life: courage, honour, commitment,” she said.
Ms. Williams also highlighted the opportunity she had to work and live in space with people from all over the world.

“I can't thank the military enough for the time I have spent, the lessons I have learned, and looking forward to giving those lessons to the next generation and seeing how they can do even more than we've ever dreamed of,” she said, adding that “exploration is in our heart and in our soul.”

“Freedom is not free, and we have shown that time and time again by being role models for the world in our journey for exploration and for brotherhood and sisterhood throughout this planet,” she said.

Separately, in a statement, Ms. Williams said, “It is an incredible honour to serve as Grand Marshal of the NYC Veterans Day Parade and to march alongside my fellow veterans. My time in the Navy shaped who I am and prepared me for every challenge that followed. I'm proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honouring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation.”
Grand Marshal Sunita "Suni" L. Williams takes part in a Veterans Day parade on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, New York City. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Mark Otto, President and Executive Director of the United War Veterans Council and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, said: “We are incredibly proud to welcome Suni as Grand Marshal of this year's NYC Veterans Day Parade on the 250th birthday of the United States of America."

"Her dedication and service embody the values we honour each Veterans Day. Year after year, this tradition brings us together to recognise the courage, commitment and sacrifice of the men and women who have served our country and to ensure their stories are never forgotten. We are honoured to have Suni lead this year's parade and help kick off the nation's largest commemoration of service.”

The New York City Veterans Day Parade 2026 was held Wednesday (November 11, 2026) through the streets of Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. The parade, held annually on Veterans Day, is organised by United War Veterans Council (UWVC).

fullParagraphs: Despite the U.S. President’s decision to hold off on further strikes, he remains neck-deep in the war he launched alongside Israel’s Netanyahu on February 28 this year

In September this year, U.S. President Donald Trump told the UN General Assembly that he could “annihilate” Iran if the conflict was not resolved soon. In the following weeks, Mr. Trump said several times he would soon take a decision on whether he should “destroy” Iran. Media reports claimed that Mr. Trump could opt for a short but intense war against Iran, targeting the country’s critical infrastructure once the November 3 U.S. midterm elections were over .

Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost his governing majority in the October 27 elections, was pushing Mr. Trump to resume air strikes. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper were reportedly in favour of renewed strikes.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Is Trump’s ‘no-war, no-peace’ plan on Iran sustainable?. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of the U.S.-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan "under a standard business visitor status" and there were "no special flags" about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers.

Mr. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan's Parliament in response to lawmakers' questions about Alice Huang's entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements.
"At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information," Mr. Chiu said.
"If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management."
Mr. Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said.

"If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review," Mr. Chiu said.
"For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country."
The government has said Taiwan's security agencies are investigating the incident.

Cabinet spokeswoman Michelle Lee said Thursday (November 12, 2026) "there is currently no public information" about whether Alice Huang "is suspected of any criminal offence or on the related investigative procedures".

articles.title: G7 Foreign Ministers say China's actions east of Taiwan threaten stability
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The G7 statement said the Ministers ⁠stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait

China's increasingly assertive actions in the waters east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and ​freedom of navigation, G7 Foreign Ministers said in a joint ‌declaration published late on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) following a meeting ​in Paris.

China, which views Taiwan as ⁠its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Officials ‌in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, say they believe China is practising for a ‌potential maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and ‌civilian ⁠assets.
The G7 statement said the Ministers ⁠stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.
China's increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan "threaten regional ​stability, freedom of ‌navigation and the safety of international shipping", the statement said.
"We reaffirmed our opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force ‌or coercion, or the threat thereof."
China's Foreign Ministry ​did not immediately respond to a request for comment. China recognises no claims of ⁠sovereignty by Taiwan.
Following the Chinese Coast Guard's latest patrol off the east coast last month, Taiwan said China ‌was harassing shipping and trying to exert a fictional jurisdiction.
Taipei regards the area off its east coast as critical to wartime supply routes from allies in the event of a blockade or conflict.
The United States, Britain, France and Germany have all previously expressed ‌their concern about China's actions off Taiwan's east coast.
China's military ​also operates around Taiwan on a daily basis.

China is carrying out "area denial" drills in the ⁠Western Pacific involving one of its aircraft carriers and ⁠other naval formations, Taiwan Defence Minister Wellington Koo said on Tuesday (November 10), following a reported rise in ‌Chinese activities.
China has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, though ​it says it would prefer "peaceful reunification".

articles.title: Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy

The tide of history cannot be ‌stopped, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Thursday (November 12, 2026), as he urged complete "reunification" of Taiwan with ​the motherland and pledged to do so peacefully, making no mention of the use ⁠of force.

China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy not supported by any major Taiwanese political party.
Resolving the Taiwan question is an "unwavering ‌historical mission" of China's Communist Party, Mr. Xi said in a speech in Beijing's Great Hall of the People.
"The tide of history cannot be stopped," Mr. Xi added. "The complete reunification of the ‌motherland must be realised, and it will certainly be realised."

Mr. Xi said China adheres to "peaceful reunification and the policy of 'one country, two systems'" and is willing to talk to Taiwan while upholding the "one-China principle", or Beijing's position that both sides ​of the Taiwan Strait are one country.
All ‌Chinese, including those in Taiwan, should join hands to jointly oppose Taiwan independence "separatist" forces and strive for peaceful development of cross-Strait ties, Mr. Xi added.
Taiwan's government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Despite Mr. Xi not mentioning the use of force, which China has never renounced for Taiwan, its military ‌operates around the island daily, and is extending its reach further into the ​Pacific.

Mr. Xi's speech comes a week ahead of the APEC summit in China's southern tech hub of Shenzhen, where he is due to ⁠meet U.S. President Donald Trump again, and also a little more than two weeks before important local elections in Taiwan.
Last month, Taiwan called on its people to steer clear of any of China's events to mark the ‌Sun anniversary, saying China had a distorted view of him and his legacy.

Beijing calls Mr. Sun a great national hero and patriot, as well as the forerunner of the 1949 communist revolution that forced the defeated Republic of China government to flee to Taiwan, where it remains to this day.
Mr. Xi said Mr. Sun was a great national hero, a great patriot and a "great pioneer of China's democratic revolution".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Xi said Mr. Sun was a great national hero, a great patriot and a "great pioneer of China's democratic revolution".

articles.title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of U.S. curbs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, per sources

Chinese ‌artificial intelligence companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centres outside China, ​concerned that a scandal involving the U.S. chipmaker’s chief executive Jensen Huang could spur Washington to ⁠tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors, three people familiar with the matter said.

The moves underline concern among Chinese technology companies over the potential closing of a gap in U.S. export controls. Seeking to protect U.S. dominance of the ‌critical sector, Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence chips, but Chinese companies can access such processors remotely by renting computing power at data centres overseas.

A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said. The people declined to be identified, or ⁠to identify the cloud provider because of the sensitivity of the matter.
Smaller AI labs are considering similar steps, including approaching major providers of rented computing power in Southeast Asia, two of the people said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces possible ouster amid fresh affair allegations

The companies fear the controversy surrounding Huang could add political momentum to ​the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, a ‌U.S. bill that would give the Commerce Department authority to regulate remote, cloud-based access to restricted technology, the people said. The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.

Advanced Nvidia processors are used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots ‌and other generative AI products. Restricting overseas cloud access would make it harder for Chinese developers to ​obtain high-end computing power without importing the chips directly.

Huang said on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times reported that the woman involved ⁠was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed, and that U.S. authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Reuters could not independently verify that allegation, which China has denied.

Alice Huang had business dealings and ‌investment ties with several leading Chinese technology companies, including Tencent and Alibaba, according to two people familiar with the matter. Tencent and Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Singapore business filings show that Alibaba subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions provided financing to Speedmatrix, a Malaysian company linked to Megaspeed, according to records reviewed by Reuters.

Megaspeed has faced scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Chinese customers gain access to advanced Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export controls. The company has denied illegally diverting chips to China.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, are facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.
Few public details are available about Ms. Huang, also known as Huang Le. She reportedly held a senior position at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International.
Despite sharing the same surname, Ms. Alice Huang is not related to the 63-year-old Nvidia chief executive.

articles.title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation

Revelations that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen ​Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker’s board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for ‌the company and concerns about the board’s ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, “There have definitely been affair scandals and ​sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No,” said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a ⁠term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation “regarding the national security concerns raised ‌in news reports,” according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company’s code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal “with ‌or without cause” by the vote of a majority of directors.
The company’s advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI ‌superiority. ⁠China’s Foreign Ministry called the spying claim “a groundless accusation, slander and a smear.”
Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as ⁠close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.
Shares in Nvidia were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang’s affair.

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three ​independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark ‌Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.
The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple’s Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.
But the U.S. probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.

“If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street ‌as well as in Silicon Valley would say they’re entitled to some leeway or deference,” said Marc Goldstein, head of U.S. research for ​proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.

articles.title: Indoor air pollution poses critical, year-round health threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Outdoor emissions regularly infiltrate living spaces, combining with domestic activities to create complex, toxic indoor environments

As Delhi, and various other parts in the northern parts of India , brace for severe winter smog, spokespeople for consumer durable makers LG and Dyson said that the air inside homes, too, presents a critical, year-round health threat. Outdoor emissions regularly infiltrate living spaces, combining with domestic activities to create complex, toxic indoor environments.

Citing the 2026 Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) analysis, an LG spokesperson said that Delhi’s winter PM2.5 pollution stems from secondary particulates (27%), transport (23%), biomass burning (20%), dust (15%), and industry (9%).

Closing doors and windows does not make homes airtight as outdoor pollutants enter through micro-gaps. They then mix with emissions from cooking, incense, candles, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from paints and furniture, and human respiratory particles.

Alex Hudson, a Dyson engineer, said that indoor air pollution is rarely driven by a single origin as even walking on carpets and sitting on sofas can stir up settled dust particles into breathing zones.
The impact extends beyond respiratory irritation as the LG spokesperson highlighted the alarming cognitive toll on children’s brain development.

A 2021 study in World Development linked higher short-term air pollution exposure among Indian children aged 5–16 to significantly lower reading and mathematics scores. A 2022 working paper by the Institute of Economic Growth and IIT Delhi confirmed similar cognitive declines in children aged 8–11.

Furthermore, a 2024 analysis in Environmental Health involving 4,860 children across three continents found that every 1 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 0.27-point drop in full-scale IQ. For older adults, cumulative exposure accelerates cardiovascular disease, stroke, and COPD risks.
Dyson’s spokesperson told that young children breathe more air relative to their body size, making them particularly vulnerable given that people spend up to 90% of their time indoors.

To combat indoor pollution, Dyson recommends source control such as using low-VOC products, installing microfibre doormats, and deep cleaning carpets with HEPA-filter vacuums. LG suggested monitoring outdoor AQI via the CPCB’s SAMEER app or IQAir to schedule ventilation, alongside kitchen exhaust fans.

When choosing air purifiers, LG advises evaluating real-time sensing, comprehensive filtration (HEPA for particles and activated carbon for gases), and clean air delivery rate (CADR) for room-wide airflow. Addressing energy concerns, LG noted modern air purifiers consume roughly 1.73 units per day under continuous 24-hour operation, costing approximately ₹14 daily.

Both spokespersons urged consumers to reject common misconceptions. LG quoted 2025 CAQM data showing Delhi had only 79 days of “Good” or “Satisfactory” AQI (≤100), with an annual PM2.5 average of 96 µg/m³, well above India’s 40 µg/m³ national standard and WHO’s 5 µg/m³ guideline.

Mr. Hudson added that fine particulate matter and gases like nitrogen dioxide are often invisible, proving that indoor air quality requires active management throughout the entire year, not just during peak winter months.

articles.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: U.S. media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with Nvidia's vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell

Nvidia's board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, U.S. media reported Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as the chip giant's chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.

The tech company's board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday (November 11, 2026) to determine Huang's future, according to the Wall Street Journal , which quoted people familiar with the matter.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that Mr. Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia's vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell.

Ms. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia's efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they "were seen being affectionate at the hotel" by bystanders, the Times reported.

The report of the second affair follows Mr. Huang's acknowledgement of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025.
U.S. intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security.

The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Ms. Huang -- to whom he bears no familial relation -- in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday (November 8, 2026) , writing: "I was unfaithful to my wife."

The same day, Nvidia's board of directors said in a statement that they'd launched "an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

"I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company," Mr. Huang wrote in his statement. The Times reported that Congress has also called on him to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang.

As the surge in the artificial intelligence industry has driven Nvidia's stock to new heights, Mr. Huang has appeared alongside U.S. President Donald Trump at White House events, most recently last month, when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader.

Mr. Huang was among the world's most influential tech leaders -- including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg -- who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Mr. Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity.
Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Mr. Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors.

articles.title: ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani POCSO case: First charge sheet filed, Madras High Court told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan told that the charge sheet was filed before a special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on November 11, 2026, and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in the next few days

A special investigation team (SIT) probing the serial child sexual abuse cases against Gem Granties founder R. Veeramani has already filed the first charge sheet in one of the multiple cases registered against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and other laws, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan told the Madras High Court on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP said, the first charge sheet in the case was filed before the special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in some of the cases. He told the court that the charge sheets in other crime numbers would also be filed one after another in the next 10 to 15 days.
Gem Granites Veeramani’s daughter Archana moves Madras High Court alleging human rights violations by SIT
Police seize third video allegedly showing ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani abusing minor

After hearing him, the judge adjourned a couple of connected writ petitions pending before him to November 30, 2026. He also perused a status report filed on behalf of the SIT, explaining to the court the progress made in the investigation so far, and told the counsel present in the court that he was satisfied with the substantial work done in the sensitive case related to sexual exploitation of children.

The judge directed the High Court Registry to keep the status report in safe custody and produce it before the court during the next hearing. The SIT had been filing periodical status reports ever since R. Varaaki and advocate M.L. Ravi filed writ petitions (criminal) in the High Court, seeking the transfer of investigation in the POCSO cases against Veeramani from the State police to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
Fresh sexual harassment complaint against ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani
Special Public Prosecutors appointed to conduct trial in POCSO Act cases against Veeramani

After not finding any reason to order such transfer for the present, the judge had said that the SIT must be allowed to work in peace and called for periodical status reports on the ongoing investigation. When Mr. Varaaki’s counsel presented some evidence before the court on Thursday, the judge directed the petitioner to submit all those materials with the SIT instead of waiting for the court proceedings.

He also recorded the submission of the SPP that the SIT was also probing whether any of the police officials or others had ever tried to protect the prime accused Veeramani. When the judge wanted to know why the SIT should not conduct media briefings, the SPP said, the team was avoiding media interactions in order to ensure that sensitive information related to child sexual abuse does not get disclosed.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Today | Senior IAS officer sentenced to imprisonment for contempt of court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Welcome to the Tamil Nadu Today newsletter, your guide from The Hindu on the major news stories to follow today.

The Madras High Court has found senior IAS officer and former Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) Member Secretary Anshul Mishra guilty of contempt of court and directed him to undergo simple imprisonment for a month.
Justice P. Velmurugan also directed Mr. Mishra to pay a compensation of ₹25,000 to elderly siblings who had been struggling for years to retrieve their valuable immovable property.
Later on June 12, 2025, a Division Bench of the Madras High Court suspended the sentence imposed by a single judge.

Months after, in September 2025, a Division Bench of the Madras High Court set aside the order passed by a single judge who found Mr. Mishra guilty of contempt of court proceedings and directed him to undergo simple imprisonment for a month.
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin left for New Delhi to take part in the 10 th Governing Council meeting of the NITI Aayog to be held tomorrow. The meeting will be chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Stalin was seen off at the Chennai airport by Tamil Nadu Ministers and DMK functionaries. DMK Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs received the Mr. when he arrived in New Delhi.
Later in the day, the CM met Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi at their residence.

S.P. Velumani, AIADMK MLA from Thondamuthur constituency in Coimbatore and former Minister, received an anonymous letter threatening to kill his family members and warning of a bomb blast in Coimbatore before July 30.

The letter, which was undersigned with the note “Allahu Akbar Pakistan Zindabad”, stated that three of his family members would be killed if a sum of ₹1 crore is not placed at a specific location in Coimbatore on May 25.

articles.title: Chennai draft electoral roll records 29.14 lakh voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Perambur has the highest number of electors at 2,28,139, followed by Velachery with 2,19,352 and Kolathur with 2,13,539. Harbour has the lowest electorate at 1,20,852

The draft electoral roll for Chennai district, published on November 12 following the Special Summary Revision (SSR), has recorded 29,14,908 electors across 16 Assembly constituencies and 4,071 polling stations. The revised list has 21,403 more electors than the previous roll, which had 28,93,505 voters and 4,079 polling stations as on April 6, according to the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
The draft roll includes 14,04,968 male electors, 15,09,040 female electors, and 900 third-gender electors. The revision has also resulted in a reduction of eight polling stations across the district.

articles.title: Madras High Court suspends IAS officer Anshul Mishra’s one-month sentence in contempt plea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Division Bench of Justices M.S. Ramesh and V. Lakshminarayanan direct the officer to deposit ₹25,000 with the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court

A Division Bench of the Madras High Court on Thursday (June 12, 2025) suspended the sentence of one-month simple imprisonment imposed by a single judge on Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Anshul Mishra after finding him guilty of contempt of court.

The Bench comprising Justices M.S. Ramesh and V. Lakshminarayanan suspended the sentence and directed the IAS officer to deposit ₹25,000 with the Registrar (Judicial) of the High Court within three weeks and without prejudice to his clean service records.

articles.title: Madras High Court sentences senior IAS officer to one-month simple imprisonment in contempt case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P. Velmurugan also directs Anshul Mishra, former member secretary of CMDA, to pay a compensation of ₹25,000 from his salary to two aged petitioners

Justice P. Velmurugan directed the Madras High Court Registry to take steps for securing the custody of the former Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) Member Secretary and make him undergo the sentence if he does not prefer the appeal within the limitation period of 30 days.

articles.title: Iran’s Guards say ‘accident’ left two tankers on fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that two tankers carrying over four million barrels of oil had caught fire after an "accident" on an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz.
Since the outbreak of the war in West Asia in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic shipping channel, insisting vessels use routes it has approved.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.

"Last night, two tankers - acting in violation of regulations and despite repeated warnings from the Revolutionary Guards Navy regarding the unauthorised and dangerous nature of the southern maritime route - were involved in an accident while traversing this prohibited path in the strait," the Guards said in a statement.
They did not specify the nature of the "accident" but said it left the two tankers immobilised after they were hit with a "violent explosion".

"These two supertankers were carrying a combined total of over four million barrels of oil, which are now ablaze - a consequence of the blind trust placed in the aggressive American military," the statement said.
Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
Tehran has often said they struck mines, but the U.S. military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

articles.title: OpenAI now allows enterprises to process AI requests within India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The facility initially supports GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI’s API, allowing requests to be processed and AI responses generated within the country to address enterprise data localisation requirements

OpenAI on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced local processing and inference for its API in India , allowing eligible businesses and developers to have supported AI requests processed and model computations performed within the country.

The move expands the company’s existing data residency offering in India, which was introduced in May 2025 and allowed eligible customers to store their data in the country. The latest development extends this capability to cover where the AI model processes information and generates responses, addressing a key concern among businesses handling sensitive information.

Initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model, the new offering is aimed at organisations that have not fully deployed artificial intelligence in business operations because of requirements around where their information is processed. This is particularly relevant to customers in financial services with specific data localisation requirements, OpenAI said.

“Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country,” said Nitin Bawankule, Head of Enterprise - India, OpenAI.

“Local inference gives them more control over where supported workloads run and helps address a practical barrier to adoption. It gives more businesses a way to put OpenAI’s tools to work, and gives Indian developers and startups more scope to build for their own, and enterprise needs.”

Under the new arrangement, both the processing of an API request and the model computation that generates its response will take place in India for supported workloads. Supported customer content will also be stored in the country, the company said.

The launch covers direct API usage and currently supports GPT-6 Luna input and output through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. Customers can access the capability by creating a new API project, selecting India for both storage and processing, and using the corresponding India regional endpoint.

The development comes as OpenAI expands its presence in India. Earlier this year, the company introduced OpenAI for India, an initiative spanning AI infrastructure, enterprise adoption, skills development and local partnerships. The initiative included a partnership with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data-centre capacity, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI models were also made available for in-country inference through Amazon Web Services’ Bedrock platform. AWS announced the availability of OpenAI models on Bedrock in August 2026, including regional inference capabilities for supported models.
OpenAI said its now launched API inference residency offering is available in other parts of the world, with India, Australia and Japan among the latest markets to receive the capability.

articles.title: Six researchers win Infosys Science Foundation prizes for 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A total of 222 applications were received across six categories with the highest for ‘Engineering and Computer Science’ category, ISF said

The Infosys Science Foundation (ISF) on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced the winners of the ‘Infosys Prize 2026’ in six categories — Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences.
Among the recipients is Riddhipratim Basu, Associate Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (ICTS-TIFR) in Bengaluru.

The prize for each category comprises a gold medal, a citation, and a prize purse of $100,000 (or its equivalent in Indian rupees). The laureates of Infosys Prize 2026 were selected by an international panel of jurors comprising renowned scholars and experts.

This year 222 applications were received compared to 150 last year, ISF Trustee Kris Gopalakrishnan said. He added that the highest number of applications were received in the Engineering and Computer Science category and the youngest winner this year is 31 years of age.

ISF said that from 2024, the prize has shifted focus to honour researchers under the age of 40, emphasising the need for early recognition of exceptional talent. “This encouragement of early career researchers will serve as an inspiration for the next generation of scholars and future innovators,” it said.

“Recognising exceptional researchers early in their careers is particularly important, as it gives them the encouragement and opportunity to pursue bold questions, challenge established thinking and make lasting contributions to their fields,” ISF President Srinath Batni said.
Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs at Princeton University, has won the award for his contributions to the field of climate change, and technological innovation, and to the study of business cycle fluctuations. “His work provides deep insights into how societies adapt to climate change through technological innovations and is likely to have far-reaching policy implications,” the jury said.
Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, has been awarded in this category for his pioneering work that extends low-power wireless networks beyond information delivery to perception and action in the physical world. He combines insights on the physics of wireless technology with novel architectures and algorithms to obtain innovative designs in connectivity, sensing, control, and actuation.
Gautam Bhatia, Adjunct Professor at Jindal Global Law School and Green Fellow at the University of New South Wales | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Gautam Bhatia, Adjunct Professor at Jindal Global Law School and Green Fellow at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, has won the award in this category. The jury has described Prof. Bhatia as “an outstanding young legal scholar”, with a gift for marshalling arguments rigorously towards conclusions that seek to make the law an instrument for constructing a fair, equal, and humane society. He is the author of five books and many academic articles. He has worked in neighboring disciplines that have an impact on the law, such as macro-economics, sociology, political theory, and moral philosophy.

articles.title: Cakes sent to government, government-aided schools across Tamil Nadu for Children’s Day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cakes have been procured at total cost of ₹9.27 crore, through the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation. The type and quantity will vary across regions.
Cakes, meant for distribution on Friday (November 13, 2026), to mark Children’s Day that falls on Saturday (November 14), have reached schools in most districts in Tamil Nadu.
School principals have been instructed to count the cakes to ensure that there is no shortage, and store them in air-conditioned classrooms such as hi-tech labs.

They will be distributed to 61,84,566 students, teachers, and non-teaching staff at government and government-aided schools in the State on Friday. They have been stored in air-conditioned classrooms such as hi-tech labs until distribution.

According to a circular, 61,84,566 students, teachers, and non-teaching staff of government and government-aided schools will be receiving the cakes, procured at total cost of ₹9.27 crore, through the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation.

The type and quantity will vary across regions. While two packets each of 25-g mini Swiss roll packets will be distributed across schools in districts such as Mayiladuthurai, Salem, Thanjavur, Madurai, Tiruvannamalai, and Tiruchi, schools in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, The Nilgiris, Erode, Namakkal, and Karur districts will receive two packets of 21.6-g cake each. Students in other districts will receive a 45-g cake.
Sources in the department said Chief Education Officers have been directed to maintain a 1% buffer stock to meet additional requirements.

articles.title: India, Canada trade pact talks may conclude by December: Canadian Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: India and Canada are currently holding the sixth round negotiations for the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)

Canadian Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu on Thursday (November 12, 2026) said negotiations are underway between India and Canada for a trade pact and expressed the hope that these talks will conclude by the time Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits Canada next month.
India and Canada are currently holding the sixth round negotiations for the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

"We're negotiating right now with India. I'm here for Round Six between our chief negotiators, and we're going to hopefully get there by the time Prime Minister Modi Ji visits Canada next month," he said at a session of CII Partnership Summit.
Mr. Sidhu is in Visakhapatnam to attend the summit and also held discussions on the pact with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.
Between India and Canada, he said it's not about competition, it's about complementarities between the two economies.
The talks are moving at a faster pace as both the countries are targeting to conclude the negotiations by the end of this year.
The Canadian Minister said India is growing at a rapid rate and requires a lot more energy, 75% more energy by 2035.

"... we're building up our capacity in the energy sector. We've got a handful of LNG projects across the country. And once those projects come online, we'll be the fifth-largest exporter of LNG in the world within the next five years. That will help India with its growth plan," he said.
He added that Canada has the ability to help meet objectives of India's SHANTI Act.

The SHANTI Act which got the assent of President of India on December 21, 2025, allows private sector participation to set up a nuclear facility, or to carry out activities for the production, use, and disposal of nuclear energy under a licence from the central government and safety authorisation of the Regulatory Board.

"We were here earlier this year around March 1st, and we signed a uranium deal roughly worth $2.5 billion to provide India that uranium that you need for your nuclear sector. But, we want to do more," he said.
India and Canada, he said, also had great conversations on critical minerals.

articles.title: Viksit Bharat needs fair administrative system, says Karnataka HC while rapping State government for denying job for SC candidate for officials’ mistake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Manjunath cleared the KPSC’s competitive exam for Excise Guard post in 2010 but was denied appointment due to a date of birth discrepancy.

Observing that “fair, transparent and responsible administrative system is the need of the hour and wish of Viksit Bharat,” the High Court of Karnataka has criticised the State government for denying a Scheduled Caste (SC) candidate his rightful appointment to the post of Excise Guard merely relying on a typographical error of his date of birth in his SSLC certificate.

The Division Bench comprising Justice S.G. Pandit and Justice Chillakur Sumalatha dismissed the State’s writ petition challenging a 2018 Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (KSAT) order that had directed the appointment of Manjunath K. to the post.

Mr. Manjunath cleared the KPSC’s competitive exam for Excise Guard post in 2010 but was denied appointment due to a date of birth discrepancy. His SSLC marks card showed his date of birth as June 15, 1980, while his transfer certificate and cumulative records contained the correct date of birth as 1982. The KPSC gave him one week to correct the error in SSLC certificate.
He approached SSLC authorities and also filed a civil suit, but before resolution, the KPSC published provisional and final selection lists, excluding him and selecting lower-scoring candidates.

The SSLC authorities later admitted the error, corrected its records, and issued a revised certificate. Mr. Manjunath then withdrew the suit. However, the KPSC refused to consider the corrected certificate, citing completion of the recruitment process.
Hence, he approached KSAT in 2011, which in August 2018 directed the State government to appoint him prospectively as Excise Guard or create a supernumerary post for him, if there is no vacancy.

The government challenged this before the High Court in 2021, citing various administrative difficulties, and contended that under a 2000 government circular, an SSLC date of birth cannot be altered without a civil court decree.

However, it was pointed out to the court that having lost his father at a young age, Mr. Manjunath was raised by his coolie-worker mother and educated in a government school and mistake of his date of birth in SSLC certificate came to his knowledge only when it was verified by the KPSC.

The Bench noted that the government’s claim was not correctness of his date of birth but manner in which it was corrected. The Bench also noted that the government itself had issued two notifications in 2009 and 2015 recalling 2000 circular on noticing difficulty faced by students and parents.

Also, the Bench found it strange that the KPSC and the government did not accept the correction of date of birth carried out by SSLC authorities, who were none other than the government’s functionaries.
“State has not only became an author of injustice, but took shelter under the very same circumstances to deny the lawful entitlement of an innocent, his plate of meal,” the court observed..

“An aspirant of public employment who met all required criteria and fulfilled all prescribed requirements should not be deprived of an opportunity merely because of a mistake of one official and improper exercise of authority by another official,” the Bench said, while giving eight weeks for the government to appoint him to the post as per the tribunal’s order.

However, it was pointed out to the court that having lost his father at a young age, Mr. Manjunath was raised by his coolie-worker mother and educated in a government school and mistake of his date of birth in SSLC certificate came to his knowledge only when it was verified by the KPSC.

The Bench noted that the government’s claim was not correctness of his date of birth but manner in which it was corrected. The Bench also noted that the government itself had issued two notifications in 2009 and 2015 recalling 2000 circular on noticing difficulty faced by students and parents.

Also, the Bench found it strange that the KPSC and the government did not accept the correction of date of birth carried out by SSLC authorities, who were none other than the government’s functionaries.

“State has not only became an author of injustice, but took shelter under the very same circumstances to deny the lawful entitlement of an innocent, his plate of meal,” the court observed..

“An aspirant of public employment who met all required criteria and fulfilled all prescribed requirements should not be deprived of an opportunity merely because of a mistake of one official and improper exercise of authority by another official,” the Bench said, while giving eight weeks for the government to appoint him to the post as per the tribunal’s order.

articles.title: Sanction granted by PMO to prosecute two IAS officers in Tamil Nadu, Madras High Court told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Anand Venkatesh directs DVAC to proceed with the process of filing charge sheet against former AIADMK Minister S.P. Velmunai and IAS officers K.S. Kandasamy and K. Vijaya Karthikeyan in the ₹98.25-crore corporation tender irregularities case

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) has accorded sanction to prosecute two IAS officers, K.S. Kandasamy and K. Vijaya Karthikeyan, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, in connection with the ₹98.25-crore corporation tender irregularities case, primarily registered against former AIADMK Minister S.P. Velumani, the Madras High Court was told on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Justice N. Anand Venkatesh recorded the submission made by Additional Solicitor General A.R.L. Sundaresan, assisted by Central government senior panel counsel V. Chandrasekar, and directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to proceed with the process of filing the charge sheet against all the accused in the long-pending corruption case.

Referring to the long-drawn process involved in obtaining sanction to prosecute the two IAS officers, ever since the complainant Jayaram Venkatesan of Arappor Iyakkam filed a contempt of court petition against the DVAC officials in 2025, the judge said: “It is a classic case of how much of effort had to be put in to obtain sanction to prosecute IAS officers in criminal cases.”

He also said: “The wheels (of law enforcement) move faster against poor people, but for influential people, the wheels hardly move.” The judge, last year, issued a series of directions to the State government to send the files to the Centre and then suo motu impleaded the Department of Personnel and Tranining (DoPT) in New Delhi in order to make it expedite the process of obtaining sanction.

After the ASG submitted a copy of the sanction order before the court on Thursday, the judge ordered the deletion of the DoPT from the array of respondents since it was not a necessary party in the contempt proceedings any more. He decided to keep the contempt petition pending only for the purpose of monitoring the further progress to be made by the DVAC.

In the contempt petition filed through its counsel V. Suresh, Arappor Iyakkam told the court that its complaint was related to irregularities in the award of Greater Chennai and Coimbatore municipal corporation civil contracts issued between 2014 and 2018 when Mr. Velumani served as the Minister for Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department during the AIADMK rule.

The DVAC registered a First Information Report (FIR), on the basis of the complaint, in 2021 and completed the probe a few years later. On February 12, 2024, then Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Speaker M. Appavu granted sanction to prosecute Mr. Velumani. However, as there was a delay in obtaining sanction to prosecute the two IAS officers, Arappor Iyakkam had filed the contempt petition last year.

Following continuous nudging by the High Court, the Tamil Nadu government forwarded its proposal for grant of sanction to the DoPT along with voluminous documents, which had to be translated from Tamil to English. Thereafer, on September 16, 2026, Sushil Kumar Patel, Joint Secretary, DoPT, told Justice Venkatesh that the PMO was the competent authority to grant sanction to prosecute IAS officers.

He said, the DoPT had sent the files to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) for its remarks and that it would forward the files to the PMO after receipt of the CVC’s remarks. Then, the officer had also assured the court that the entire process of obtaining sanction would be completed within two months.

articles.title: Police get five-day custody of ex-MLA Muthukumar in private school bribery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The case was registered on a complaint from a private schools’ association that money had been collected from more than 1,000 private schools during the previous DMK regime for permanent recognition and other permissions

A special court has permitted the Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Chennai police to take former MLA Muthukumar into custody for five days for interrogation in connection with the alleged collection of several crores of rupees in bribes from private schools in return for securing permanent recognition and various government approvals.

The case was registered by the CCB following a complaint from a private schools’ association, alleging that money had been collected from more than 1,000 private schools during the previous DMK regime on the promise of permanent recognition and other permissions.

Former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association president B.T. Arasakumar, and Muthukumar, a former DMDK MLA who is now with the DMK, are among those booked in the case.

While Anbil Mahesh has been lodged in prison, Muthukumar surrendered before the special court for cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act in Chennai on October 29. Judge L.S. Sathyamurthy remanded him in judicial custody.
Subsequently, the CCB filed a petition seeking five days of police custody to interrogate Muthukumar.

Passing orders on Thursday, judge Sathyamurthy permitted the CCB to take Muthukumar into custody from 1 p.m. on November 12 until November 16. The police were directed to produce him before the court on the morning of November 16.
The judge also permitted Muthukumar’s advocate to be present during the interrogation and directed the police not to subject him to any physical or mental harassment.

articles.title: Earlier, PM said 'sab changa si', now it is 'sab mehnga si': Congress taunts government over price rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said prices of milk, rice, flour, lentils, cooking oil, onions, potatoes, tomatoes, sugar, ghee, and other essential everyday items are skyrocketing, and Amul and Mother Dairy have once again raised milk prices
The Congress on Thursday (November 12, 2026) targeted the Modi government over rising prices, and said the public wants inflation to be reined in rather than the government's claims and promises.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said prices of milk, rice, flour, lentils, cooking oil, onions, potatoes, tomatoes, sugar, ghee, and other essential everyday items are skyrocketing, and Amul and Mother Dairy have once again raised milk prices.

"There was a promise of good days; every day brought a new blow from rising prices. The policies of the ruthless Modi government have repeatedly hit the pockets of the poor and the middle class," he said on X.

"In the 'Modani government', which came to power by seeking votes against rising prices, the math of inflation is such that only the country’s middle and poor classes have to bear it all. Rising prices every day, from the kitchen to FMCG products, have thrown every household’s budget into disarray," he said.
"Prime Minister, You once said — 'sab changa si' (everything is fine), now it is — 'sab mehnga si' (everything is expensive!)," the Congress leader said taking a swipe at the Prime Minister.

Since Diwali, major brands such as Hindustan Unilever have raised prices of detergents and home care products by up to 11%, he claimed, adding that everyday essentials such as Surf Excel, Rin, Wheel, and Moti Gulab soap are becoming increasingly unaffordable for ordinary people.

"On the one hand, the government says sugar production in the country has increased fourfold and that 3.6 million tonnes of old stocks are also available. The same is true of lentils. So the big question is — if that is the case, why is the general public getting no relief? Is the country suffering a double blow from the E20 blend in petrol in the form of rising prices and adulterated petrol?" he said.
The Congress leader said the public wants to know how long their pockets will be picked while the government hides behind false claims?
"The people of this country do not want government claims and policy promises; our demand is that inflation be effectively reined in," Mr. Ramesh said in his post.
Indian National Congress / Narendra Modi / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Venezuela tells COP31 it has sovereign right to pump more oil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Venezuela’s Acting President ​Delcy Rodriguez’s comments at the UN ‌talks on Turkiye’s Mediterranean coast jar with efforts by other conference leaders to convince global governments to accelerate a ‌shift from carbon-emitting fossil fuels

Venezuela’s Acting President ​Delcy Rodriguez told the COP31 climate conference on Thursday (November 12, 2026) ⁠that the country has the sovereign right to develop its oil industry, even as it recognises the importance of combating climate change.
But they dovetail with the United ‌States' ⁠efforts to raise billions of dollars towards increasing oil output in ⁠Venezuela, a member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

"We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national ​development," Ms. Rodriguez told the summit. "It is ‌possible to grow and protect the environment at the same time."

Venezuela's forests acted as a "lung for the planet", absorbing more carbon than the country emits, she added. She did not address the impact ‌that oil exported from the country had on global emissions.

President ​Donald Trump, who withdrew the United States from formal climate cooperation last year after calling global warming a hoax, ⁠has said investing in Venezuela's oil can bolster national security by increasing Western Hemisphere energy supplies.

Earlier on Thursday (November 12, 2026), British Prime ‌Minister Andy Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine showed the need for countries to switch from fossil fuels to clean energy.

"It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed ‌to prices we cannot control," he said. "The shift to clean energy is the only route ​to energy security."

Thursday (November 12, 2026) is the fifth day of the two-week COP31 conference where representatives from nearly 200 countries ⁠are trying to agree a deal to improve progress in tackling climate ⁠change.

A UN report last month found the world was on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees ‌Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

articles.title: Indonesia's Vice President resigns as eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents submitted by Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements
Indonesia's Vice President resigned on Thursday (November 12, 2026) as questions grew over his eligibility for the office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials.

Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, submitted his resignation to the leadership of the People's Consultative Assembly, the country's highest legislative body, at the Parliament building in the capital, Jakarta.
The academic credentials investigation was apparently not related to investigations into allegations that top police officials had been involved in wiretapping targeting the president.

Under Indonesia's Constitution, a Vice Presidential vacancy does not trigger a new election. The office remains vacant until the People's Consultative Assembly elects a replacement from two candidates nominated by the president within 60 days.

Mr. Raka had offered to resign on Tuesday during a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, saying he wanted to avoid a prolonged political controversy. But a Cabinet minister said the president urged Mr. Raka at the time to defend himself and it wasn't clear if he accepted the resignation offer.
The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Mr. Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.
A subsequent petition, submitted on Wednesday to the House leadership by 120 lawmakers from eight political parties, began a parliamentary process that could lead to his impeachment.

Under Indonesian law, House leaders must establish a special committee to examine whether Mr. Raka has violated the Constitution by serving as Vice President, despite allegedly failing to meet election requirements. If lawmakers determine there is sufficient basis for the accusation, the House must ask the Constitutional Court to rule on whether a constitutional violation has occurred.

articles.title: Phage therapy holds promise in fighting against antimicrobial resistance: Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Dr. Kalyan noted that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail

Phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to selectively eliminate harmful bacteria, holds significant potential in combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR), said Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy Koganti, sepsis and infectious diseases specialist at SHRI Hospital, Guntur.

He said this while sharing his research experience in a press release, after presenting his team's scientific findings at an international symposium jointly organised by the Chinese University of Hong Kong and reputed biomedical research journals.

Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy said his team's research presentation on phage therapy received appreciation from participants at the symposium. Dr. Sutharsan Govindarajan, Associate Professor and phage biologist, SRM University, AP, also presented research conducted by the team.

He described the event as an enriching learning experience, particularly the discussions on the wider applications of bacteriophages in diagnostics and therapy, including cancer research. Professor Chuanbin Mao, chair of the symposium, has been researching bacteriophages for 25 years and has contributed extensively to scientific literature, he said.
Dr. Kalyan noted that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail.

His team has administered phage therapy to a few patients at its centre with encouraging results. In collaboration with SRM University and Szeged University, Hungary, the team is working to advance its availability in India.

articles.title: Karnataka plans app to track used cooking oil, prevent re-entry into food chain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Food Safety Department to develop digital system within three months; pilot project in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, and Hubballi

Karnataka’s Health Department is developing a mobile application to track the collection, sale, and reuse of used cooking oil , with the objective of preventing re-entry into the food chain, Health Minister U.T. Khader said on November 12.

The application, which is expected to be developed within three months, will create a digital trail from the point at which cooking oil is purchased by hotels and other food business operators to its eventual disposal or transfer to authorised agencies for industrial use, Mr. Khader said.

The initiative is aimed at addressing the illegal diversion of used cooking oil, which is sometimes collected for industrial purposes such as soap manufacturing and biodiesel production but allegedly finds its way back to small hotels and eateries for reuse in cooking.

Addressing presspersons in Bengaluru, Mr. Khader said the Food Safety and Drugs Administration Department would manage the application. All manufacturers and food business operators would be required to register on the platform. The department would initially conduct a trial run in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, and Hubballi.

Explaining the proposed mechanism, he said hotels and other establishments would have to enter details of the quantity of fresh cooking oil purchased, its source, and the quantity of used oil generated. They would have to record the identity of the person or agency to whom the used oil was handed over.
The collectors, in turn, would have to upload details of whom they sold the oil to, the quantity transferred, and the amount paid.

“If a hotel uses 500 litres of oil in a month, it must account for the 50 to 75 litres of used oil generated, assuming a 10% to 15% recovery. It must submit details of whom it handed over the used oil to. The person who collects it must record whom he has sold it to. The entire chain has to be tracked,” he said.
The Minister said the system is necessary because the department currently lacked reliable data on the movement of used cooking oil and its eventual destination.
Under the proposed arrangement, used oil collected from food establishments would have to be channelled towards authorised industrial uses rather than being sold back to food businesses.
Mr. Khader said some agencies authorised to collect used cooking oil for industrial purposes were diverting a portion of it to small hotels.

Explaining the economics behind the diversion, he said collectors could receive around ₹80 for a litre of used oil intended for industrial purposes, while small hotels are willing to pay ₹120 to ₹125 a litre.
“Why would someone sell it for ₹80 when they can get ₹120 by supplying it to a small hotel?”

articles.title: Deceased TGSRTC driver’s son gets job
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: TGSRTC driver K. Shankar Goud succumbed to burn injuries in April during a strike
The son of a Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) worker, K. Shankar Goud, who succumbed to burn injuries in April 2026, was given a letter of appointment on Thursday.

Mr. Goud, who was from Narasampet, was a driver at the local bus depot. He had attempted to immolate himself during the TGSRTC workers’ stir, and was immediately rushed to the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Warangal. But, given his critical condition, he was later shifted to Hyderabad where he succumbed.
The Telangana government assured Mr. Goud’s family of financial assistance and a job. Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar had condoled his death.
On Thursday, Mr. Prabhakar and TGSRTC Chairman Y. Nagi Reddy handed over the letter of appointment to the deceased’s son Hemanth Goud.

Mr. Prabhakar appreciated the effort of the TGSRTC employees to raise funds for Mr. Goud’s family. He said that the Telangana goverment was committed to help TGSRTC workers and that the letter of appointment was a part of its responsibility.
He reiterated that issues of TGSRTC workers, or instances of indiscipline should be escalated to senior officers and physical attacks against staff would not be tolerated.
Touching upon the integrity of TGSRTC workers, he said that they had returned lost items worth several lakhs to their rightful owners.
“The unity shown by the RTC staff in supporting Shankar Goud’s family through financial aid is commendable,” he said.
